7
7
transcending the tendency to close
超越了关闭的倾向

The foundations of spiritual growth and personal awakening are very much strengthened by the findings of Western science. Science has shown us how an underlying energy field forms into atoms, which then bind together into molecules, and ultimately manifest into the entire physical universe. The same is true inside of us. All that goes on inside also has its foundation in an underlying energy field. It is the movements in this field that create our mental and emotional patterns as well as our inner drives, urges, and instinctual reactions. Regardless of what you call this inner force field—Chi, Shakti, or Spirit—it is an underlying energy that flows in particular patterns through your inner being.

西方科学的发现极大地巩固了灵性成长和个人觉醒的基础。科学已经向我们揭示了潜在的能量场如何形成原子，原子又如何结合成分子，最终显化为整个物质宇宙。同样的道理也适用于我们自身。我们内在的一切活动也都根植于潜在的能量场之中。正是这个能量场的运行塑造了我们的心理和情感模式，以及我们内在的驱动力、冲动和本能反应。无论你如何称呼这个内在的能量场——气、夏克提还是灵性——它都是一种以特定模式流经你内在生命的潜在能量。

When looking at these patterns within yourself, as well as in other living species, it is not difficult to see that the most primal energy flow is the survival instinct. During eons of evolution, from the simplest of living forms to the most complex, there has always been the day-to-day struggle to protect oneself. In our highly evolved cooperative social structures, this survival instinct has gone through evolutionary changes. Many of us no longer lack food, water, clothing, or shelter; nor do we regularly face life-threatening physical danger. As a result, the protective energies have adapted toward defending the individual psychologically, rather than physiologically. We now experience the daily need to defend our self-concepts rather than our bodies. Our major struggles end up being with our own inner fears, insecurities, and destructive behavior patterns, and not with outside forces.

当我们审视自身以及其他生物的这些模式时，不难发现，最原始的能量流动是生存本能。在漫长的进化过程中，从最简单的生命形式到最复杂的生物，保护自身始终是日常斗争的一部分。在我们高度进化的合作型社会结构中，这种生存本能经历了进化的转变。我们中的许多人不再缺乏食物、水、衣物或住所；我们也不再经常面临危及生命的身体危险。因此，保护性能量已经适应于从生理层面保护个体，转向心理层面。我们现在每天都需要捍卫的是自我认知，而不是身体。我们最终面临的主要挑战不再来自外部力量，而是来自我们内心的恐惧、不安全感和破坏性的行为模式。

Nonetheless, the same impulses that make a deer run away urge you to run away. Suppose somebody raises their voice at you or talks about an uncomfortable subject. These are not physically threatening circumstances, yet your heart starts pumping a little faster. That’s exactly what happens to deer whenever they hear a sudden sound. Their hearts start pumping faster, and they either freeze or run away. In your case, however, it’s not usually the kind of fear that causes you to physically run away. It’s just a deep, personal fear demanding protection.

然而，驱使鹿逃跑的本能，同样也会驱使你逃跑。假设有人对你提高音量，或者谈论一些让你不舒服的话题。这些情况并不构成人身威胁，但你的心跳却会不由自主地加快。鹿听到突如其来的声响时，也会有同样的反应。它们的心跳加速，要么僵住不动，要么逃之夭夭。但对你而言，通常驱使你逃跑的并非那种会真正让你动弹不得的恐惧，而是一种深藏于心、需要保护的恐惧。

Since it’s not socially acceptable to run into the woods and hide like a deer, you hide inside. You withdraw, close down, and pull back behind your protective shield. What you are actually doing is closing down your energy centers. Even if you don’t know you have energy centers, you’ve been closing them since kindergarten. You know exactly how to close your heart and put up a psychological protective shield. You know exactly how to close down the centers to avoid being too receptive and sensitive to the different energies coming in and causing fear.

既然像鹿一样躲进树林里是不合时宜的，你就选择躲在室内。你退缩、封闭自己，躲在你的保护罩后面。你实际上是在关闭你的能量中心。即使你不知道自己有能量中心，你也从幼儿园就开始关闭它们了。你非常清楚如何封闭你的心扉，筑起一道心理保护屏障。你非常清楚如何关闭这些能量中心，以避免对涌入的各种能量过于敏感，从而避免恐惧的产生。

When you close down and protect yourself, you are pulling a shell around the part of you that is weak. This is the part that feels it needs protection even though no physical attack is taking place. You are protecting your ego, your self-concept. Although a situation may present no physical danger, it may cause you to experience disturbance, fear, insecurity, and other emotional problems. So you feel the need to protect yourself.

当你封闭自己、保护自己时，你其实是在为内心脆弱的部分套上一层保护壳。即使没有遭受任何实际的攻击，这部分也会感到需要保护。你是在保护你的自尊，你的自我认知。即使某种情况没有带来任何实际的危险，它也可能让你感到不安、恐惧、不安全感以及其他情绪问题。因此，你会感到需要保护自己。

The problem is that the part of you that gets disturbed is way out of balance. It’s so sensitive that the slightest little thing causes it to overreact. You are living on a planet spinning around the middle of outer space, and you’re either worrying about your blemishes, the scratch on your new car, or the fact that you burped in public. It’s not healthy. If your physical body were that sensitive, you would say you were sick. But our society considers psychological sensitivities normal. Because most of us don’t have to worry about food, clothing, or shelter, we have the luxury of worrying about a spot on our pants, or laughing too loud, or saying something wrong. Because we’ve developed this hypersensitive psyche, we constantly use our energies to close around it and protect ourselves. But this process only hides the problems; it doesn’t fix them. You’re locking your illness inside yourself, and it will only get worse.

问题在于，你内心那个容易受到干扰的部分严重失衡。它过于敏感，哪怕最轻微的事情都会引发它的过度反应。你生活在一颗围绕外太空旋转的星球上，却还在担心脸上的瑕疵、新车上的划痕，或者在公共场合打嗝。这很不健康。如果你的身体也如此敏感，你会觉得自己生病了。但我们的社会却认为心理上的敏感是正常的。因为我们大多数人不必为食物、衣物或住所担忧，所以我们才有闲暇去担心裤子上的污渍、笑得太大声，或者说错话。由于我们发展出了这种高度敏感的心理，我们不断地消耗精力来封闭自己，保护自己。但这种做法只是掩盖了问题，并没有解决问题。你把自己的病痛锁在内心深处，只会让情况变得更糟。

You will get to a point in your growth where you understand that if you protect yourself, you will never be free. It’s that simple. Because you’re scared, you have locked yourself within your house and pulled down all the shades. Now it’s dark and you want to feel the sunlight, but you can’t. It’s impossible. If you close and protect yourself, you are locking this scared, insecure person within your heart. You will never be free that way.

在你成长的过程中，你会明白，如果你把自己保护起来，就永远无法获得自由。就这么简单。因为你害怕，所以你把自己锁在家里，拉下了所有的窗帘。现在一片漆黑，你想感受阳光，却无法做到。这是不可能的。如果你封闭自己，保护自己，就等于把那个恐惧、不安全的人锁在了心里。那样，你永远无法获得自由。

Ultimately, if you protect yourself perfectly, you will never grow. All your habits and idiosyncrasies will stay the same. Life becomes stagnant when people protect their stored issues. People say things like, “You know we don’t talk about that subject around your father.” There are all these rules about things that are not supposed to happen outside because they could cause disturbance inside. Living like this allows for very little spontaneous joy, enthusiasm, and excitement for life. Most people just go from day to day protecting themselves and making sure nothing goes too wrong. At the end of the day, when someone asks, “How was your day?” a normal response is, “Not too bad,” or “I’ll survive.” What is that telling you about their view of life? They see life as a threat. A good day means you made it through without getting hurt. The longer you live like this, the more closed you become.

最终，如果你把自己保护得完美无缺，你就永远不会成长。你所有的习惯和怪癖都会保持不变。当人们保护自己积压的问题时，生活就会停滞不前。人们会说：“你知道我们不会在你父亲面前谈论那个话题。” 有太多关于哪些事情不应该发生在外面的规矩，因为它们可能会扰乱家庭内部。这样的生活让人很难感受到自发的快乐、热情和对生活的兴奋。大多数人只是日复一日地保护自己，确保一切平安无事。一天结束时，当有人问“你今天过得怎么样？”时，通常的回答是“还不错”或“我能挺过去”。这反映了他们怎样的生活观？他们把生活视为一种威胁。美好的一天意味着你平安度过。你这样生活的时间越长，你就会变得越封闭。

If you really want to grow, you have to do the opposite. Real spiritual growth happens when there is only one of you inside. There’s not a part that’s scared and another part that’s protecting the part that’s scared. All parts are unified. Because there is no part of you that you’re not willing to see, the mind is no longer divided into the conscious and subconscious. Everything you see inside is just something you see inside. It’s not you; it’s what you see. There is simply the pure energy pouring inside of you that creates the ripples of thoughts and emotions, and there is the consciousness that’s aware of it. There is simply you watching the dance of the psyche.

如果你真的想成长，就必须反其道而行之。真正的灵性成长发生在你内心只有一个自我的时候。没有一部分恐惧，另一部分则保护着恐惧的部分。所有部分融为一体。因为你不再回避自己的任何一部分，所以意识不再分裂为意识和潜意识。你内心所见的一切，都只是你内心所见。那不是你；那是你所看到的。你内心涌动的纯粹能量，激起思想和情感的涟漪；而你的意识觉察着这一切。你只是在观察心灵的舞动。

In order to reach this state of awareness, you must let your entire psyche surface. Every little separated piece of it must be permitted to pass through. Right now, many fragmented parts of your psyche are held within you. If you want to be free, it all has to be equally exposed to your awareness and released. But it will never get exposed if you’re closing yourself. After all, the purpose of closing was to make sure that the sensitive parts of your psyche don’t get exposed. So you catch on that no matter how much pain the exposure creates, you are willing to pay that price for freedom. When you are no longer willing to identify with the part of you that is separating itself into a million pieces, you are ready for real growth.

为了达到这种觉知状态，你必须让你的整个心灵浮现出来。每一个分裂的碎片都必须被允许通过。此刻，你内心深处藏着许多破碎的心灵碎片。如果你想要获得自由，它们都必须平等地暴露在你的觉知之下，并被释放。但如果你封闭自己，它们就永远不会被暴露。毕竟，封闭的目的正是为了确保你心灵中那些敏感的部分不被暴露。所以你明白，无论暴露会带来多少痛苦，你都愿意为自由付出这样的代价。当你不再愿意认同那个正在分裂成无数碎片的自我时，你就准备好迎接真正的成长了。

Begin by seeing the tendency to protect and defend yourself. There is a very deep, innate tendency to close, especially around your soft spots. But eventually you will notice that closing creates tremendous work. Once you close, you have to make sure that what you protected doesn’t get disturbed. You then carry this task for the rest of your life. The alternative is to become conscious enough to simply watch the part of your being that is constantly trying to protect itself. You can then give yourself the ultimate gift by deciding not to do that anymore. You decide, instead, to get rid of that part.

首先，要觉察到自己保护和防御的倾向。我们内心深处有一种与生俱来的封闭倾向，尤其是在脆弱之处。但最终你会发现，封闭会带来巨大的负担。一旦你封闭了自己，就必须确保你所保护的东西不被打扰。然后，你将终生背负这项重担。另一种选择是，你要足够清醒地觉察到自己内心那个不断试图保护自己的部分。然后，你可以给自己一份终极礼物：决定不再这样做。相反，你决定摆脱那个部分。

You start by watching life and noticing the constant flow of people and situations that hit your stuff every day. How often do you find yourself trying to protect and defend that weak part of you? You feel like the world wants to get right at it. Every place you go there’s someone or something trying to disturb you, trying to get your goat. Why not let them have it? If you don’t really want it, then don’t protect it.

你首先要观察生活，留意每天不断涌现的人和事，它们冲击着你的生活。你是不是经常试图保护自己脆弱的那一部分？你感觉全世界都想攻击它。无论你走到哪里，总有人或事想要打扰你，惹你生气。为什么不让他们得逞呢？如果你并不真的想要它，那就不要保护它。

The reward for not protecting your psyche is liberation. You are free to walk through this world without a problem on your mind. You are just having fun experiencing whatever happens next. Because you got rid of that scared part of you, you don’t ever have to worry about getting hurt or disturbed. You no longer have to listen to “What will they think of me?” or, “Oh God, I wish I hadn’t said that. It sounded so stupid.” You just go about your business and put your whole being into whatever’s happening, instead of putting your whole being into your personal sensitivity.

不保护你的心灵所带来的回报是解脱。你可以自由自在地行走于世，心中毫无顾虑。你只需尽情享受接下来发生的一切。因为你摆脱了内心恐惧的束缚，你再也不用担心受到伤害或困扰。你不再需要纠结于“他们会怎么看我？”或者“天哪，我真后悔说了那些话，听起来太蠢了。”你只需专注于自己的事情，全身心地投入到当下发生的一切，而不是将全部精力都放在个人的敏感情绪上。

Once you’ve made the commitment to free yourself of that scared person inside, you will notice that there is a clear decision point at which your growth takes place. Spiritual growth is about the point at which you start to feel your energy change. For instance, somebody says something, and you start to feel the energy get a little strange inside. You will actually start to feel a tightening. That is your cue that it’s time to grow. It’s not time to defend yourself, because you don’t want the part of you that you would be defending. If you don’t want it, let it go.

一旦你下定决心释放内心那个恐惧的自己，你就会发现，你的成长会在一个清晰的转折点发生。灵性成长就在于你开始感受到自身能量的变化。例如，当有人说了什么话，你开始感到内心的能量有些异样，甚至会感到一种紧绷感。这就是你成长的信号。此时此刻，你无需为自己辩护，因为你并不想要你正在捍卫的那个自己。如果你不想要它，那就放手吧。

You will eventually get conscious enough so that the minute you see the energy start getting strange, you stop. You stop getting involved in the energy. If it normally causes you to start talking, you stop talking. You just stop, mid-sentence, because you know where it will go if you continue. The moment you see the energy getting imbalanced inside, the moment you see the heart starting to tense and get defensive, you just stop.

你最终会变得足够清醒，一旦察觉到能量开始变得异常，就立刻停止。停止与能量互动。如果它通常会让你开始说话，你就停止说话。即使话说到一半，也要立刻停下来，因为你知道如果继续下去会发生什么。一旦察觉到体内能量失衡，一旦察觉到心脏开始紧张和防御，你就立刻停止。

What exactly does it mean “to stop”? It’s something you do inside. It’s called letting go. When you let go, you are falling behind the energy that is trying to pull you into it. Your energies inside have power. They are very strong, and they draw your awareness into them. If a hammer falls on your toe, all your awareness will focus there. If there’s a sudden loud sound, again, all of your awareness will focus there. Consciousness has the tendency to focus on disturbance, and disturbed energies inside are no exception. These disturbed energies will draw your consciousness to them. But you do not have to let this happen. You really do have the ability to disengage and fall back behind them.

“停止”究竟意味着什么？这是一种内在的行为，叫做放手。当你放手时，你便不再受制于试图将你拉入其中的能量。你内在的能量拥有强大的力量，它们会吸引你的注意力。如果锤子砸到你的脚趾，你的所有注意力都会集中在那里。如果突然传来一声巨响，你的所有注意力也会集中在那里。意识倾向于关注干扰，而内在的紊乱能量也不例外。这些紊乱的能量会将你的意识吸引到它们那里。但你无需让这种情况发生。你完全有能力脱离它们的控制，不再受其影响。

When the energies inside start to move, you do not have to go there. For instance, when your thoughts start, you do not have to go with them. Let’s say you’re outside taking a walk and a car drives by. Your thoughts say, “Boy, I wish I had that car.” You could just keep on walking, but instead you start getting upset. You want a car like that, but your salary isn’t high enough. So you begin thinking about how you can get a raise or a different job. You didn’t have to do all that. It could have just been—here comes the car and there it goes, and here comes the thought and there it goes. They’re both gone together because you didn’t go with them. That is what’s called being centered.

当内在能量开始流动时，你不必非得跟着它走。例如，当你的思绪开始涌现时，你不必非得跟随它。假设你在户外散步，一辆车驶过。你的思绪会想：“唉，真希望我也有那辆车。”你可以继续往前走，但你却开始感到沮丧。你想要一辆那样的车，但你的工资不够高。于是你开始思考如何加薪或换工作。你其实不必做这些。事情本可以很简单——车来了，车走了；思绪来了，思绪也走了。它们同时消失，因为你没有跟随它们。这就是所谓的“保持专注”。

If you aren’t centered, your consciousness is just following whatever catches its attention. You see the car drive by and you’re off doing something about it. Another day you see a boat, and then it is all about the boat, and you forget about the car. There are people like that. They don’t hold jobs very well and relationships don’t tend to work out for them. They’re just all over the place; their energy is very scattered.

如果你无法保持专注，你的意识就会被任何吸引它注意力的事物所左右。你看到一辆车驶过，就立刻去做点什么。又有一天，你看到一艘船，你的全部注意力就都集中在船上，把车抛在了脑后。有些人就是这样。他们工作不稳，人际关系也往往不顺。他们心神不宁，精力分散。

You have the ability to not go with any of these thoughts. You can just sit in the seat of consciousness and let go. A thought or emotion emerges, you notice it, and it passes by because you allow it to. This technique of freeing yourself is done with the understanding that thoughts and emotions are just objects of consciousness. When you see your heart start getting anxious, you are obviously aware of this experience. But who is aware? It is the consciousness, the indwelling being, the Soul, the Self. It is the seer, the one who sees. The changes you experience in your inner energy flow are simply objects of this consciousness. If you want to be free, then every time you feel any change in the energy flow, relax behind it. Don’t fight with it, don’t try to change it, and don’t judge it. Don’t say, “Oh, I can’t believe I’m still feeling this. I promised myself I wouldn’t think about that car anymore.” Don’t do that; you’ll just end up going with the guilt thoughts instead of the car thoughts. You have to let them all go.

你有能力不去理会这些念头。你可以安住于意识之中，顺其自然。当一个念头或情绪浮现，你觉察到它，它便会过去，因为你允许它过去。这种自我解脱的技巧建立在这样的理解之上：念头和情绪都只是意识的对象。当你感到内心开始焦虑时，你当然会意识到这种体验。但究竟是谁在觉察呢？是意识，是内在的生命，是灵魂，是真我。是观察者，是洞察一切的存在。你内在能量流动的变化仅仅是意识的对象。如果你想要获得自由，那么每当你感受到能量流动的任何变化时，就放松地接纳它。不要与之对抗，不要试图改变它，也不要评判它。不要说：“哦，我真不敢相信我还在感受这种情绪。我答应过自己不再想那辆车了。”不要那样做；那样你最终只会陷入内疚的念头，而不是关于那辆车的念头。你必须放手。

But it’s not just about letting go of thoughts and emotions. It’s actually about letting go of the pull that the energy itself has on your consciousness. The disturbed energy is trying to draw your attention into it. If you use your inner willpower to not go with it, and just remain seated within, you will notice that the distinction between the consciousness and the object of consciousness is like night and day. They are totally different things. The object comes and goes, and the consciousness watches it come and go. Then the next object comes and goes while the consciousness watches it. Both objects came and went, but the consciousness didn’t go anywhere. It stays constant and simply watches all of it. The consciousness experiences the creation of thoughts and emotions, and it has the clarity to see where they came from. It sees all of this without thinking about it. It sees what’s going on inside as easily as it sees what’s going on outside. It simply watches. The Self is watching the inside energies change in accordance to both inside and outside forces. All the energies that it watches will just come and go, unless you lose your center of consciousness and go with them.

但这不仅仅是放下念头和情绪。实际上，它是放下能量本身对你意识的拉扯。紊乱的能量试图将你的注意力吸引到它身上。如果你运用内在的意志力不去顺从它，只是安住于内在，你会发现意识与意识对象之间的区别如同白昼与黑夜。它们是完全不同的事物。对象来来去去，意识观察着它的来来去去。然后下一个对象来来去去，意识依然观察着它。两个对象都来来去去，但意识却始终停留在原地。它保持着恒定的状态，只是观察着这一切。意识体验着念头和情绪的产生，并且清晰地看到它们的来源。它无需思考就能看到这一切。它能像观察外部世界一样轻松地看到内在发生的一切。它只是观察着。自我观察着内在能量如何随着内外力量的变化而变化。它所观察的所有能量都会来来去去，除非你失去意识中心并随它们而去。

Let’s take a slow-motion look at what happens if you go with these energies. First, you start to have a thought or feeling. This feeling could be as subtle as your energy flow starting to tighten and become defensive, or it could be something much stronger. If these energies capture your consciousness and all the power of awareness gets focused on them, this power actually feeds them. Consciousness is a tremendously powerful force. When you concentrate on these thoughts and emotions, they become charged with energy and power. This is why thoughts and emotions get stronger the more attention you give them. Let’s say you feel a little jealousy or a little fear. If you focus on it, it grows in importance and demands more of your attention. Then, because your attention feeds it, it becomes infused with even more energy and draws more attention. That’s how the cycle goes. Eventually, what started as a passing thought or emotion can become the center of your entire life. If you don’t let go, it can get completely out of control.

让我们慢下来仔细看看，如果你顺应这些能量会发生什么。首先，你会开始产生某种想法或感觉。这种感觉可能很微妙，比如你的能量流动开始收紧，变得具有防御性；也可能非常强烈。如果这些能量占据了你的意识，你所有的觉察力都集中在它们身上，那么这种力量实际上会滋养它们。意识是一种极其强大的力量。当你专注于这些想法和情绪时，它们就会被赋予能量和力量。这就是为什么你越关注它们，想法和情绪就越强烈。假设你感到一丝嫉妒或一丝恐惧。如果你专注于它，它的重要性就会增加，并需要你更多的关注。然后，因为你的关注滋养了它，它会被注入更多的能量，吸引更多的注意力。这就是循环的运作方式。最终，最初只是转瞬即逝的想法或情绪可能会成为你生活的中心。如果你不放手，它就会完全失控。

A wise person remains centered enough to let go every time the energy shifts into a defensive mode. The moment the energy moves and you feel your consciousness start to get drawn into it, you relax and release. Letting go means falling behind the energy instead of going into it. It just takes a moment of conscious effort to decide that you’re not going there. You just let go. It’s simply a matter of taking the risk that you are better off letting go than going with the energy. When you’re free from the hold the energy has on you, you will be free to experience the joy and expansiveness that exists within you.

智者始终保持内心的平静，每当能量进入防御模式时，都能学会放手。当能量流动，你感到意识开始被它吸引时，就放松下来，释放自己。放手意味着顺应能量，而不是被它牵着鼻子走。你只需要片刻的觉察，就能决定不去那里。你只需放手。这仅仅意味着你要承担风险，相信放手比顺应能量更好。当你摆脱了能量的束缚，你就能自由地体验内在的喜悦和广阔。

So you decide to use life to free yourself. You become willing to pay any price for the freedom of your soul. You will realize that the only price you have to pay is letting go of yourself. Only you can take inner freedom away from yourself, or give it to yourself. Nobody else can. It doesn’t matter what others do, unless you decide that it matters to you. Begin with small things. We tend to let ourselves get bothered by the little, meaningless things that happen every day. For example, somebody beeps at you at the stoplight. As these little things happen, you will feel your energy change. The moment you feel a change, relax your shoulders and relax the area around your heart. The moment the energy moves, you simply relax and release. Play with letting go and falling behind this sense of being bothered. Let’s say someone at work took your pencil, and you notice that every time you go to use another one, your inner energy shifts—even the slightest amount. Are you willing to release the old pencil in order to liberate yourself? This is how you make freedom a game. Instead of getting into being bothered, you get into being free. When you reach for a pencil, and you see yourself getting a little uptight, let go. Your mind might start saying, “It was a pencil today and if I let go, they’ll step all over me. It’ll be my desk tomorrow, or my house, or maybe even my husband.” That’s how the mind talks. It’s very melodramatic. But you decide that for the cost of a pencil, you’ll go for the ride. You tell your mind, “When it’s the car, we’ll have a talk. Right now, it only costs a pencil to be free.” Just decide that no matter what the mind says, you aren’t getting involved. You don’t fight the mind. In fact, you don’t even try to change it. You just make a game out of relaxing in the face of its melodrama. You simply learn how to release the tendency for getting drawn into the energy. The root is where the consciousness is aware of the pull of these energies.

所以你决定用生命来解放自己。你愿意为灵魂的自由付出任何代价。你会意识到，你唯一需要付出的代价就是放手。只有你能夺走内心的自由，也能赋予自己内心的自由。没有人能做到。别人做什么都无关紧要，除非你决定它对你很重要。从小事开始。我们常常会被每天发生的琐碎小事所困扰。例如，有人在红绿灯前按喇叭。随着这些小事的发生，你会感觉到你的能量发生了变化。当你感觉到变化的那一刻，放松你的肩膀，放松你心脏周围的区域。当能量流动的那一刻，你只需放松并释放。尝试放下这种烦恼，不再在意它。假设有人在工作中拿走了你的铅笔，你注意到每次你拿起另一支铅笔时，你的内心能量都会发生变化——哪怕只是微小的变化。你愿意放下那支旧铅笔来解放自己吗？这就是你如何将自由变成一场游戏。与其让自己陷入烦恼，不如让自己获得自由。当你伸手去拿铅笔，却发现自己开始有些紧张时，就放手。你的脑海里可能会响起这样的话：“今天只是一支铅笔，如果我放手，他们就会把我踩在脚下。明天会不会是我的桌子，或者我的房子，甚至可能是我的丈夫？” 这就是大脑的运作方式，它非常戏剧化。但你决定，为了这支铅笔的代价，就放手一搏吧。你告诉你的大脑：“等到是车的时候，我们再好好谈谈。现在，获得自由只需要一支铅笔的代价。” 只需决定，无论大脑说什么，你都不要卷入其中。不要与大脑对抗。事实上，你甚至不要试图改变它。你只需把面对它的戏剧化反应，放松下来，当作一种游戏。你只需学会如何摆脱被能量牵引的倾向。问题的根源在于意识是否意识到这些能量的牵引力。

You will see that the energy does have the power to draw you in. Even once you decide you’re not going to let this happen, it still has a tremendous power over you. It happens at work and it happens at home. It happens with your children and with your husband or wife. It happens with everything and everybody all the time. Your opportunities to grow are endless. It’s always there in front of you. Just commit to not letting the energy draw you in. When you feel the pull, like somebody pulling on your heart, you just let go. You fall behind it. You simply relax and release. And no matter how many times you’re pulled, that’s how many times you relax and release. Because the tendency to get drawn in is constant, the willingness to let go and fall behind has to be constant.

你会发现，这股能量确实有吸引你的力量。即使你决定不再让它发生，它仍然对你有着巨大的影响。它会在工作中发生，也会在家里发生。它会发生在你的孩子身上，也会发生在你的伴侣身上。它无时无刻不在影响着一切人和事。你成长的机会无穷无尽，它始终就在你眼前。你只需要下定决心，不让这股能量把你拉进去。当你感受到那股拉力，就像有人在拉你的心一样，你就放手。顺其自然。你只需放松，然后释放。无论你被拉扯多少次，你也需要放松和释放多少次。因为被吸引的倾向是持续不断的，所以放手和顺其自然的意愿也必须是持续不断的。

Your center of consciousness is always stronger than the energy that is pulling on it. You just have to be willing to exercise your will. But it’s not a fight or a struggle. It’s not that you are trying to stop the energies from coming up inside. There is nothing wrong with feeling the energies of fear, jealousy, or attraction. It’s not your fault that such energies exist. All the attractions, repulsions, thoughts, and feelings don’t make any difference. They don’t make you pure or impure. They are not you. You are the one who’s watching, and that one is pure consciousness. Don’t think you’d be free if you just didn’t have these kinds of feelings. It’s not true. If you can be free even though you’re having these kinds of feelings, then you’re really free—because there will always be something.

你的意识中心永远比拉扯它的能量更强大。你只需要愿意运用你的意志。但这并非一场斗争或挣扎。你并非试图阻止内在能量的涌现。感受恐惧、嫉妒或吸引的能量并没有错。这些能量的存在并非你的过错。所有的吸引、排斥、想法和感受都无关紧要。它们不会让你变得纯洁或不纯洁。它们并非你本身。你是那个观察者，而那个观察者才是纯粹的意识。不要以为只要没有这些感受你就能获得自由。事实并非如此。如果你即使拥有这些感受也能感到自由，那么你才是真正自由的——因为总会有一些东西存在。

If you can learn to remain centered with the smaller things, you will see that you can also remain centered with bigger things. Over time, you will find that you can even remain centered with the really big things. The types of events that would have destroyed you in the past can come and go, leaving you perfectly centered and peaceful. You can be fine, deep inside, even in the face of a deep sense of loss. There’s nothing wrong with being peaceful and centered as long as you are releasing the energy, not suppressing it. Ultimately, even if terrible things happen, you should be able to live without emotional scars and impressions. If you don’t hold these issues inside, you can go about your life without getting psychologically damaged. No matter what events take place in life, it is always better to let go rather than to close.

如果你能学会对小事保持内心的平静，你会发现自己也能对大事保持平静。久而久之，你会发现自己甚至能对真正的大事保持平静。那些过去会摧毁你的事件，如今都会过去，让你内心平静安宁。即使面对深深的失落感，你的内心深处依然可以安然无恙。只要你释放能量，而不是压抑它，保持平静和内心的平静就没有任何错。最终，即使遭遇可怕的事情，你也应该能够摆脱情感创伤和阴影。如果你不把这些问题藏在心里，你就能安心地生活，不会受到心理伤害。无论生活中发生什么，学会放手永远比封闭自己要好。

There’s a place deep inside of you where the consciousness touches the energy, and the energy touches the consciousness. That’s where your work is. From that place, you let go. Once you’ve let go, every minute of every day, year after year, then that’s where you’ll live. Nothing will be able to take your seat of consciousness from you. You’ll learn to stay there. After you’ve put years and years into this process, and learned to let go no matter how deep the pain, you will achieve a great state. You will break the ultimate habit: the constant draw of the lower self. You will then be free to explore the nature and source of your true being—Pure Consciousness.

在你内心深处，有一个地方，意识与能量在此交汇，能量也与意识在此交汇。这就是你修行的地方。从那里，你学会放下。一旦你放下，日复一日，年复一年，每一分每一秒，你都将安住于此。没有任何事物能够夺走你意识的居所。你将学会安住于此。当你在这个过程中投入多年，学会无论痛苦多么深切都能放下，你便会达到一种极高的境界。你将打破终极的习惯：对低级自我的持续吸引。那时，你将自由地探索你真我的本质和源泉——纯粹的意识。

8
8
let go now or fall
现在放手，否则就摔倒

The exploration of Self is inextricably interwoven with the unfolding of one’s life. The natural ups and downs of life can either generate personal growth or create personal fears. Which of these dominates is completely dependent upon how we view change. Change can be viewed as either exciting or frightening, but regardless of how we view it, we must all face the fact that change is the very nature of life. If you have a lot of fear, you won’t like change. You’ll try to create a world around you that is predictable, controllable, and definable. You’ll try to create a world that doesn’t stimulate your fears. Fear doesn’t want to feel itself; it’s actually afraid of itself. So you utilize the mind in an attempt to manipulate life for the purpose of not feeling fear.

对自我的探索与人生的展开密不可分。人生的起伏跌宕既能促进个人成长，也能滋生恐惧。究竟哪一种占据主导地位，完全取决于我们如何看待变化。变化既可以令人兴奋，也可以令人恐惧，但无论我们如何看待，都必须面对一个事实：变化是生命的本质。如果你内心充满恐惧，你就不会喜欢变化。你会试图创造一个可预测、可控、可定义的世界。你会试图创造一个不会刺激你恐惧的世界。恐惧本身并不想感受它；它实际上害怕它自己。因此，你会运用思维去操控生活，以求摆脱恐惧。

People don’t understand that fear is a thing. It’s just another object in the universe that you are capable of experiencing. You can do one of two things with fear: you can recognize that you have it and work to release it, or you can keep it and try to hide from it. Because people don’t deal with fear objectively, they don’t understand it. They end up keeping their fear and trying to prevent things from happening that would stimulate it. They go through life attempting to create safety and control by defining how they need life to be in order to be okay. This is how the world becomes frightening.

人们不明白恐惧是一种真实存在的事物。它只是宇宙中你能体验到的众多事物之一。面对恐惧，你可以选择两种方式：要么承认它的存在并努力摆脱它，要么选择压抑它并试图逃避它。因为人们无法客观地看待恐惧，所以他们无法理解它。最终，他们选择压抑恐惧，并试图阻止任何可能引发恐惧的事情发生。他们终其一生都在试图通过定义自己需要怎样的生活才能感到安心来创造安全感和掌控感。这就是世界变得令人恐惧的原因。

This may not sound frightening; it may sound safe. But it’s not. If you do this, the world truly becomes threatening. Life becomes a “me against it” situation. When you have fear, insecurity, or weakness inside of you, and you attempt to keep it from being stimulated, there will inevitably be events and changes in life that challenge your efforts. Because you resist these changes, you feel that you are struggling with life. You feel like this person is not behaving the way they should, and this event is not unfolding the way you want. You see situations that happened in the past as disturbing, and you see things down the road as potential problems. Your definitions of desirable and undesirable, as well as good and bad, all come about because you have defined how things need to be in order for you to be okay.

这听起来或许并不可怕，甚至很安全。但事实并非如此。如果你这样做，世界就会变得充满威胁。生活会变成一场“我与它对抗”的局面。当你内心充满恐惧、不安或软弱，并试图阻止它们被激发时，生活中必然会出现一些事件和变化来挑战你的努力。因为你抗拒这些变化，你会感觉自己在与生活抗争。你会觉得这个人没有按照他应该的方式行事，这件事也没有按照你想要的方式发展。你会把过去发生的事情视为令人不安的，把未来的事情视为潜在的问题。你对理想与不理想、好与坏的定义，都源于你对事物必须如何才能让你感到安心的设定。

We all know that we’re doing this, but nobody questions it. We think we’re supposed to figure out how life should be, and then make it that way. Only someone who looks deeper, and questions why we need the events of life to be a particular way, will question this assumption. How did we come up with the notion that life is not okay just the way it is, or that it won’t be okay the way it will be? Who said that the way life naturally unfolds is not all right?

我们都知道我们正在这样做，但却没有人质疑。我们认为自己应该弄清楚生活应该是什么样子，然后按照那种方式去实现。只有那些深入思考、质疑我们为什么需要生活以某种特定方式展开的人，才会质疑这种假设。我们是如何得出“生活现在的样子不够好”或者“生活将来的样子不够好”这种想法的呢？是谁说生活自然而然的发展方式不好？

The answer is, fear says so. The part of you inside that’s not okay with itself can’t face the natural unfolding of life because it’s not under your control. If life unfolds in a way that stimulates your inner problems, then, by definition, it’s not okay. It’s really very simple: that which doesn’t disturb you is okay, and that which does disturb you is not. We define the entire scope of our outer experience based upon our inner problems. If you want to grow spiritually, you have to change that. If you are defining creation based upon the most messed up part of your being, what do you expect creation to look like? It’s going to look like a frightful mess.

答案是，恐惧如是说。你内心深处那个不接纳自己的部分，无法面对生命的自然发展，因为它不在你的掌控之中。如果生命的发展方式刺激了你内心的不安，那么，从定义上讲，它就是不好的。道理其实很简单：不困扰你的就是好的，困扰你的就是不好的。我们根据内心的不安来定义我们所有的外部体验。如果你想在灵性上成长，就必须改变这一点。如果你用你内心最糟糕的部分来定义创造，你期望创造会是什么样子？它会是一团糟，令人恐惧。

As you grow spiritually, you will realize that your attempts to protect yourself from your problems actually create more problems. If you attempt to arrange people, places, and things so they don’t disturb you, it will begin to feel like life is against you. You’ll feel that life is a struggle and that every day is heavy because you have to control and fight with everything. There will be competition, jealousy, and fear. You will feel that anyone, at any moment, could cause you disturbance. All they have to do is say or do one thing, and the next thing you know there’s disturbance inside of you. That makes life a threat. That’s why you have to worry so much. That’s why you have all these dialogues going on inside your mind. You’re either trying to figure out how to keep things from happening, or you’re trying to figure out what to do because they did happen. You are fighting with creation, and that’s what makes creation itself the most frightening thing in your life.

随着你灵性上的成长，你会意识到，你试图保护自己免受问题困扰的努力，实际上反而会制造更多的问题。如果你试图安排人、事、物，以免它们打扰你，你就会开始觉得生活处处与你作对。你会感到生活充满挣扎，每一天都无比沉重，因为你必须控制和对抗一切。竞争、嫉妒和恐惧都会出现。你会觉得任何人，在任何时刻，都可能扰乱你的心绪。他们只需要说一句话或做一件事，你就会立刻感到内心的不安。这让生活充满威胁。这就是为什么你如此忧虑。这就是为什么你的脑海中总是充斥着各种各样的对话。你要么试图弄清楚如何阻止事情发生，要么试图弄清楚事情发生后该如何应对。你在与造物主抗争，而这正是造物主本身成为你生命中最可怕之物的原因。

The alternative is to decide not to fight with life. You realize and accept that life is not under your control. Life is continuously changing, and if you’re trying to control it, you’ll never be able to fully live it. Instead of living life, you’ll be afraid of life. But once you’ve decided not to fight with life, you’ll have to face the fear that was causing you to fight. Fortunately, you don’t have to keep this fear inside of you. There is such a thing as a life without fear. In order to relate to this possibility, we must first have a deeper understanding of fear itself.

另一种选择是决定不再与生活抗争。你要意识到并接受生活并非由你掌控。生活瞬息万变，如果你试图控制它，就永远无法真正体验生活。你不会真正地生活，反而会恐惧生活。但一旦你决定不再与生活抗争，就必须面对让你与之抗争的恐惧。幸运的是，你不必将这种恐惧深藏心底。的确存在一种没有恐惧的生活。为了理解这种可能性，我们首先必须对恐惧本身有更深刻的理解。

When you have fear inside of you, the events of life invariably stimulate it. Like a rock thrown into water, the world with its continuous changes creates ripples in whatever is held within you. There’s nothing wrong with that. Life creates situations that push you to your edges, all with the effect of removing what is blocked inside of you. That which is blocked and buried within you forms the root of fear. Fear is caused by blockages in the flow of your energy. When your energy is blocked, it can’t come up and feed your heart. Therefore, your heart becomes weak. When your heart is weak it becomes susceptible to lower vibrations, and one of the lowest of all vibrations is fear. Fear is the cause of every problem. It’s the root of all prejudices and the negative emotions of anger, jealousy, and possessiveness. If you had no fear, you could be perfectly happy living in this world. Nothing would bother you. You’d be willing to face everything and everyone because you wouldn’t have fear inside of you that could cause you disturbance.

当你内心充满恐惧时，生活中的种种事件无一例外地会刺激它。就像一块石头投入水中，世界不断变化，在你内心深处激起涟漪。这本身并无不妥。生活会创造各种境遇，将你推向极限，其最终目的都是为了清除你内心深处的阻塞。那些被阻塞和埋藏在你内心的东西，正是恐惧的根源。恐惧源于能量流动受阻。当你的能量受阻时，它无法涌现，滋养你的心灵。因此，你的心灵变得虚弱。当你的心灵虚弱时，它更容易受到低频振动的影响，而恐惧正是所有低频振动之一。恐惧是所有问题的根源。它是所有偏见以及愤怒、嫉妒和占有欲等负面情绪的根源。如果你没有恐惧，你就能在这个世界上无比快乐地生活。没有什么能困扰你。你会愿意面对一切人和事，因为你的内心不会有恐惧来扰乱你的心绪。

The purpose of spiritual evolution is to remove the blockages that cause your fear. The alternative is to protect your blockages so that you don’t have to feel fear. To do this, however, you will have to try to control everything in order to avoid your inner issues. It’s hard to understand how we decided that avoiding our inner issues is an intelligent thing to do, but everybody’s doing it. Everyone is saying, “I will do every single thing I can to keep my stuff. If you say anything that disturbs me, I will defend myself. I’ll yell at you and make you take it back. If you cause any disturbance inside of me, I will make you so sorry.” In other words, if somebody does something that stimulates fear, you think they did something wrong. You then do everything you can to make sure they never do it again. First you defend yourself, and then you protect yourself. You do whatever you can to keep from feeling disturbance.

灵性进化的目的是消除导致你恐惧的障碍。另一种选择是保护这些障碍，这样你就不必感受恐惧。然而，要做到这一点，你必须试图控制一切，以逃避内心的问题。我们很难理解为什么会认为逃避内心的问题是一种明智的做法，但每个人都在这样做。每个人都在说：“我会竭尽全力守护我的东西。如果你说了任何让我不安的话，我会为自己辩护。我会冲你大吼，让你收回那些话。如果你在我内心造成任何不安，我会让你后悔莫及。”换句话说，如果有人做了让你感到恐惧的事情，你就会认为他们做错了。然后你会竭尽所能确保他们以后不再这样做。首先，你会为自己辩护，然后你会保护自己。你会竭尽所能避免感受到不安。

Eventually, you become wise enough to realize that you do not want that stuff inside of you. It doesn’t matter who stimulates it. It doesn’t matter what situation hits it. It doesn’t matter whether it makes sense, or whether it seems fair or not. Unfortunately, most of us are not that wise. We’re really not trying to be free of our stuff; we’re trying to justify keeping it.

最终，你会足够明智地意识到，你不想要那些东西留在你的心里。是谁刺激了它，是什么情况让它产生这种想法，是否合情合理，是否公平，都无关紧要。可惜的是，我们大多数人都没有那么明智。我们其实并不是想摆脱这些东西，而是在试图为保留它们找借口。

If you truly want to grow spiritually, you’ll realize that keeping your stuff is keeping you trapped. Eventually you’ll want out, at any cost. You will then realize that life is actually trying to help you. Life is surrounding you with people and situations that stimulate growth. You don’t have to decide who’s right or wrong. You don’t have to worry about other people’s issues. You only have to be willing to open your heart in the face of anything and everything, and permit the purification process to take place. When you do this, the first thing you’ll see is that situations will unfold that hit your stuff. But, in truth, that’s exactly what has been happening your entire life. The only difference is that now you see it as a good thing because it’s an opportunity to let go.

如果你真心想要在灵性上成长，你会意识到，执着于过去和现在只会让你深陷其中。最终，你会不惜一切代价想要挣脱束缚。那时你就会明白，生活其实是在帮助你。生活围绕着你，为你安排各种人和事，这些都能促进你的成长。你无需评判谁对谁错，也无需为他人的烦恼而忧虑。你只需要敞开心扉，坦然面对一切，允许净化的过程自然发生。当你这样做时，首先你会发现，一些事情会接踵而至，冲击着你曾经的执念。但事实上，这正是你一生都在经历的事情。唯一的区别在于，现在你把它看作是一件好事，因为它是一个让你放下执念的机会。

The stuff that holds you down periodically rears its head. When it does, let it go. You simply permit the pain to come up into your heart and pass through. If you do that, it will pass. If you are sincerely seeking truth, you’ll let go every time. This is the beginning and end of the entire path—you surrender yourself to the process of emptying yourself. When you work with this, you start to learn the subtler laws of the process of letting go.

那些让你感到压抑的事物会周期性地浮现。当它们出现时，就放手吧。你只需允许痛苦涌入你的心间，然后自然流淌。如果你这样做，它就会过去。如果你真心寻求真理，你每次都会学会放手。这就是整个修行之路的起点和终点——你把自己交付给一个清空自我的过程。当你实践这个过程时，你便开始领悟到放手的微妙法则。

There is a law you will learn very early in the game because it is an unavoidable truth. You will learn it early, but you will fall many times while trying to adhere to it. The law is very straightforward: When your stuff gets hit, let go right then because it will be harder later. It won’t be easier if you explore it or play with it, hoping to take the edge off. It won’t be easier to think about it, talk about it, or try to release only part of it at a time. If you want to be free to the core of your being, you must let go right away because it will not be easier later.

你会在游戏初期就领悟到一条法则，因为它是一个无法回避的真理。你会很快明白它，但在试图遵循它的过程中，你会屡屡跌倒。这条法则非常简单明了：当你的内心受到打击时，立刻放手，因为之后只会更难。试图去探索或玩弄它，希望以此减轻痛苦，并不会更容易。思考它、谈论它，或者试图一次只释放一部分，也不会更容易。如果你想要获得真正的自由，就必须立刻放手，因为之后只会更难。

In order to live by this law, you have to understand its principles. First, you must be aware that there is something within you that needs to be released. You must then be aware that you, the one who notices the stuff coming up, are distinct from what you’re experiencing. You are noticing it, but who are you? This place of centered awareness is the seat of the witness, the seat of Self. That is the only seat from which you can let go. Let’s say you notice that something in your heart gets hit. If you let go and stay in the seat of awareness, what you are noticing will pass. If you don’t let go, and instead get lost in the disturbed feelings and thoughts that arise, you’ll see a sequence of events unfold so quickly you won’t know what hit you.

为了遵循这条法则，你必须理解它的原则。首先，你必须意识到你内心深处有一些东西需要释放。然后，你必须意识到，你——那个觉察到这些感受的人——与你正在经历的事物是不同的。你在觉察，但你是谁？这种专注觉察的状态是见证者的居所，是自我的居所。只有从这里，你才能真正放下。假设你注意到你的内心受到了冲击。如果你放下执念，保持觉察的状态，你所觉察到的一切都会过去。如果你不放下，反而沉溺于涌现的纷乱情绪和念头中，你会看到一系列事件迅速发生，让你措手不及。

If you don’t let go, you’ll notice that the energy that got stimulated in your heart works like a magnet. It’s a phenomenally attractive force that will pull your consciousness into it. The next thing you know, you won’t be there. You won’t maintain the same perspective of awareness that you had when you first noticed the disturbance. You will leave the seat of objective awareness from which you saw your heart begin to react, and you will get involved in the shifting energies coming from your heart. Some time later you’ll come back and realize you weren’t there. You’ll come back and realize that you were totally lost in your stuff. Then you will hope that you didn’t say or do anything you’ll regret.

如果你不放手，你会发现心中被激发出的能量就像磁铁一样。它是一种极其强大的吸引力，会将你的意识拉向它。接下来，你就会发现自己已经不在了。你无法保持最初察觉到这种变化时的那种觉知视角。你会离开你最初观察到心脏开始做出反应的客观觉知位置，转而卷入源自心脏的不断变化的能量之中。过一段时间后，你会回过头来，意识到自己当时并不在那里。你会回过头来，意识到自己完全迷失在了自己的思绪中。那时，你会祈祷自己没有说过或做过任何会让你后悔的事情。

You’ll look at the clock, and five minutes will have gone by, or an hour, or even a year. You can lose your clarity for quite some time. Where did you go? How did you come back? We will address these questions shortly, but what really matters is that when you’re seeing clearly, you’re not going anywhere. You’re simply sitting in the seat of centered awareness watching your stuff get hit. As long as you’re watching, you’re not getting lost in it.

你会看看时间，五分钟过去了，也可能一个小时过去了，甚至一年过去了。你可能会长时间失去清醒的头脑。你去了哪里？你又是如何回来的？我们稍后会探讨这些问题，但真正重要的是，当你看得清楚的时候，你并没有迷失方向。你只是静静地坐在觉知的中心，看着你的事物发生。只要你保持觉知，你就不会迷失其中。

The key is to understand that if you don’t let go immediately, the disturbing force of the activated energy draws the focus of your consciousness. As your consciousness gets immersed in the disturbance, you lose your clear seat of Self. It happens instantaneously. There’s no feeling of going anywhere, any more than there is when you leave the room by getting absorbed in a book or TV show. You simply lose the fixed point of consciousness from which you were objectively aware of your surroundings. Your consciousness leaves the centered position of witnessing the many energies around you, and you get sucked into focusing on just one of them.

关键在于理解，如果你不立即放手，激活能量的扰动力量就会吸引你的意识焦点。当你的意识沉浸于这种扰动之中时，你便失去了清晰的自我意识。这一切瞬间发生。你不会感到自己要去往何处，就像你沉浸于书本或电视节目中而离开房间一样。你只是失去了原本客观感知周围环境的意识焦点。你的意识离开了观察周围众多能量的中心位置，转而专注于其中一种能量。

This leaving the seat of Self is not generally a willful act. The laws of attraction will cause it to happen. Consciousness is always drawn to the most distracting object: the bumped toe, the loud noise, or the hurting heart. It’s the same law, both inside and out. The consciousness goes to the place that distracts it the most. That’s what we mean when we say, “It was so loud it caught my attention.” It drew your consciousness to it. When a blockage gets hit, this same attraction takes place, and the consciousness gets pulled to the source of discomfort. That place then becomes your seat of consciousness. After the discomfort settles down and lets you go, you’ll naturally drift back toward your higher seat of awareness. This is where you sit when you’re not distracted by disturbance. But as important as this higher seat is, it is equally important to see what happens when you are distracted by disturbance—your seat of consciousness falls down to where the disturbance is happening, and the whole world looks different.

这种离开自我中心的状态通常并非出于自愿，而是吸引力法则导致的。意识总是会被最令人分心的事物所吸引：比如磕到的脚趾、震耳欲聋的噪音，或是心痛的悸动。无论内在还是外在，这都是同样的法则。意识会趋向最令它分心的地方。这就是我们常说的“声音太大了，吸引了我的注意力”的含义。它吸引了你的意识。当遇到阻碍时，同样的吸引力也会发生，意识会被拉向不适的源头。那个地方就成了你的意识中心。当不适感消退，让你离开之后，你自然会回到更高的意识中心。当你不受干扰时，你就处于这个意识中心。但是，尽管更高的意识中心很重要，但同样重要的是要观察当你被干扰分心时会发生什么——你的意识中心会落到干扰发生的地方，整个世界看起来都不一样了。

Let’s analyze this fall, step by step. It begins when you get pulled down into the disturbed energy. You end up exactly where you don’t belong. The last place you want to put your consciousness is down there. But that’s where it will get pulled. Now, as you look out through your disturbed energy, everything is distorted by the haze of your disturbance. Things that looked beautiful now look ugly. Things you liked, now look dark and depressing. But nothing has really changed. It’s just that you’re looking at life from that seat of disturbance.

让我们一步步分析这种坠落。它始于你被拉入紊乱的能量之中。最终，你会落到你根本不该在的地方。你最不想让自己的意识落在那里，但它却会被拉到那里。现在，当你透过紊乱的能量向外看时，一切都被紊乱的迷雾扭曲了。曾经美丽的事物现在看起来丑陋不堪，曾经喜欢的事物现在显得阴暗压抑。但实际上，一切都没有改变。只不过，你是从紊乱的视角来看待生活的。

Each of these shifts in your perception should remind you to let go. The moment you start seeing that you don’t like the people you used to like, the moment you start seeing that your life looks really different, the moment it all starts getting negative—let go. You should have let go before, but you didn’t. The trouble is that it’s more difficult now. You could have taken one breath and let go when it started. Now it takes serious work to get your previous seat of consciousness back without going through the whole cycle.

你认知上的每一次转变都应该提醒你放手。当你开始发现自己不再喜欢以前喜欢的人，当你开始意识到自己的生活发生了翻天覆地的变化，当一切开始变得消极——放手吧。你本该早点放手，但你没有。问题在于，现在放手更难了。你本可以在一切开始时就深吸一口气，然后放手。现在，你需要付出巨大的努力才能找回之前的意识状态，而无需经历整个循环。

The cycle is the time it takes from the moment you leave your seat of relative clarity until you come back. This period of time is determined by the depth of the energy blockage that caused the initial disturbance. Once activated, the blockage must run its course. If you don’t let go, you get sucked in. You are no longer free; you are caught. Once you fall from your seat of relative clarity, you are under the mercy of the disturbed energy. If that blockage is stimulated by an ongoing situation, you may stay down there for a long time. If it happens to be just a passing event, and the energy released by the blockage dissipates immediately, then you’ll find that you drift back up quickly. The main point is that it’s not under your control. You lost it.

这个周期指的是从你离开相对清醒的状态到你重新回到清醒状态所需的时间。这段时间取决于最初造成干扰的能量阻塞的深度。一旦阻塞被激活，它就必须经历其自身的过程。如果你不放手，就会被卷入其中。你不再自由，而是被困住了。一旦你从相对清醒的状态跌落，你就只能任由紊乱的能量摆布。如果阻塞是由某种持续存在的情况刺激的，你可能会长时间停留在低谷。如果这只是一个短暂的事件，阻塞释放的能量立即消散，那么你会发现自己很快就能重新回到清醒的状态。关键在于，这并非由你掌控。你失去了控制。

This is the anatomy of falling. When you’re in this state of disturbance, your tendency will be to act in order to try to fix things. You don’t have the clarity to see what’s going on; you just want the disturbance to stop. So you start getting down to your survival instincts. You may feel that you have to do something drastic. You may want to leave your husband or wife, or move, or quit your job. The mind starts saying all kinds of things because it doesn’t like this space, and it wants to get away from it any way it can.

这就是坠落的本质。当你处于这种混乱状态时，你的倾向是采取行动来试图解决问题。你无法清晰地看清发生了什么；你只想让混乱停止。于是，你的求生本能开始发挥作用。你可能会觉得必须采取一些激烈的措施。你可能想离开你的伴侣，或者搬家，或者辞职。你的大脑开始胡思乱想，因为它不喜欢这种境地，它想尽一切办法逃离它。

Now that you’ve fallen to that point, here comes the crème de la crème. Imagine that while you’re lost in the disturbed energy, you actually do one or more of the things that your mind is telling you to do. Imagine what would happen if you actually quit your job, or if you decide, “I’ve held this in long enough. I’m going to give him a piece of my mind.” You have no idea how big a step down that is. It’s one thing if the disturbance is going on inside of you. But the moment you allow it to express itself, the moment you let that energy move your body, you have descended to another level. Now it’s almost impossible to let go. If you start yelling at somebody, if you actually tell someone how you feel about them from this state of nonclarity, you have involved that person’s heart and mind in your stuff. Now both of your egos are involved. Once you externalize these energies, you will want to defend your actions and make them look appropriate. But the other person will never think they were appropriate.

既然你已经跌落到这个地步，接下来才是最精彩的部分。想象一下，当你迷失在混乱的能量中时，你竟然真的去做了你头脑中指示你做的一件或几件事。想象一下，如果你真的辞职了，或者你决定：“我已经忍够了，我要好好教训他一顿。”会发生什么？你根本无法想象这会是多大的堕落。如果这种混乱只发生在你的内心，那还好说。但当你允许它表达出来，当你让这种能量支配你的身体时，你就已经堕落到了另一个层次。现在，你几乎不可能放手。如果你开始对某人大吼大叫，如果你在这种混乱的状态下真的向某人倾诉你的感受，你就已经把对方的身心卷入了你的情绪之中。现在，你们双方的自我都卷入了其中。一旦你将这些能量外化，你就会想要为自己的行为辩护，让它们看起来合情合理。但对方永远不会认为你的行为是合理的。

Now even more forces are keeping you down. First you fall into the darkness, and then you manifest that darkness. When you do this, you are literally taking the energy of the blockage and passing it on. When you dump your stuff into this world, it’s like painting the world with your stuff. You put more of that kind of energy into your environment and it comes back to you. You are now surrounded by people who will interact with you accordingly. It’s just another form of “environmental pollution,” and it will affect your life.

现在，有更多的力量在压制你。你先是陷入黑暗，然后又将黑暗具象化。当你这样做时，你实际上是在吸收阻塞的能量并将其传递下去。当你把自己的负面情绪倾倒在这个世界上时，就如同用这些负面情绪涂抹世界。你把更多类似的能量注入到你的环境中，而这些能量最终会回到你身上。你周围的人也会以同样的方式对待你。这不过是另一种形式的“环境污染”，它会影响你的生活。

That is how negative cycles happen. You actually take a piece of your stuff, which is nothing but deeply seated disturbance from your past, and you implant it in the hearts of those around you. At some point it will come back to you. Anything you put out comes back. Imagine if you got upset and fully released your disturbed energies onto another person. This is how people ruin relationships and destroy their lives.

这就是负面循环的成因。你实际上是将自己的一部分——其实就是过去根深蒂固的负面情绪——植入到周围人的心中。总有一天，它会回到你身上。你付出的一切都会回到你身上。想象一下，如果你情绪激动，把所有的负面能量都倾泻到另一个人身上，会发生什么？人们就是这样破坏人际关系，毁掉自己的人生。

How far down can you go? Once you’re weakened, another blockage could get hit, and yet another. You can fall all the way down until your life is an absolute mess. You can reach a point of total loss of control and completely lose your center. In this state, your previous seat of clarity may drift by once in a while, but you can’t hold it. Now you’re lost. Do you doubt that a single blockage getting hit in your heart could cause a fall that lasts a lifetime? It has been known to happen.

你能堕落到什么地步？一旦你变得虚弱，另一个阻塞点就可能被击中，然后又一个。你会一路跌落谷底，直到生活彻底崩溃。你会彻底失去控制，失去内心的平静。在这种状态下，你曾经清醒的意识或许偶尔会浮现，但你无法抓住它。现在，你迷失了方向。你难道怀疑，心中一个阻塞点的出现，就足以让你坠入深渊，终生难愈吗？这样的事情并非没有发生过。

What if all you had to do to avoid all of this was to let go in the beginning? If you had, you would have gone up instead of down. That’s how it works. When a blockage gets hit, it’s a good thing. It’s time to open up internally and release the blocked energy. If you let go, and permit the purification process to take place inside, that blocked energy will be released. When it’s released and allowed to flow up, it becomes purified and merges back into your center of consciousness. This energy then strengthens you instead of weakening you. You begin to go up and up, higher and higher, and you learn the secret of the ascent. The secret of the ascent is to never look down—always look up.

如果避免这一切的唯一方法就是在一开始就放下执念呢？如果你做到了，你就会向上攀登而不是向下沉沦。事情就是这样运作的。当遇到阻碍时，这其实是件好事。是时候打开内在的通道，释放被阻塞的能量了。如果你放下执念，允许内在的净化过程发生，那些被阻塞的能量就会被释放。当它被释放并向上流动时，它会被净化，并重新融入你的意识中心。这种能量会增强你的力量，而不是削弱你。你会开始不断向上攀登，越来越高，最终你会领悟到上升的秘密。上升的秘密就是永远不要向下看——永远向上看。

No matter what happens below you, just turn your eyes upward and relax your heart. You do not have to leave the seat of Self in order to deal with the darkness. It will purify itself if you let it. Getting involved in the darkness does not dispel darkness; it feeds it. Don’t even turn toward it. If you see disturbed energies within you, it’s okay. Don’t think that you don’t have blockages left to release. Just sit in the seat of awareness and never leave. No matter what goes on below you, open your heart and let it go. Your heart will become purified, and you will never know another fall.

无论你身下发生什么，只需抬起头，放松你的心。你无需离开自我之座去应对黑暗。如果你顺其自然，它自会净化自身。卷入黑暗并不能驱散黑暗，反而会滋养它。甚至不要靠近它。如果你看到内心能量紊乱，那也没关系。不要以为你已经没有需要释放的阻塞。只需安住于觉知之座，永不离开。无论你身下发生什么，敞开你的心扉，放下一切。你的心将会得到净化，你将不再经历任何跌倒。

If you fall along the way, just get up and forget it. Use the lesson to strengthen your resolve. Let go right then. Do not rationalize, blame, or try to figure it out. Don’t do anything. Just let go immediately, and allow the energy to go back to the highest center of consciousness it can achieve. If you feel shame, let it go. If you feel fear, let it go. All of these are the remnants of the blocked energy that is finally being purified.

如果途中跌倒，就爬起来，忘掉它。把这次经历当作力量的源泉，增强你的决心。立刻放手。不要找借口，不要责怪，也不要试图弄明白。什么都不要做。就立刻放手，让能量回归它所能达到的最高意识中心。如果你感到羞愧，就放下它。如果你感到恐惧，就放下它。所有这些都是阻塞能量的残余，而它们最终正在被净化。

Always let go as soon as you’re aware that you didn’t. Don’t waste your time; use the energy to go up. You are a great being who has been given a tremendous opportunity to explore beyond yourself. The whole process is very exciting, and you will have good times and bad times. All sorts of things will happen. That’s the fun of the journey.

一旦意识到自己没有放手，就立刻放手。不要浪费时间，把精力用来提升自己。你是一个了不起的人，被赋予了探索自我之外的绝佳机会。整个过程令人兴奋，你会经历顺境和逆境。各种各样的事情都会发生。这正是旅程的乐趣所在。

So don’t fall. Let go. No matter what it is, let it go. The bigger it is, the higher the reward of letting go and the worse the fall if you don’t. It’s pretty black-and-white. You either let go or you don’t. There really isn’t anything in between. So let all of your blockages and disturbances become the fuel for the journey. That which is holding you down can become a powerful force that raises you up. You just have to be willing to take the ascent.

所以，别跌倒。放手。无论是什么，都放手。事情越大，放手的回报就越高；不放手，跌倒的后果就越严重。这事非黑即白。要么放手，要么不放手。没有中间地带。所以，让所有的阻碍和干扰都成为你旅程的燃料。那些曾经束缚你的事物，可以变成一股强大的力量，将你托起。你只需要愿意攀登。
