12
12
taking down the walls
拆除墙壁

At some point in your growth, it starts to become quieter inside. This happens quite naturally as you take a deeper seat within yourself. You then come to realize that though you have always been in there, you have been completely overwhelmed by the constant barrage of thoughts, emotions, and sensory inputs that draw on your consciousness. As you see this, it begins to dawn on you that you might actually be able to go beyond all these disturbances. The more you sit in the seat of witness consciousness, the more you realize that since you are completely independent of what you are watching, there must be a way to break free of the magical hold that the psyche has on your awareness. There must be a way out.

在成长的某个阶段，你的内心会逐渐平静下来。当你更深入地探索自我时，这种平静自然而然地发生。你会意识到，虽然你一直都在那里，但你却一直被源源不断的思绪、情绪和感官刺激所淹没，这些都占据了你的意识。当你意识到这一点时，你开始明白，或许你真的可以超越所有这些干扰。你越是静下心来，以观察者的视角看待事物，就越会明白，既然你完全独立于你所观察的一切，那么一定存在一种方法可以挣脱心灵对你意识的束缚。一定有一条出路。

This inner breakthrough to complete freedom is traditionally depicted by the overused and generally misunderstood term: “enlightenment.” The problem is that our views of enlightenment are either based upon our personal experiences or upon our limited conceptual understanding. Since most people have never had experiences in this realm, the state of enlightenment is either scoffed at completely or viewed as the ultimate mystical state accessible to almost no one. It’s safe to say that the only thing most people know for sure about enlightenment is that they are not there.

这种通往彻底自由的内在突破，传统上用一个被过度使用且普遍被误解的词——“开悟”——来描述。问题在于，我们对开悟的理解要么基于个人经验，要么基于我们有限的概念认知。由于大多数人从未体验过这种境界，开悟要么被彻底嘲笑，要么被视为几乎无人能够企及的终极神秘境界。可以肯定地说，大多数人对开悟唯一确定的认知就是他们尚未达到开悟的境界。

However, with the understanding that thoughts, emotions, and sensory objects are simply passing before your consciousness, it becomes reasonable to question whether your sense of awareness need be limited to this experience. What if consciousness were to remove its focus from your personal set of thoughts, your personal set of emotions, and your limited sensory input? Would you become untethered from the bonds of the personal self and be set free to explore beyond? And how, exactly, did consciousness become bound to the personal self to begin with? The problem with even attempting to consider these questions is that they call for a discussion of what exists beyond the confines of the mind. Obviously, that discussion is very difficult to have from within the mental structure we are so accustomed to using. For this reason, we will begin exploring the untethered state through the use of an allegory. Much like Plato used dialogue to tell his “Allegory of the Cave” in 360 BC, we will use a short story to tell our allegory of a very special house.

然而，既然我们理解了思想、情感和感官对象都只是意识的过客，那么质疑我们的意识是否必须局限于此就变得合情合理了。如果意识不再专注于我们个人的思想、情感和有限的感官输入，会发生什么呢？我们是否会挣脱个人自我的束缚，自由地探索更广阔的世界？而意识最初又是如何与个人自我绑定的呢？即便只是尝试思考这些问题，也存在一个难题：它们需要我们探讨超越思维局限之外的事物。显然，在我们习以为常的思维框架内，这样的探讨是极其困难的。因此，我们将通过寓言来探索这种不受束缚的状态。正如柏拉图在公元前360年用对话讲述了他的“洞穴寓言”一样，我们将用一个短篇故事来讲述一个关于一座特殊房子的寓言。

Imagine that you found yourself in the midst of an open field where the sun was always shining. It was a beautiful place of great light and great openness. It was so beautiful that you decided you wanted to live there. So you bought the land, and right in the middle of the enormous field, you began personally designing and building the house of your dreams. You put down a solid foundation because you wanted the house to be very strong and to last a long time. You built the house out of concrete blocks so that you wouldn’t have any problems with decaying or leaking. To make the house ecologically sound, you decided to put in very few windows and to build a roof with lots of overhang. After you put in the windows, and the house was complete, you realized that a lot of heat still came in. So you installed high-quality protective shutters that not only reflected sunlight and heat back to the outside, but also could be locked down for security purposes. It was a very large house that could store enough supplies to allow for complete self-sufficiency. You even built separate quarters for a quiet acquaintance who would keep the house clean and leave you to be in solitude. And solitude it would be, since your romantic quest included a commitment to no phones, radios, televisions, or Internet connections.

想象一下，你置身于一片阳光普照的开阔田野之中。这里光线充足，视野开阔，美不胜收。你被这里的美景深深吸引，决定在此定居。于是，你买下了这块地，在这片广袤的田野中央，开始亲手设计建造梦想中的房子。你打下了坚实的地基，因为你希望房子坚固耐用，能够长久屹立。你用混凝土砌块建造房屋，这样就不会出现腐烂或漏水的问题。为了使房子更加环保，你决定只安装少量的窗户，并建造一个屋檐宽阔的屋顶。窗户安装完毕，房子也竣工了，但你发现仍然有很多热量进入室内。于是，你安装了高质量的防护百叶窗，这些百叶窗不仅可以将阳光和热量反射到室外，还可以上锁以确保安全。这是一栋非常大的房子，可以储存足够的物资，让你完全实现自给自足。你甚至为一位安静的熟人建造了单独的房间，让她打扫房子，让你享受独处时光。而你的独处时光也的确如此，因为你的浪漫追求包括放弃电话、收音机、电视和互联网连接。

Your house was finally finished, and you were very excited to be living out there. You loved the openness of the field and all the light and beauty of nature. But most of all, you were enamored with the house. You had put your heart and soul into every aspect of the design, and it showed—it was truly “you.” In fact, over time, between your infatuation with the house and your growing discomfort with all the strange sights and sounds outside, you started spending more time indoors. It was then that you realized that with the shutters and doors fully locked down, the house actually began to feel like a fortress. And this was just fine with you. Being a city person, it was pretty scary living so far out of touch in total isolation. But you were committed to making it on your own.

你的房子终于完工了，你兴奋极了，迫不及待地想住进去。你喜欢开阔的田野，喜欢大自然的光影和美景。但最让你着迷的还是这栋房子本身。你倾注了全部心血，设计中的每一个细节都体现了这一点——它真正代表了“你”。事实上，随着时间的推移，你对房子的迷恋与对屋外陌生景象和声音日益增长的不适感交织在一起，让你开始更多地待在室内。这时你才意识到，当百叶窗和门窗全部锁好后，房子真的像一座堡垒。而你对此也欣然接受。作为一个城市人，生活在如此远离尘嚣、完全与世隔绝的地方，确实让人感到有些害怕。但你决心要靠自己闯出一片天地。

So you gradually became accustomed to living safely within the confines of the house. You happily went about your business of reading and writing as you had always longed to do. It was actually quite comfortable in there since it was fully climate controlled, and you had been wise enough to install a modern full-spectrum lighting system. Ironically, you found your house so comfortable, enjoyable, and safe that you stopped thinking about the outside altogether. After all, the inside was familiar, predictable, and within the realm of your control. The outside was unknown, unpredictable, and completely out of your control. Your sense of inner sanctum was supported by the fact that when the shutters and blinds were locked in place they blended like paintings on the walls, and you never even considered risking going outside to unlock them. They were so well made that when the lights were turned off it was absolutely pitch black, day or night. But since you were accustomed to never turning off the lights, you didn’t notice this until they started burning out. It was only then that you realized your predicament: no one had left you replacement bulbs compatible with the new system. This meant that once the final light failed, you were left to find your way around the house in absolute darkness.

于是，你渐渐习惯了在房子里安全地生活。你如愿以偿地读书写作，这正是你一直以来梦寐以求的。房子里的确很舒适，因为它配备了全套温控系统，而且你明智地安装了现代化的全光谱照明系统。讽刺的是，你发现自己的房子如此舒适、惬意、安全，以至于你完全不再去想外面的世界。毕竟，室内的一切都是熟悉的、可预测的，并且都在你的掌控之中。而室外的一切却是未知的、不可预测的，并且完全超出你的掌控。百叶窗和卷帘锁上后，与墙壁融为一体，就像一幅幅画作，这更加强化了你对这片“内殿”的敬畏之情，你甚至从未想过要冒险出去解锁。它们的做工非常精良，关灯后，无论白天黑夜，屋内都漆黑一片。但由于你习惯了从不关灯，直到它们开始烧坏，你才注意到这一点。直到那时你才意识到自己的困境：没有人给你留下与新系统兼容的替换灯泡。这意味着，一旦最后一盏灯也坏了，你就只能在彻底的黑暗中摸索着在房子里走动了。

From that point forward, the only light you had came from the few candles you kept for emergencies. But there were very few of these, so you conserved them well. Being a person who loved light, this was very difficult for you. Yet it was not difficult enough to force you to overcome the fears you had developed about leaving the safety of your house. Eventually, the stress of living in this darkness took its toll on your health, both physically and mentally. With time, the very memory of the beautiful sunlit field began to fade from your mind, never to return again.

从那时起，你唯一的照明就只剩下几根应急蜡烛。但蜡烛数量很少，所以你格外珍惜。你生性热爱光明，这让你倍感煎熬。然而，这点痛苦还不足以让你克服对离开家门的恐惧。最终，长期生活在黑暗中，你的身心都受到了损害。随着时间的流逝，那片阳光普照的美丽田野的记忆也渐渐从你的脑海中消逝，再也没有出现过。

You became very concerned about keeping the house lit. The only light you knew about was the light you created in the darkness with your precious candles. It became pretty lonely in there. You were cut off from everything, and the only comfort you felt was the sense of protection your house afforded you. You were no longer aware of exactly what you were so afraid of; you were just aware of always being scared and uncomfortable. It was all you could do just to try to hold yourself together. You even stopped reading and writing because of the lack of light. It was dark, and you too were falling into darkness.

你开始非常在意如何保持屋内的照明。你唯一知道的光亮，就是用你珍爱的蜡烛在黑暗中营造出来的微光。屋里变得异常孤独。你与世隔绝，唯一能让你感到慰藉的，只有房子带给你的安全感。你不再清楚自己究竟在害怕什么；你只知道自己一直处于恐惧和不安之中。你所能做的，只是努力让自己保持镇定。因为缺少光线，你甚至停止了阅读和写作。黑暗笼罩着你，你也正坠入黑暗之中。

Then one day, the housekeeper, who shared your overwhelming need to stay in the safety of the house, called you down to the storage cellar. You were amazed by what you saw. A full supply of emergency flashlights had been found that could be powered simply by shaking them. Your housekeeper had already set some up, and the cellar was fully radiant. This was a true turning point in your life.

有一天，管家——她和你一样，都迫切希望待在房子里——叫你下到储藏室。你被眼前的景象惊呆了。那里竟然藏着一大堆应急手电筒，只要摇晃一下就能充电。管家已经摆放好了一些，整个储藏室灯火通明。这真是你人生的一个转折点。

You set about your business of trying to create light, beauty, and happiness within the confines of your house. You decorated each room and worked together to keep the light shining brightly until you went to sleep. You started reading and writing again, and it turned out that your housemate loved reading your writings. In fact, it was not just the artificial lights that were lighting the house. The ember of love had begun to glow in both of your hearts. Imagine the light you could create together instead of apart. You began spending all of your time with each other, and you even staged a marriage ceremony. It was so beautiful as you vowed to take care of each other and bring love and light into your home. Compared to the darkness in which you had been living, this was heaven.

你们开始努力在有限的居家空间里创造光明、美丽和幸福。你们精心布置了每个房间，齐心协力让灯光一直明亮到你们入睡。你们重新开始阅读和写作，结果发现室友很喜欢读你们的作品。事实上，照亮这栋房子的不仅仅是人造灯光。爱的火花在你们彼此的心中开始闪耀。想象一下，如果你们能够携手共创光明，而不是各自分离，那该是多么美好的景象。你们开始把所有时间都花在彼此身上，甚至还举行了婚礼。当你们许下誓言，要彼此照顾，将爱与光明带入家中时，一切都显得那么美好。与你们曾经生活在的黑暗相比，这里简直就是天堂。

One day you came across a book in your library. It interested you because it talked about the natural, radiant light that exists “outside.” It even spoke of bathing in that light. But it was talking about more light than you could ever imagine, without anyone having to do anything to create it. This was confusing to you. After all, the only light you knew about was the artificial light from candles and flashlights. How could you make that much light and keep it going? You didn’t have a clue what this book was talking about because you could only view things in relation to the way you were living. You were living inside the house, and therefore you were living inside of darkness. All the light that you could experience was limited to what you could create within the house. You had lived there for so long that all your hopes, dreams, philosophies, and beliefs were founded upon being inside that dark house. Your whole world was about keeping together the life you had managed to build for yourself within the confines of the house.

有一天，你在图书馆里偶然发现了一本书。它引起了你的兴趣，因为它谈到了“外面”存在的自然而耀眼的光芒。书中甚至提到了沐浴在这种光芒中。但它所描述的光芒远超你的想象，而且无需任何人为创造。这让你感到困惑。毕竟，你所知道的光芒只有蜡烛和手电筒的人造光。你怎么可能制造出如此多的光，并且让它持续存在呢？你完全不明白这本书在说什么，因为你只能从你自身的生活方式来理解事物。你住在房子里，因此你生活在黑暗之中。你所能体验到的所有光芒都局限于你在房子里所能创造的。你在那里生活了太久，以至于你所有的希望、梦想、哲学和信仰都建立在那间黑暗的房子里。你的整个世界都围绕着如何在这间房子的局限中维系你为自己建立的生活。

When you continued reading this seemingly mystical book, it spoke of what it was like to actually walk around in this natural light. It seemed to be describing a self-luminous, omnipresent light that shines everywhere all at once. It was a light that falls on everything constantly and evenly. Though you had no frame of reference for understanding this, it touched something deep inside of you. The book then discussed actually going outside, that is, going beyond the walls of the world you have created for yourself. In fact, it said that while you are attached and enamored with the world you created to avoid darkness, you will never know the abundance of natural light that is beyond the confines of your house. How will you ever go outside when you are so dependent upon what you have built inside?

当你继续阅读这本看似神秘的书时，它描述了在自然光下漫步的感受。它似乎在描述一种自发光、无处不在的光芒，它同时照亮了所有地方。这光芒持续均匀地照射着万物。尽管你对此一无所知，但它却触动了你内心深处。书中接着探讨了走出户外，也就是走出你为自己创造的世界。事实上，它指出，当你依恋并沉迷于你为了逃避黑暗而创造的世界时，你永远不会体会到屋檐之外那丰沛的自然光。当你如此依赖自己建造的室内空间时，你又怎能走出户外呢？

The analogy of life inside this house is a perfect fit for our predicament. Our consciousness, our awareness of being, is living deep inside of us in an artificially sealed off area that is absolute. It has four walls, a floor, and a roof. It is so solid that not one ray of natural light comes in. The only light we get is what we manage to create for ourselves. If we don’t create good situations for ourselves, there is darkness. So we are very busy decorating daily. We do this by trying to bring things in there with us—hoping to create at least a little light, in the house of our own making, where we have sealed ourselves off.

这栋房子里的比喻完美地契合了我们目前的困境。我们的意识，我们对存在的感知，深藏于我们体内一个完全封闭、人为打造的绝对空间。它有四面墙、一块地板和一个屋顶，坚固到一丝自然光都无法穿透。我们唯一能获得的光明，是我们自己努力创造的。如果我们不为自己创造美好的环境，黑暗便会笼罩一切。所以我们每天都在忙着“装饰”它。我们试图把各种东西带进这个空间——希望能在我们自己建造的、把自己封闭起来的房子里，至少创造出一丝光亮。

That is the visual: you are inside a house, totally sealed off from natural light, and the house is sitting in the middle of an open field full of brilliant light. But what is your house made of? What are your walls made of? How can they seal off all that light and keep you locked inside? Your house is made of your thoughts and emotions. The walls are made of your psyche. That’s what that house is. It is all your past experiences; all your thoughts and emotions; all the concepts, views, opinions, beliefs, hopes, and dreams that you have collected around yourself. You hold them in place on all sides, including above and below you. You have pulled together in your mind a specific set of thoughts and emotions, and then you have woven them together into a conceptual world in which you live. This mental structure completely blocks you from whatever natural light is on the outside of its walls. You have walls of thoughts thick enough, and closed enough, to where nothing but darkness is inside that structure. You are so entranced into paying attention to your thoughts and emotions that you never go beyond the borders they create.

这就是画面：你身处一栋房子里，与自然光完全隔绝，而这栋房子却坐落在阳光普照的开阔田野中央。但你的房子是由什么构成的？你的墙壁又是由什么构成的？它们如何能阻挡所有的光线，将你困在里面？你的房子是由你的思想和情感构成的。墙壁是由你的心灵构成的。这就是那栋房子的本质。它包含了你所有过去的经历；你所有的想法和情感；你围绕自身积累的所有概念、观点、意见、信仰、希望和梦想。你将它们牢牢地固定在四面八方，包括你的上方和下方。你在脑海中汇集了一系列特定的思想和情感，然后将它们编织成一个你生活其中的概念世界。这种精神结构完全阻挡了你与外界自然光线的接触。你的思想之墙足够厚重，也足够封闭，以至于结构内部只有黑暗。你如此沉迷于关注你的思想和情感，以至于你从未超越它们所创造的边界。

If you want to see how restrictive your walls are, just start walking toward them. Let’s say you have an emotional fear of heights. When you were young you fell off a ladder, and the impression stayed with you. That is one of your walls. If you doubt that it’s a wall, let’s see you walk through it. Let’s say something happens that activates these old feelings of fear, and you decide to walk right toward it. The closer you get, the more you will have the urge to pull back. That which you collected from your past forms a boundary that you intuitively want to avoid. That’s natural, that’s what we do with walls; we avoid running into them. But because you avoid running into them, they lock you inside their perimeter. They become your prison because they are the boundaries of your awareness. Because you are not willing to approach them, you cannot see what is beyond them.

如果你想看看你的心墙有多强，那就试着朝它们走去。假设你恐高，小时候从梯子上摔下来，留下了深刻的印象。这就是你的一道心墙。如果你怀疑它是不是一堵墙，那就试试穿过它。假设发生了一件事，唤起了你尘封已久的恐惧，你决定径直走向它。你越靠近，就越想退缩。你从过去的经历中汲取的教训，在你本能的驱使下，形成了一道想要避开的界限。这很自然，就像我们对待墙壁一样；我们避免撞上它们。但正因为你避免撞上它们，它们反而把你困在了它们的边界之内。它们成了你的牢笼，因为它们是你意识的边界。因为你不愿靠近它们，所以你无法看到它们之外的世界。

When you approach the barrier areas of your thoughts and emotions, it feels like going into an abyss. You don’t want to go near that place. But you can go there, and if you want to get out, you will go there. Eventually you will realize that darkness is not what’s really there. What is really there are the walls that are blocking the infinite light. When you’re looking for light, that is a crucial distinction. If you see a wall and it is protecting you from unending darkness, you will not want to go there. But if you see a wall that is blocking the light, you will want to go there in order to remove the wall. It is often said that you must go through the darkest night in order to get to the infinite light. This is because what we call darkness is really the blockage of light. You must go past these walls.

当你接近思想和情感的屏障时，感觉就像坠入深渊。你不想靠近那里。但你可以去那里，如果你想要离开，你就会去那里。最终你会明白，真正的黑暗并非黑暗本身。真正的黑暗是阻挡无限光明的墙壁。当你寻求光明时，这是一个至关重要的区别。如果你看到一堵墙，它保护你免受无尽黑暗的侵袭，你不会想靠近它。但如果你看到一堵墙阻挡了光明，你会想要靠近它，去移除这堵墙。人们常说，你必须穿越最黑暗的夜晚才能到达无限的光明。这是因为我们所谓的黑暗，实际上是对光明的阻挡。你必须跨越这些墙壁。

It’s not really difficult to get past the walls. Time and again, every day, the natural flow of life collides with our walls and tries to tear them down. But time and again, we defend them. You must realize that when you defend yourself, you are really defending your walls. There is nothing else to defend in there. There is just your awareness of being and the limited house you built to live in. What you are defending is the house you built to protect yourself. You are hiding inside. If something happens to challenge the walls of your psyche, you get highly defensive. You have built a self-concept, moved inside, and now you defend that home with all you have. But what creates that inner home, other than the walls of your thoughts? When you say, “I’m a woman and I’m forty-five years old. I’m married to Joe and I graduated from this school…” those are thoughts. The actual situations don’t exist in there with you except in the form of thoughts that you cling to: “But I was a cheerleader, and I was president of my senior class.” That was thirty years ago. Those situations don’t exist anymore. But they exist inside of you, and they form the walls in which you live.

其实突破这些壁垒并不难。每天，生活的自然流动都会一次又一次地冲击我们的心墙，试图将它们摧毁。但我们却一次又一次地捍卫它们。你必须明白，当你捍卫自己时，你实际上是在捍卫你的心墙。里面没有什么需要捍卫的。只有你对存在的认知，以及你为了居住而建造的那座有限的房子。你捍卫的是你为了保护自己而建造的房子。你躲在里面。如果有什么事情挑战了你心灵的壁垒，你就会变得非常具有防御性。你构建了一个自我概念，住进了里面，现在你用尽一切来捍卫这个家。但是，除了你思想的壁垒之外，还有什么创造了这个内在的家呢？当你说道：“我是一个女人，我45岁了。我嫁给了乔，我毕业于这所学校……”这些都只是想法。真实的情况并不存在于你的内心，它们只是你执着于的想法：“但我曾经是啦啦队长，我还是高年级的学生会主席。”那是三十年前的事了。那些情况早已不复存在。但它们仍然存在于你的内心深处，构成了你生活的围墙。

What if somebody challenges your self-concept and breaks a little hole in it? What if somebody manages to shake one of those foundational thoughts that the house of your psyche is built upon? Imagine if someone told you when you were twenty years old, “Wait a minute. Those are not your parents. You were adopted. Didn’t they ever tell you?” You would adamantly deny it until they showed you the documents. It would shake up your whole inner being. Just one wrong thought and the structure starts to crumble. Tremendous fear and turmoil can open up inside of you simply because something is not the way you thought it was. It shakes you to the core of your being because it challenges the house of thoughts in which you are dwelling. To fix this, you start in with your rationalizations: “I knew they were really nice. They were just like my real parents would’ve been. Imagine them adopting someone like me and bringing me up just like their own. God, they were even more special than I thought they were.” You patched that hole up very well. That’s what we do with our walls. We keep them solid. Nothing is allowed to shake those walls.

如果有人挑战你的自我认知，在你心中撕开一道小小的裂缝，你会作何感想？如果有人动摇了你精神世界赖以建立的根基，你会作何感想？想象一下，如果你二十岁的时候，有人告诉你：“等等，他们不是你的亲生父母。你是被收养的。他们从来没告诉过你吗？”你会坚决否认，直到他们拿出收养文件。这会彻底动摇你的内心。仅仅一个错误的想法，就足以让你的内心开始崩塌。仅仅因为事情并非你所想，你内心就会涌起巨大的恐惧和不安。这会撼动你的灵魂深处，因为它挑战了你赖以生存的思维模式。为了弥补这一点，你会开始寻找各种理由：“我知道他们人很好。他们就像我的亲生父母一样。想想看，他们收养了我，像对待亲生孩子一样抚养我。天哪，他们比我想象的还要特别。”你把那个裂缝堵得严严实实。我们就是这样保护我们的墙的。我们让它们坚固无比。任何东西都不允许动摇这些墙。

Notice that you patched the cracking wall with thoughts. You patched with thoughts that which is made of thoughts. That’s what we do. Just like the people who fearfully locked themselves inside the dark house in the middle of a sunlit field, and then struggled to create some light, we work hard to build a world within the confines of our inner walls that is better than the inner darkness. We decorate our walls with the memories of our past experiences and with our dreams of the future. In other words, we decorate them with thoughts. But just as the people in the house had the potential to step out of their own self-made, artificial world into the beauty of the natural light, you can step outside your house of thoughts into the unlimited. Your awareness can expand to encompass vast space instead of the limited space in which you dwell. Then, when you look back at that little house you built, you will wonder why you were ever in there.

注意，你用思想修补了那道裂痕。你用思想修补了由思想构成的东西。我们就是这样做的。就像那些恐惧地把自己锁在阳光普照的田野中央黑暗小屋里，然后努力创造光亮的人们一样，我们也努力在内心的围墙之内，建造一个比内心黑暗更好的世界。我们用过往经历的记忆和对未来的梦想来装饰我们的墙壁。换句话说，我们用思想来装饰它们。但是，正如小屋里的人们有潜力走出他们自己创造的、人为的世界，拥抱自然之光的美好一样，你也可以走出你思想的小屋，进入无限的宇宙。你的意识可以扩展到广阔的空间，而不是你栖居的有限空间。那时，当你回头看你建造的那座小屋时，你会疑惑自己当初为什么会待在那里。

That is your journey out. True freedom is very close; it’s just on the other side of your walls. Enlightenment is a very special thing. But in truth, one should not focus on it. Focus, instead, on the walls of your own making that are blocking the light. Of what purpose is it to build walls that block the light and then strive for enlightenment? You can get out simply by letting everyday life take down the walls you hold around yourself. You simply don’t participate in supporting, maintaining, and defending your fortress.

这就是你走出困境的旅程。真正的自由近在咫尺，就在你围墙的另一边。开悟固然珍贵，但实际上，你不应该执着于此。相反，你应该关注那些阻挡你光芒的、你自己建造的围墙。建造阻挡光芒的围墙，然后又去追求开悟，这又有何意义呢？你只需让日常生活慢慢拆除你为自己筑起的围墙，就能走出困境。你只需不再参与支撑、维护和捍卫你的堡垒。

Imagine your house of thoughts standing in the middle of an ocean of light from a trillion stars. Imagine your awareness trapped inside the darkness of that house, struggling daily to live off the artificial light of your limited experiences. Now imagine the walls crumbling down, and the effortless release of consciousness expanding into the brilliance of what is and always was. Now give that experience a name—enlightenment.

想象一下，你那由思想构成的房屋矗立在亿万星辰汇聚而成的光海之中。想象一下，你的意识被困在那黑暗的房屋里，日复一日地挣扎着，试图依靠你有限经验所发出的人造光芒生存。现在，想象一下，墙壁崩塌，意识毫不费力地释放出来，扩展到那永恒存在的辉煌之中。现在，给这种体验起个名字——开悟。

# ↩

13
13
far, far beyond
远远超出

Ultimately, the word “beyond” captures the true meaning of spirituality. In its most basic sense, going beyond means going past where you are. It means not staying in your current state. When you constantly go beyond yourself, there are no more limitations. There are no more boundaries. Limitations and boundaries only exist at the places where you stop going beyond. If you never stop, then you go beyond boundaries, beyond limitations, beyond the sense of a restricted self.

归根结底，“超越”一词捕捉到了灵性的真谛。从最基本的意义上讲，超越意味着超越你当下的状态，意味着不停留在当前的境地。当你不断超越自我时，便不再有任何限制，不再有任何界限。限制和界限只存在于你停止超越的地方。如果你永不停歇，你就能超越界限，超越限制，超越被束缚的自我意识。

Beyond is infinite in all directions. If you take a laser beam and aim it in any direction, it will go on for infinity. It would only cease to be infinite if you created an artificial boundary that it could not penetrate. Boundaries create the appearance of finiteness in infinite space. Things seem finite because your perception hits mental boundaries. In truth, everything is infinite. It is you who takes that which goes on forever and talks about a mile from here. What is a mile from here? It’s nothing but a piece of infinity. There are no limits. There is just the infinite universe.

超越一切皆是无限。如果你用激光束指向任何方向，它都会无限延伸。只有当你人为地设置一个它无法穿透的边界时，它才会停止无限延伸。边界的存在使无限的空间呈现出有限的假象。事物之所以看起来有限，是因为你的感知触及了思维的边界。事实上，一切都是无限的。是你把这永恒的事物拿来谈论“离这里一英里”。“离这里一英里”又是什么呢？它不过是无限的一部分。没有极限。存在的只有无限的宇宙。

To go beyond, you must keep going past the limits that you put on things. This requires changes at the core of your being. Right now you are using your analytical mind to break the world up into individual thought objects. You are then using the same mind to put these discrete thoughts together in a defined relationship to each other. You do this in an attempt to feel a semblance of control. This is seen most clearly in your constant attempt to make the unknown known. You say to yourself, “It wouldn’t dare rain tomorrow, it’s my day off. And since Jennifer loves being outdoors, she will certainly want to go hiking with me. In fact, if I want an extra day off, Tom won’t mind covering for me. After all, I covered for him once.” You have it all figured out. You know how everything is supposed to be, even the future. Your views, your opinions, your preferences, your concepts, your goals, and your beliefs are all ways of bringing the infinite universe down to the finite where you can feel a sense of control. Since the analytical mind cannot handle the infinite, you created an alternate reality of finite thoughts that can remain fixed within your mind. You have taken the whole, broken it into pieces, and selected a handful of these pieces to be put together in a certain way within your mind. This mental model has become your reality. You must now struggle day and night to make the world fit your model, and you label everything that doesn’t fit as wrong, bad, or unfair.

要想超越，你必须不断突破自己设定的界限。这需要你内在本质的改变。此刻，你正运用分析思维将世界分解成一个个独立的思维对象。然后，你又用同样的思维将这些分散的思维组合成一个彼此明确关联的关系。你这样做是为了寻求某种程度的掌控感。这一点在你不断尝试将未知转化为已知时体现得最为明显。你对自己说：“明天肯定不会下雨，因为我休息。而且詹妮弗喜欢户外活动，她肯定会想和我一起去徒步旅行。事实上，如果我想多休息一天，汤姆不会介意替我顶班。毕竟，我以前也替他顶班过。” 你觉得自己已经把一切都安排妥当了。你知道一切应该如何发展，甚至包括未来。你的观点、意见、偏好、概念、目标和信念，都是将无限的宇宙拉回到有限世界，让你从中获得掌控感的方式。由于分析性思维无法处理无限，你便创造了一个由有限思维构成的平行世界，并将其固化在你的脑海中。你将整体分解成碎片，然后从中挑选出一些碎片，按照某种特定的方式在你的脑海中拼凑起来。这种思维模式就此成为你的现实。你现在必须日夜苦苦挣扎，才能让世界符合你的模式，而所有不符合的事物都被你贴上错误、糟糕或不公平的标签。

If anything happens that challenges how you view things, you fight. You defend. You rationalize. You get frustrated and angry over simple little things. This is the result of being unable to fit what’s actually happening into your model of reality. If you want to go beyond your model, you have to take the risk of not believing in it. If your mental model is bothering you, it’s because it doesn’t incorporate reality. Your choice is to either resist reality or go beyond the limits of your model.

如果发生任何挑战你固有认知的事情，你就会反抗、辩解、找借口。你会因为一些小事而感到沮丧和愤怒。这是因为你无法将现实融入你原有的认知模型。如果你想超越这个模型，就必须承担不相信它的风险。如果你的思维模型让你感到困扰，那是因为它无法涵盖现实。你的选择要么是抗拒现实，要么是超越你现有模型的局限。

In order to truly go beyond your model, you must first understand why you built it. The easiest way to understand this is to study what happens when the model doesn’t work. Have you ever built your whole world on a model of life predicated upon another person’s behavior or the permanence of a relationship? If so, have you ever had that foundation pulled out from under you? Somebody leaves you. Somebody dies. Something goes wrong. Something shakes your model to the core. When this happens, your entire view of who you believe you are, including your relationship to everyone and everything around you, begins to fall apart. You panic and do everything you can to hold it together. You beg, fight, and struggle to try to keep your world from collapsing.

要想真正超越你现有的模式，首先必须理解你构建这个模式的初衷。最简单的理解方式就是研究当这个模式失效时会发生什么。你是否曾经将整个世界建立在基于他人行为或一段关系的稳定性之上？如果是，你是否经历过这种根基崩塌的打击？有人离开你，有人离世，事情出了差错，某种力量彻底动摇了你的模式。当这种情况发生时，你对自我的认知，包括你与周围所有人、所有事物的关系，都会开始瓦解。你会惊慌失措，竭尽全力去维系这一切。你会苦苦哀求、挣扎抗争，试图阻止你的世界崩塌。

Once you’ve had an experience like that, and most people have, you realize that the model you’ve built is tenuous, at best. The entire thing can fall apart. The whole model and all that it’s built upon, including your entire view of yourself and everything else, can start to crumble. What you experience when this happens is one of the most important learning experiences of your life. You come face-to-face with what made you build the model. The level of discomfort and disorientation you experience is frightening. You struggle just to get back some semblance of normal perception. What you are really doing is trying to pull the mental model back around you so that you can settle down into your familiar mental setting.

一旦你经历过类似的事情（大多数人都有过），你就会意识到，你构建的模型充其量也只是脆弱不堪。整个模型随时可能崩塌。它所建立的一切，包括你对自身和一切事物的看法，都可能开始瓦解。当这种情况发生时，你所经历的将是你人生中最重要的一次学习经历。你将直面是什么让你构建了这个模型。你所感受到的不适和迷茫程度令人恐惧。你挣扎着想要恢复一丝正常的感知。你实际上是在试图将你的心理模型重新拉回到你身边，以便你能重新适应你熟悉的心理环境。

But our whole world doesn’t have to fall apart in order for us to see what we’re doing in there. We are constantly trying to hold it all together. If you really want to see why you do things, then don’t do them and see what happens. Let’s say you’re a smoker. If you decide to stop smoking, you quickly confront the urges that cause you to smoke. These urges are the reason you smoke. They are the outermost layer of cause. If you can sit through these urges, you will see what caused them. If you can get comfortable with what you see, you will face the next layer of causation, and so on, layer upon layer. Likewise, there’s a reason you overeat. There’s a reason why you dress the way you do. There’s a reason for everything you do. If you want to see why you care so much about what you wear and what your hair is like, then just don’t do it one day. Wake up in the morning and go somewhere disheveled with your hair a mess, and see what happens to the energies inside of you. See what happens to you when you don’t do the things that make you comfortable. What you’ll see is why you’re doing them.

但我们不必等到整个世界分崩离析才能看清自己的所作所为。我们一直在努力维系一切。如果你真的想弄明白自己为什么会做某些事，那就先别做，看看会发生什么。假设你是个烟民。如果你决定戒烟，很快就会直面那些驱使你吸烟的冲动。这些冲动就是你吸烟的原因，是最外层的因果关系。如果你能坦然面对这些冲动，就会明白它们的根源。如果你能坦然接受你所看到的，你就会面对下一层因果关系，以此类推，一层又一层。同样，你暴饮暴食是有原因的，你那样穿衣打扮也是有原因的，你做的每件事都有其原因。如果你想知道为什么你如此在意自己的穿着打扮和发型，那就有一天别那样做。清晨醒来，蓬头垢面地去某个地方，看看你内心的能量会发生什么变化。看看当你不再做那些让你感到舒适的事情时，会发生什么。你会发现，你做这些事情的真正原因。

You are constantly trying to stay within your comfort zone. You struggle to keep people, places, and things in a manner that supports your model. If they start to go any other way, you get uncomfortable. Your mind then becomes active telling you how to get things back the way you need them to be. The moment somebody starts behaving in a way that is outside your expectations, your mind starts talking. It says, “What should I do about this? I can’t just ignore what he did. I could confront him directly or ask someone else to talk to him.” Your mind is telling you to fix it. And it doesn’t really matter what you end up doing; it’s all about getting back within your comfort zone. This zone is finite. All attempts to stay within it keep you finite. Going beyond always means letting go of the effort to keep things within your defined limits.

你总是试图待在舒适区。你努力让周围的人、事、物都符合你的预期。一旦它们偏离你的预期，你就会感到不自在。这时，你的大脑就会活跃起来，告诉你该如何让一切回到你期望的状态。一旦有人行为出乎你的意料，你的大脑就开始运转。它会说：“我该怎么办？我不能对他的行为视而不见。我可以当面质问他，或者让别人去跟他谈谈。”你的大脑在告诉你该如何解决问题。但你最终采取什么行动其实并不重要；关键在于回到你的舒适区。这个舒适区是有限的。所有试图待在舒适区的努力都只会让你更加局限。超越舒适区意味着放弃将事物限制在你设定的范围内的努力。

So there are two ways you can live: you can devote your life to staying in your comfort zone, or you can work on your freedom. In other words, you can devote your whole life to the process of making sure everything fits within your limited model, or you can devote your life to freeing yourself from the limits of your model.

所以，人生有两种选择：你可以终其一生待在舒适区，也可以努力追求自由。换句话说，你可以把一生都用来确保一切都符合你既定的模式，也可以把一生都用来挣脱这种模式的束缚。

To understand this better, let’s take a trip to the zoo. Imagine that you’re having a great time until you see a tiger inside a small cage. This causes you to contemplate what it would be like to live the rest of your life in such tight confinement. The very thought is extremely frightening to you. But in truth, the confines of your comfort zone create just such a cage. This inner cage doesn’t limit your body; it limits the expanse of your consciousness. Because you are unable to go outside your comfort zone, you are, in essence, locked in confinement.

为了更好地理解这一点，我们不妨去动物园看看。想象一下，你正玩得开心，直到你看到一只老虎被关在一个狭小的笼子里。这让你不禁思考，如果余生都要生活在如此狭小的空间里，会是什么感觉？光是想想就让你感到无比恐惧。但事实上，你的舒适区本身就构成了一个这样的牢笼。这个内在的牢笼并非限制你的身体，而是限制你意识的广度。因为你无法走出舒适区，所以从本质上讲，你被困在了牢笼之中。

If you examine this, you will see that you’re willing to stay in this cage because you’re afraid. Your comfort zone is familiar to you; beyond it is the unknown. To fully appreciate this, just imagine the most paranoid person you have ever met in your entire life. He’s so scared. Every moment of his life he thinks somebody’s trying to hurt him. If you offer him that tiger’s cage, he might accept your offer. He doesn’t see it as being locked in a cage. He sees it as protection from what could harm him. That which looks like prison to you, looks like safety to him. What if a security service came to your house and bolted down all the doors and barred all the windows? If you happened to be inside at the time, would you panic and want to get out, or would you thank them for helping you feel safe?

如果你仔细想想，就会发现你之所以愿意待在这个笼子里，是因为你害怕。你的舒适区对你来说是熟悉的；而舒适区之外则是未知。为了更深刻地理解这一点，不妨想象一下你这辈子见过的最偏执的人。他非常害怕。他时刻都觉得有人想要伤害他。如果你给他一个老虎笼子，他或许会接受。他并不觉得那是被关在笼子里。他觉得那是保护他免受伤害的屏障。在你看来如同监狱的地方，在他看来却是安全港湾。试想一下，如果保安人员来到你家，把所有的门窗都锁上了，你会作何感想？如果你当时正好在家，你会惊慌失措地想要逃出去，还是会感谢他们让你感到安全？

Most people have the second reaction when it comes to the limitations of their psyche. They want to stay in there and feel safe. They don’t say, “Get me out of here! I’m locked in this tiny world in which everything has to be a certain way. I have to worry about what everybody’s doing, what I look like, and everything I’ve ever said. I want out.” Instead of wanting out, they try to keep their cage stable. If something is not comfortable, they do whatever they must to protect themselves and get back to a feeling of safety. If you’ve ever done that, it means you love your cage. When the cage of the psyche got rattled, you fixed it so that you could be comfortable inside.

大多数人面对心理局限时，都会有第二种反应。他们想要待在里面，寻求安全感。他们不会说：“放我出去！我被困在这个狭小的世界里，一切都必须按部就班。我必须担心每个人的所作所为，担心自己的外表，担心自己说过的话。我想出去。” 他们不会想要逃离，而是努力维持牢笼的稳定。如果有什么不舒服的地方，他们会不惜一切代价保护自己，重新获得安全感。如果你也曾这样做过，那就意味着你热爱你的牢笼。当心理牢笼受到震动时，你会把它修好，让自己在里面感到舒适。

When you truly awake spiritually, you realize you are caged. You wake up and realize that you can hardly move in there. You’re constantly hitting the limits of your comfort zone. You see that you’re afraid to tell people what you really think. You see that you’re too self-conscious to freely express yourself. You see that you have to stay on top of everything in order to be okay.

当你真正觉醒，获得精神上的觉醒时，你会意识到自己被囚禁了。你醒来后发现自己几乎寸步难行。你不断地挑战着舒适区的极限。你会发现自己害怕向别人表达真实想法。你会发现自己太过在意他人的眼光，以至于无法自由地表达自我。你会发现自己必须时刻掌控一切，才能安心。

Why? There’s really no reason. You have set these limits on yourself. If you don’t stay within them, you get scared, you feel hurt, and you feel threatened. That’s your cage. The tiger knows the limits of his cage when he hits the bars. You know the limits of your cage when the psyche starts to resist. Your bars are the outer boundary of your comfort zone. The minute you come to the edge of your cage, it lets you know it in no uncertain terms.

为什么？其实没什么理由。这些限制是你自己设定的。如果你不遵守这些限制，你就会感到害怕、受伤和受到威胁。这就是你的牢笼。老虎撞到笼子的栏杆时，就知道自己的极限在哪里。当你的心理开始抗拒时，你也知道自己牢笼的极限在哪里。你的笼子就是你舒适区的边界。一旦你走到牢笼边缘，它就会毫不含糊地让你明白。

Let’s look at this edge by way of an example. In the old days, if you wanted to keep your dog in the backyard, you had to put up a fence. Nowadays you don’t need a fence because everything is electronic. You just bury wires underground and put a little collar on the dog. The dog thinks, “Hey, I’m free! I used to have to be inside a fence. This is great!” Of course he goes running right to where he’s not supposed to go, and—zap!—he jumps back and barks. What happened? An invisible limit was there, and when the dog approached that limit, it gave him a little shock. It hurt. It was uncomfortable enough so that now the dog feels fear whenever he approaches the boundaries. So you see, a cage doesn’t have to look like a cage. It can be a cage created by your fear of discomfort. If you approach your limits, you begin to feel uncomfortable and insecure. Those are the bars of your cage. As long as you stay inside of it, you cannot possibly know what is on the other side. The boundaries of this cage are what make your world appear finite and temporal. The infinite and eternal are just outside the limits of your cage.

我们举个例子来说明这个界限。以前，如果你想把狗关在后院，就得建个围栏。现在不用围栏了，因为一切都电子化了。你只需要把电线埋在地下，再给狗戴个小项圈。狗会想：“嘿，我自由了！以前我得被关在围栏里。这太棒了！” 当然，它会径直跑到不该去的地方，然后——啪！——它就跳回来吠叫。发生了什么？那里有一条看不见的界限，当狗接近这条界限时，它会受到轻微的电击。这很疼。这种不适感足以让狗在接近边界时感到恐惧。所以你看，笼子不一定非得看起来像笼子。它可以是你对不适感的恐惧所创造的笼子。当你接近你的界限时，你就会开始感到不舒服和不安全。这些就是你笼子的栏杆。只要你待在里面，你就永远不可能知道另一边是什么。正是这牢笼的边界，使你的世界显得有限而短暂。无限和永恒，就在牢笼之外。

Going beyond means going beyond the borders of the cage. There should be no cage. The soul is infinite. It is free to expand everywhere. It is free to experience all of life. This can only happen when you are willing to face reality without mental boundaries. If you still have barriers, and you know what they are because you hit them every day, you must be willing to go beyond them. Otherwise you remain within your cage. And remember, decorating your cage with beautiful experiences, fond memories, and great dreams is not the same as going beyond. A cage by any other name is still a cage. You must be willing to go beyond.

超越意味着超越牢笼的边界。本不该有牢笼。灵魂是无限的，它自由地向四面八方扩展，自由地体验人生百态。只有当你愿意抛开一切心理障碍直面现实时，这一切才能实现。如果你心中仍有障碍，并且因为每天都在与它们对抗而清楚地知道它们是什么，那么你必须愿意超越它们。否则，你仍将困于牢笼之中。记住，用美好的经历、温馨的回忆和远大的梦想来装饰你的牢笼，并不等同于超越。无论牢笼换了什么名字，它仍然是牢笼。你必须愿意超越它。

Throughout each day, you frequently hit the edges of your cage. When you hit these edges, you either pull back or try to force things to change so that you can remain comfortable. You actually use the brilliance of your mind to stay inside your cage. Day and night you plot and plan how to stay within your comfort zone. Sometimes you can’t even fall asleep at night because you’re too busy thinking about what you need to do to stay within your cage: “How can I make it so that she will never leave me? How can I keep her from ever becoming interested in someone else?” You’re trying to figure out how to be sure that you won’t hit the edges of your cage.

每天，你都会频繁地触碰到笼子的边缘。每当触碰到边缘，你要么会退缩，要么会试图强迫自己改变现状，以求继续待在舒适区。你甚至运用自己聪明的头脑来让自己留在笼子里。你日夜盘算着如何才能待在舒适区。有时，你甚至无法入睡，因为你一直在思考如何才能留在笼子里：“怎样才能让她永远不离开我？怎样才能让她永远不爱上别人？” 你努力想办法确保自己不会触碰到笼子的边缘。

Let’s go back to the dog. Since that particular dog was used to roaming free, it’s a sad day when he stops trying to get out of the yard. The only reason he would stop trying to go beyond his little space is that he’s afraid of the edges. But what if we’re dealing with a very brave dog that’s determined to be free? Imagine that the dog has not given up. You find him sitting there, right at the place where the collar starts vibrating, and he is not backing off. Every minute he’s stepping forward a little bit more in order to get used to the force field. If he continues, he will eventually get out. There’s not a chance in the world that he won’t. Since it’s just an artificial edge, he can get through if he can learn to withstand the discomfort. He just has to be ready, willing, and able to handle the discomfort. The collar cannot actually hurt him; it’s just uncomfortable. If he is willing to go beyond his comfort zone, he is free to come and go at will.

让我们回到那只狗身上。这只狗习惯了自由自在地漫游，所以当它不再尝试离开院子时，我们感到很遗憾。它之所以不再尝试离开自己的小天地，唯一的原因是它害怕边界。但如果我们面对的是一只非常勇敢、决心要获得自由的狗呢？想象一下，这只狗没有放弃。你发现它坐在那里，就在项圈开始震动的地方，它没有后退。它每分钟都向前迈出一小步，试图适应这个力场。如果它坚持下去，最终一定能出去。它绝对不可能失败。因为这只是人为设置的边界，只要它能学会忍受这种不适，就能穿过去。它只需要做好准备，愿意并且能够承受这种不适。项圈实际上不会伤害它，只是让它感到不舒服而已。如果它愿意走出舒适区，它就能自由自在地来去。

Your cage is just like this. When you approach the edges you feel insecurity, jealousy, fear, or self-consciousness. You pull back, and if you are like most people, you stop trying. Spirituality begins when you decide that you’ll never stop trying. Spirituality is the commitment to go beyond, no matter what it takes. It’s an infinite journey based upon going beyond yourself every minute of every day for the rest of your life. If you’re truly going beyond, you are always at your limits. You’re never back in the comfort zone. A spiritual being feels as though they are always against that edge, and they are constantly being pushed through it.

你的牢笼就像这样。当你接近边缘时，你会感到不安、嫉妒、恐惧或自我意识过强。你会退缩，如果你和大多数人一样，就会放弃尝试。而当你决定永不放弃时，灵性便开始了。灵性是一种超越自我的承诺，无论付出什么代价。这是一段无限的旅程，意味着在余生的每一分每一秒都超越自我。如果你真的在超越自我，你就会永远处于极限。你永远不会回到舒适区。一个有灵性的人会感觉自己始终在挑战极限，并且不断地被推着向前。

Eventually you will realize that it cannot actually hurt you to go beyond your psychological limits. If you are willing to just stand at the edge and keep walking, you will go beyond. You used to pull back when it got uncomfortable. Now you relax and go past that point. That is all it takes to go beyond. Go beyond where you were a minute ago by handling what’s happening now.

最终你会明白，超越心理极限其实并不会伤害你。只要你愿意站在边缘，继续前行，你就能超越极限。过去，一旦感到不适，你就会退缩。现在，你放松下来，跨越那个界限。这就是超越极限的全部秘诀。通过应对当下发生的一切，超越你一分钟前的自己。

Would you like to go beyond? Would you like to feel no edges? Imagine a comfort zone that is so expanded that it can easily fit the entire day, no matter what happens. The day unfolds and the mind doesn’t say anything. You simply interact with the day with a peaceful, fully inspired heart. If your edges happen to get hit, the mind doesn’t complain. It all just passes through. This is how great beings live. When you are trained, like a great athlete, to immediately relax through your edges when they get hit, then it’s all over. You realize that you will always be fine. Nothing can ever bother you except your edges, and now you know what to do with them. You end up loving your edges because they point your way to freedom. All you have to do is constantly relax and lean into them. Then one day, when you least expect it, you fall through into the infinite. That is what it means to go beyond.

你想超越自我吗？你想感受不到任何界限吗？想象一下，一个舒适区如此广阔，足以轻松容纳一整天，无论发生什么。一天就这样展开，你的头脑不会发出任何声音。你只是用一颗平和、充满灵感的心去体验这一天。即使你的界限偶尔受到冲击，你的头脑也不会抱怨。一切都会自然而然地过去。这就是伟大生命的方式。当你像伟大的运动员一样，被训练成在遇到挑战时能够立即放松下来，那么一切都会迎刃而解。你会意识到，你永远都会安然无恙。除了你的界限之外，没有什么能够困扰你，而现在你知道该如何应对它们了。你最终会爱上你的界限，因为它们指引你走向自由。你所要做的就是不断放松，顺应它们。然后有一天，在你最意想不到的时候，你会坠入无限之中。这就是超越自我的意义。

14
14
letting go of false solidity
放下虚假的坚实性

The inside of one’s psyche is a very complex, sophisticated place. It is full of conflicting forces that are constantly changing due to both internal and external stimuli. This results in wide variations of needs, fears, and desires over relatively short periods of time. Because of this, very few people have the clarity to understand what’s going on in there. There’s just too much happening at once to follow the cause and effect relationships between all of our different thoughts, emotions, and energy levels. As a result, we find ourselves struggling just to hold it all together. But everything keeps on changing—moods, desires, likes, dislikes, enthusiasm, lethargy. It’s a full-time task just to maintain the discipline necessary to create even the semblance of control and order in there.

人的内心世界极其复杂精妙。它充满了各种相互冲突的力量，这些力量因内外刺激而不断变化。这导致人们的需求、恐惧和欲望在相对较短的时间内发生巨大变化。正因如此，很少有人能够清晰地理解内心世界正在发生的一切。同时发生的事情太多，以至于我们根本无法追踪所有不同想法、情绪和能量水平之间的因果关系。结果，我们发现自己疲于奔命，仅仅是为了维持内心的平衡。但一切都在不断变化——情绪、欲望、喜好、厌恶、热情、倦怠。仅仅为了维持内心世界里哪怕是表面上的控制和秩序，就需要耗费大量的精力。

When you’re lost and struggling with all these psychological and energetic changes, you are suffering. While it may not seem to you that you’re suffering, compared to what it can be, you are suffering. In truth, the very responsibility of having to hold it all together is itself a form of suffering. You notice this most when things start to fall apart outside. Your psyche goes into turmoil, and you have to struggle to hold your inner world together. But what exactly are you trying to hold onto? The only things in there are your thoughts, emotions, and movements of energy, none of which are solid. They are like clouds, simply coming and going through vast inner space. But you keep holding onto them, as though consistency can substitute for stability. The Buddhists have a term for this: “clinging.” In the end, clinging is what the psyche is all about.

当你迷失方向，挣扎于各种心理和能量的变化时，你正在承受痛苦。或许你感觉不到痛苦，但与痛苦的程度相比，你的确在承受。事实上，要努力维系这一切本身就是一种痛苦。当外部世界开始崩塌时，你会最明显地感受到这一点。你的内心陷入混乱，你不得不挣扎着维系你的内在世界。但你究竟在试图抓住什么呢？那里只有你的思想、情绪和能量流动，而这些都不是实体。它们就像云朵，在广阔的内在空间中来来去去。但你却执着地抓住它们，仿佛执着就能取代稳定。佛教对此有一个词：“执着”。归根结底，执着才是心灵的本质。

In order to understand clinging, we must first understand who clings. As you go deeper into yourself, you will naturally come to realize that there is an aspect of your being that is always there and never changes. This is your sense of awareness, your consciousness. It is this awareness that is aware of your thoughts, experiences the ebb and flow of your emotions, and receives your physical senses. This is the root of Self. You are not your thoughts; you are aware of your thoughts. You are not your emotions; you feel your emotions. You are not your body; you look at it in the mirror and experience this world through its eyes and ears. You are the conscious being who is aware that you are aware of all these inner and outer things.

为了理解执着，我们首先必须理解执着者是谁。当你深入探索自我时，自然会意识到你存在着一个始终存在且永不改变的面向。这就是你的觉知，你的意识。正是这种觉知觉察着你的念头，体验着你情绪的起伏，并接收着你的感官体验。这就是自我的根源。你不是你的念头；你觉察着你的念头。你不是你的情绪；你感受着你的情绪。你不是你的身体；你透过镜子观察它，并通过它的眼睛和耳朵体验这个世界。你是觉知着自己觉察着所有这些内在和外在事物的意识存在。

If you explore consciousness, which is your pure sense of awareness, you will see that it really does not exist at any particular point in space. Rather, it is a field of awareness that focuses down to a point by concentrating on a particular set of objects. You can be aware of feeling just one finger, or you can be aware of feeling your entire body at once. You can be totally lost in a single thought, or you can be simultaneously aware of your thoughts, your emotions, your body, and your surroundings. Consciousness is a dynamic field of awareness that has the ability to either narrowly focus or broadly expand. When consciousness concentrates narrowly enough, it loses its broader sense of self. It no longer experiences itself as a field of pure consciousness; it begins to relate itself more to the objects it’s focused upon. As we have seen, this is what happens when you get so absorbed in a movie that you completely lose the broader sense of sitting in a cold, dark theater. In this case, you have shifted from concentrating on your body and its surroundings to concentrating on the world of the movie. You literally get lost in the experience. This can be generalized to your entire experience of life. Your sense of self is determined by where you are focusing your consciousness.

如果你探索意识，也就是你纯粹的觉知，你会发现它实际上并不存在于空间中的任何特定点。相反，它是一个觉知的场域，通过专注于一组特定的对象而聚焦于一点。你可以觉知到只感觉到一根手指，也可以同时觉知到全身的感觉。你可以完全沉浸在一个念头中，也可以同时觉知到你的念头、情绪、身体和周围环境。意识是一个动态的觉知场域，它既可以聚焦于狭窄的领域，也可以扩展至广阔的领域。当意识聚焦得足够狭窄时，它就会失去更广阔的自我意识。它不再体验到自身作为纯粹意识场域的存在；它开始更多地与它所关注的对象联系起来。正如我们所看到的，当你完全沉浸于一部电影中，以至于完全忘记了自己身处一个寒冷黑暗的影院时，就会发生这种情况。在这种情况下，你已经从专注于你的身体及其周围环境，转移到了专注于电影的世界。你真的迷失在了电影体验之中。这可以推广到你人生的方方面面。你的自我意识取决于你将注意力集中在哪里。

But what determines where you focus your consciousness? At the most basic level, it is simply determined by anything that catches your awareness because it stands out from the rest. To understand this, imagine that your consciousness is simply observing vast, empty inner space. Now imagine that passing through this space is the gentle flow of random thought objects: a cat, a horse, a word, a color, or an abstract thought. They are sporadically floating right through your awareness. Now let one object stand out above the rest. It catches your attention and draws the focus of your awareness. You immediately realize that the more focused you become on the object, the slower it moves. Until, eventually, if you focus on it enough, it stops. The force of consciousness ends up holding the object stable simply by concentrating on it. Just as a fish can pass through water but not through ice, which is simply concentrated water, so mental and emotional energy patterns become fixed when they encounter concentrated consciousness. The very act of differentiating the amount of awareness focused on one particular object over any other creates clinging. And the result of clinging is that selective thoughts and emotions stay in one place long enough to become the building blocks of the psyche.

但究竟是什么决定了你的意识集中在哪里呢？最基本的层面来说，它仅仅取决于任何能够吸引你注意力的事物，因为它与其他事物截然不同。为了理解这一点，不妨想象你的意识正在观察一片广袤无垠的空旷内在空间。现在想象一下，一些随机的念头如同轻柔的流水般穿过这片空间：一只猫、一匹马、一个词、一种颜色，或者一个抽象的想法。它们零星地漂浮在你的意识之中。现在，让其中一个念头脱颖而出。它吸引了你的注意力，并将你的意识焦点集中于此。你会立刻意识到，你越专注于这个念头，它移动的速度就越慢。直到最后，如果你足够专注，它就会停止移动。意识的力量最终会通过专注于它而使这个念头保持稳定。正如鱼可以穿过水却无法穿过冰（冰只是浓缩的水），当精神和情绪能量模式遇到专注的意识时，它们也会变得固定下来。正是这种将注意力集中在某个特定对象而非其他对象的行为，产生了执着。而执着的结果是，某些特定的想法和情绪会在某个地方停留足够长的时间，从而成为构成心理的基石。

Clinging is one of the most primal acts. Because some objects remain in the consciousness while others pass through, your sense of awareness relates more to them. You use them as fixed points to create a sense of orientation, relationship, and security in the midst of constant inner change. And this need for orientation extends to the outside world. Although you are clinging to inner objects, you use them to orient and relate yourself to the multitude of physical objects that come in through your senses. You then create thoughts that tie all the objects together, and you cling to the entire structure. You actually end up relating so strongly to this inner structure that you build your entire sense of self around it. Because you cling to it, it stays fixed. And because it stays fixed, you relate to it above all else. This is the birth of the psyche. In the midst of the expanse of empty mind, by clinging to passing thought objects, you make an island of apparent solidity. Once you have a thought that stays, you can rest your head on it. Then, as you cling to more and more thoughts, you build an inner structure for consciousness to focus on. The more consciousness narrows its focus onto this mental structure, the greater the tendency to utilize it to define the concept of self. Clinging creates the bricks and mortar with which we build a conceptual self. In the midst of vast inner space, using nothing but the vapor of thoughts, you created a structure of apparent solidity to rest upon.

执着是最原始的行为之一。因为有些事物会留在意识中，而另一些则会转瞬即逝，所以你的意识与它们的关系更为密切。你将它们作为固定点，在不断变化的内心世界中建立方向感、联系感和安全感。这种对方向的需求也延伸到了外部世界。尽管你执着于内在的事物，但你却利用它们来定位自己，并将自己与通过感官进入的众多物质对象联系起来。然后，你创造出将所有这些事物联系起来的念头，并执着于整个结构。实际上，你最终与这个内在结构建立了如此强烈的联系，以至于你围绕它构建了整个自我意识。因为你执着于它，它便保持稳定。正因为它保持稳定，你才将它置于一切之上。这就是心灵的诞生。在空虚的心灵深处，通过执着于转瞬即逝的念头，你创造了一个看似坚实的孤岛。一旦你拥有一个停留的念头，你便可以安心地依靠它。然后，随着你执着于越来越多的念头，你便构建起一个内在的结构，让意识聚焦于此。意识越是将注意力集中于这个心理结构，就越倾向于用它来定义自我概念。执着如同砖瓦，为我们构建概念性的自我提供了基础。在浩瀚的内在空间中，你仅凭念头的虚幻之光，便创造出一个看似坚实的结构，以此为依托。

Who are you that is lost and trying to build a concept of yourself in order to be found? This question represents the essence of spirituality. You will never find yourself in what you have built to define yourself. You’re the one who’s doing the building. You may assemble the most amazing collection of thoughts and emotions; you may build a truly beautiful, unbelievable, interesting, and dynamic structure; but, obviously, it’s not you. You are the one who did this. You are the one who was lost, scared, and confused because you focused your awareness away from your awareness of Self. In this panic, in this lost state, you learned to cling and hold onto the thoughts and emotions that were passing before you. You used them to build a personality, a persona, a self-concept that would allow you to define yourself. Awareness rested itself on the objects it was aware of and called it home. Because you have this model of who you are, it is easier to know how to act, how to make decisions, and how to relate to the outside world. If you dare to look, you will see that you live your entire life based on the model you built around yourself.

你是谁？你为何迷失方向，试图构建一个自我概念以求被找到？这个问题揭示了灵性的本质。你永远无法在你用来定义自己的事物中找到真正的自己。是你自己在构建这一切。你或许能汇集最奇妙的思想和情感；你或许能构建一个真正美丽、不可思议、引人入胜且充满活力的结构；但显然，那并非真正的你。是你创造了这一切。你之所以迷失、恐惧、困惑，是因为你将注意力从对自我的觉察中转移开来。在这种恐慌和迷失的状态下，你学会了紧紧抓住眼前转瞬即逝的思想和情感。你用它们构建了一个人格、一个形象、一个自我概念，以此来定义自己。你的意识依附于它所感知的对象，并称之为家。正因为你拥有了这样一个自我模型，你才更容易知道如何行动、如何做决定以及如何与外界相处。如果你敢于正视，你会发现你的一生都是按照你自己构建的模式来度过的。

Let’s get more specific. You try to hold a consistent set of thoughts and concepts in your mind, such as “I am a woman.” Yes, even that is a thought, or a concept held in your mind. You, who are holding onto that, are neither male nor female. You are the awareness who hears the thought and sees a woman’s body in the mirror. But you cling tightly to these concepts. You think, “I am a woman, I am of a certain age and I believe in one philosophy versus another.” You literally define yourself based on what you believe: “I believe in God or I don’t believe in God. I believe in peace and nonviolence, or I believe in survival of the fittest. I believe in capitalism, or I believe in neo-socialism.” You take a set of thoughts in the mind and you hold onto them. You make a highly complex relational structure out of them, and then present that package as who you are. But it is not who you are. It is just the thoughts you have pulled around yourself in an attempt to define yourself. You do this because you are lost inside.

让我们更具体地谈谈。你试图在脑海中保持一套固定的想法和概念，比如“我是一个女人”。是的，即使是“我是一个女人”也是一种想法，或者说是一个存在于你脑海中的概念。你，这个执着于此的人，既非男性也非女性。你是那个听到这个想法，并在镜子中看到女性身体的意识。但你却紧紧抓住这些概念不放。你认为，“我是一个女人，我到了某个年龄，我信奉某种哲学，而不是另一种。”你实际上是根据你的信仰来定义自己：“我信上帝，或者我不信上帝。我信奉和平与非暴力，或者我信奉适者生存。我信奉资本主义，或者我信奉新社会主义。”你把一系列想法放在脑海中，并紧紧抓住它们。你用它们构建了一个极其复杂的关系结构，然后将这个结构包装成“你”。但这并非真正的你。这只是你为了定义自己而围绕着自己的一系列想法。你这样做是因为你内心迷失了方向。

Basically, you attempt to create a sense of stability and steadiness inside. This generates a false, but welcomed, sense of security. You also want the people around you to have done the same thing. You want people to be steady enough so that you can predict their behavior. If they aren’t, it disturbs you. This is because you have made your predictions of their behavior part of your inner model. This protective shield of beliefs and concepts regarding the outside world acts as insulation between you and the people you interact with. By having preconceived notions about other people’s behavior, you feel safer and more in control. Imagine the fear you would feel if you let the entire wall down. Who have you ever allowed directly into your true inner self without the protection of your mental buffer? Nobody, not even yourself.

基本上，你试图在内心营造一种稳定感和安稳感。这会产生一种虚假但令人欣喜的安全感。你也希望周围的人都能做到这一点。你希望人们足够稳定，以便你能预测他们的行为。如果他们做不到这一点，你就会感到不安。这是因为你已经将对他们行为的预测融入了你的内在模型。这层关于外部世界的信念和概念构成的保护罩，就像一层屏障，将你与你互动的人隔离开来。通过对他人行为的先入为主的观念，你会感到更安全、更能掌控局面。想象一下，如果你放下这层保护，你会感到多么恐惧。你曾经允许谁在没有心理屏障保护的情况下直接进入你真实的内心世界？没有人，甚至包括你自己。

People just put façades out there. They even admit that one façade is a little more real than the other. You go to work and get lost in your professional façade, but then you say, “I’m going home to be with my family and friends where I can just be myself.” So your work façade drops into the background, and your relaxed social façade comes forward. But what about you, the one who is holding the façade together? Nobody gets near that one. That’s just too scary. That one is too far back there to deal with.

人们总是戴着面具示人。他们甚至承认，其中一个面具比另一个更真实一些。你上班时沉浸在职业面具中，但随后你会说：“我要回家和家人朋友在一起，在那里我可以做回真正的自己。”于是，你的工作面具退居幕后，轻松自在的社交面具浮现出来。但是，那个支撑着整个面具的你呢？没人敢靠近。那太可怕了。那太遥远，难以面对。

So we are all clinging and then building. Some of us are better at this than others. In most societies you are well rewarded for how good you are at clinging and building. If you get that model down absolutely right, and behave consistently every time, you have actually “created” someone. And if the someone you create is what others want and need, you can be very popular and successful. You are that person. It got engrained in you at a very young age, and you never deviated from it. You can get really good at this game of creating someone. And if the person you created is not receiving the popularity and success you expected, you can adjust your thoughts accordingly. It’s not that there is anything wrong with this. Obviously, everybody does it. But who are you that’s doing this, and why are you doing it?

所以我们都在先依附，然后建立。有些人比其他人更擅长这个。在大多数社会里，你越擅长依附和建立，就越能获得丰厚的回报。如果你能完美地掌握这个模式，并且每次都始终如一地这样做，你实际上就“创造”了一个人。如果你创造的这个人正是别人想要和需要的，你就能非常受欢迎，非常成功。你就是那个人。这种观念在你很小的时候就根深蒂固，你从未偏离过它。你可以非常擅长创造这个人。如果你创造的这个人没有获得你预期的受欢迎程度和成功，你可以相应地调整你的想法。这并不是说这样做有什么错。显然，每个人都在这样做。但是，你是谁？你为什么要这样做？

It’s important to realize that it’s not just up to you what thoughts you cling to and what person you create. Society has a lot to say about this. There are acceptable and unacceptable social behaviors for almost everything—how to sit, how to walk, how to speak, how to dress, and how to feel about things. How does our society engrain these mental and emotional structures within us? When you do it well, you are rewarded with hugs and showered with positive accolades. When you don’t do it well, you are punished, either physically, mentally, or emotionally.

重要的是要意识到，你坚持什么想法、塑造怎样的人，并非完全由你决定。社会对此影响深远。几乎所有方面都有可接受和不可接受的社会行为——如何坐、如何走、如何说话、如何穿衣，以及如何看待事物。我们的社会是如何将这些心理和情感结构根植于我们心中的呢？当你做得好时，你会得到拥抱和赞扬；当你做得不好时，你会受到惩罚，无论是身体上的、精神上的还是情感上的。

Just think about how nice you are to people when they behave in accordance with your expectations. Now think about how you close up and pull back from them when they don’t. This is not to mention getting angry or even violent toward them. What are you doing? You are trying to change someone’s behavior by leaving impressions on their mind. You are attempting to alter their collection of beliefs, thoughts, and emotions so that the next time they act it is in the manner you expect. In truth, we are all doing this to each other every day.

想想看，当别人的行为符合你的预期时，你会对他们多么友善。再想想，当他们的行为不符合你的预期时，你会如何封闭自己，疏远他们。更不用说你还会对他们发火，甚至诉诸暴力。你在做什么？你试图通过在别人心中留下印象来改变他们的行为。你试图改变他们的信念、想法和情绪，以便他们下次的行为符合你的预期。事实上，我们每天都在这样做。

Why do we let this happen to us? Why do we care so much whether other people accept the façade we put out there? It all comes down to understanding why we are clinging to our self-concept. If you stop clinging, you will see why the tendency to cling was there. If you let go of your façade, and don’t try to trade it in for a new one, your thoughts and emotions will become unanchored and begin passing through you. It will be a very scary experience. You will feel panic deep inside, and you will be unable to get your bearings. This is what people feel when something very important outside does not fit their inner model. The façade ceases to work and begins to crumble. When it can no longer protect you, you experience great fear and panic. However, you’ll find that if you’re willing to face that sense of panic, there is a way to go past it. You can go further back into the consciousness that is experiencing it, and the panic will stop. Then there will be a great peace, like nothing you’ve ever felt.

为什么我们会允许这种情况发生在自己身上？为什么我们如此在意别人是否接受我们展现出来的伪装？这一切都归结于理解我们为何如此执着于自我认知。如果你不再执着，你就会明白这种执着的倾向从何而来。如果你放下伪装，并且不试图用新的伪装取而代之，你的思想和情绪就会失去锚点，开始在你体内流淌。这将是一次非常可怕的体验。你会感到内心深处的恐慌，无法找到方向。当外界某些非常重要的事物与内心的认知不符时，人们就会有这种感觉。伪装不再奏效，开始崩塌。当它无法再保护你时，你会感到极度的恐惧和恐慌。然而，你会发现，如果你愿意直面这种恐慌感，就一定有办法超越它。你可以深入体验恐慌的意识层面，恐慌就会停止。然后，你会感受到前所未有的平静。

That’s the part very few people come to know: it can stop. The noise, the fear, the confusion, the constant changing of these inner energies—it can all stop. You thought you had to protect yourself, so you grabbed onto the things that were coming at you and used them to hide. You took what you could get your hands on, and you started to cling in order to build solidity. But you can let go of what you’re clinging to and not play this game. You just have to take the risk of letting it all go and daring to face the fear that was driving you. Then you can pass through that part of you, and it will all be over. It will stop—no more struggling, just peace.

很少有人真正了解这一点：一切都可以停止。喧嚣、恐惧、迷茫，以及内心能量的不断变化——这一切都可以停止。你以为必须保护自己，于是紧紧抓住那些向你袭来的东西，用它们来掩藏自己。你攫取一切可以触及之物，开始死死抓住，试图以此构建稳固的自我。但你可以放开你所执着的一切，不再玩弄这种游戏。你只需要冒险放手，勇敢地面对驱使你的恐惧。然后，你就能穿越你内心的那部分，一切都将结束。一切都会停止——不再挣扎，只有平静。

This journey is one of passing through exactly where you have been struggling not to go. As you pass through that state of turmoil, the consciousness itself is your only repose. You will just be aware that tremendous changes are taking place. You will be aware that there is no solidity and you will become comfortable with that. You will be aware that each moment of each day is unfolding and you neither have control, nor crave it. You have no concepts, no hopes, no dreams, no beliefs, and no security. You are no longer building mental models of what’s going on, but life is going on anyway. You are perfectly comfortable just being aware of it. Here comes this moment, then the next moment, and then the next. But that’s really what has always happened. Moment after moment has been passing before your consciousness. The difference is that now you see it happening. You see that your emotions and your mind are reacting to these moments that are coming through, and you’re doing nothing to stop it. You’re doing nothing to control it. You’re just letting life unfold, both outside and inside of you.

这段旅程，正是你一路穿越你一直竭力避免的地方。当你穿越那动荡不安的状态时，意识本身就是你唯一的安宁。你会意识到巨大的变化正在发生。你会意识到世间并无稳固，并会坦然接受这一点。你会意识到每一天的每一刻都在展开，你既无法掌控，也不渴望掌控。你没有概念，没有希望，没有梦想，没有信仰，也没有安全感。你不再构建关于正在发生的事情的心理模型，但生活依然在继续。你完全可以安心地觉察这一切。这一刻来了，下一刻来了，再下一刻来了。但这其实一直都在发生。一刻又一刻一直在你的意识中流逝。不同的是，现在你看到了这一切的发生。你看到你的情绪和你的思想正在对这些涌现的瞬间做出反应，而你没有试图阻止它。你没有试图控制它。你只是让生活展开，无论是在你的外在还是在你的内心。

If you take this journey, you will get to the state in which you see exactly how the unfolding moments bring up a sense of fear. From this place of clarity, you will be able to experience the powerful tendency to protect yourself. This tendency exists because you truly have no control, and that is not comfortable to you. But if you really want to break through, you have to be willing to just watch the fear without protecting yourself from it. You must be willing to see that this need to protect yourself is where the entire personality comes from. It was created by building a mental and emotional structure to get away from that sense of fear. You are now standing face-to-face with the root of the psyche.

如果你踏上这段旅程，你终将达到一种境界：你能清晰地看到，每一个瞬间是如何唤起恐惧感的。从这种清醒的状态出发，你将体验到强烈的自我保护倾向。这种倾向的存在，是因为你实际上无法掌控一切，而这种掌控感令你感到不适。但如果你真的想要突破，就必须愿意直面恐惧，而不去保护自己。你必须愿意看到，这种自我保护的需求正是你整个人格的根源。它源于构建一种心理和情感结构，以逃避恐惧感。现在，你正直面心灵的根源。

If you go deep enough, you can watch the psyche being built. You will see that you are in the middle of nowhere, in empty infinite space, and all of these inner objects are flowing toward you. Thoughts, feelings, and the impressions of worldly experiences are all pouring into your consciousness. You will clearly see that the tendency is to protect yourself from this flow by bringing it under your control. There is an overwhelmingly strong tendency to lean forward and grab onto selective impressions of people, places, and things as they flow through. You will see that if you focus on these mental images, they become part of a complex structure where there was none. You will see events that took place when you were ten years old that you’re still holding onto. You will see that you’re literally taking all your memories, pulling them together in an orderly fashion, and saying that’s who you are. But you are not the events; you’re the one who experienced the events. How can you define yourself as the things that happened to you? You were aware of your existence before they happened. You are the one who is in there doing all this, seeing all this, and experiencing all this. You do not have to cling to your experiences in the name of building yourself. This is a false self you are building inside. It is just a concept of yourself that you hide behind.

如果你深入探索，就能看到心灵的构建过程。你会发现自己身处虚无之中，置身于空旷无垠的空间，所有内在的事物都向你涌来。思想、情感以及世俗经验的印记都涌入你的意识。你会清楚地看到，人的本能是试图控制这股洪流，以此来保护自己。你会强烈地倾向于向前倾身，抓住那些涌入脑海的人、地点和事物的选择性印象。你会发现，如果你专注于这些心理图像，它们就会构成一个原本并不存在的复杂结构。你会看到十岁时发生的那些事，而你至今仍然执着于此。你会发现，你实际上是在收集所有的记忆，将它们有序地组合在一起，然后说这就是你。但你并非那些事件本身；你是经历这些事件的人。你怎么能把自己定义为发生在你身上的事呢？在这些事发生之前，你就已经意识到自己的存在。这一切都是你亲身经历的，是你亲眼所见、亲身感受的。你无需执着于过往的经历来构建自我。你内心构建的只是一个虚假的自我，一个你用来掩藏自己的概念。

How long have you been hiding in there struggling to keep it all together? Any time anything goes wrong in the protective model you built about yourself, you defend and rationalize in order to get it back together. Your mind does not stop struggling until you’ve processed the event or somehow made it go away. People feel their very existence is at stake, and they will fight and argue until they get control back. This is all because we have attempted to build solidity where there is none. Now we have to fight to keep it together. The problem is, there is no way out that way. There is no peace and there is no winning in that struggle. You were told not to build your house upon sand. Well, this is the ultimate sand. In fact, you built your house in empty space. If you continue to cling to what you built, you will have to continually and perpetually defend yourself. You will have to keep everybody and everything straight in order to reconcile your conceptual model with reality. It’s a constant struggle to keep it together.

你躲在里面多久了？你拼命地维持着这一切。每当你为自己构建的保护模型出现任何破绽，你都会辩解、辩解，试图把它重新拼凑起来。你的大脑会一直挣扎，直到你消化了这件事，或者想办法让它消失。人们感觉自己的存在都受到了威胁，他们会争吵不休，直到重新掌控局面。这一切都是因为我们试图在根本不存在的地方建立起坚实的基础。现在，我们不得不拼命地维持它。问题是，这条路走不通。在这场斗争中，没有平静，也没有胜利。你曾被告知不要把房子建在沙子上。好吧，这就是终极的沙子。事实上，你把房子建在了空旷的空间里。如果你继续执着于你所建造的一切，你将不得不持续不断地为自己辩护。你必须把所有人、所有事都安排妥当，才能让你的概念模型与现实相符。维持这一切，是一场永无止境的斗争。

What it means to live spiritually is to not participate in this struggle. It means that the events that happen in the moment belong to the moment. They don’t belong to you. They have nothing to do with you. You must stop defining yourself in relationship to them, and just let them come and go. Don’t allow events to leave impressions inside of you. If you find yourself thinking about them later on, just let go. If an event happens that doesn’t fit your conceptual model, and you see yourself struggling and rationalizing to make it fit, just notice what you’re doing. An event in the universe didn’t match your model and it’s causing disturbance inside of you. If you will simply notice this, you will find that it is actually breaking up your model. You’ll get to the point where you like this because you don’t want to keep your model. You’ll define this as good because you are no longer willing to put any energy into building and solidifying your faÇade. Instead, you will actually permit the things that disturb your model to act as the dynamite to break it up and free you. This is what it means to live spiritually.

灵性生活意味着不参与这种挣扎。这意味着当下发生的一切都属于当下，它们不属于你，与你无关。你必须停止用它们来定义自己，让它们来来去去。不要让这些事件在你心中留下印记。如果你之后发现自己还在想着它们，那就放下吧。如果发生了一件与你的认知模型不符的事情，而你发现自己在挣扎、试图用理性去解释它，那就觉察一下你的行为。宇宙中的某个事件与你的模型不符，它在你内心造成了干扰。如果你能觉察到这一点，你会发现它实际上正在瓦解你的模型。你会喜欢这种感觉，因为你不想再维持你的模型。你会认为这是好事，因为你不再愿意耗费精力去构建和巩固你的伪装。相反，你会允许那些扰乱你模型的事物成为炸药，炸毁你的模型，让你获得自由。这就是灵性生活的意义所在。

When you become truly spiritual, you are totally different from everybody else. That which everybody else wants, you don’t want. That which everybody else resists, you totally accept. You want your model to break, and you honor the experience when something happens that can cause disturbance within you. Why should anything that anyone says or does cause you to get disturbed? You’re just on a planet spinning around the middle of absolutely nowhere. You came here to visit for a handful of years and then you’re going to leave. How can you live all stressed-out over everything? Don’t do it. If anything can cause disturbance inside of you, it means it hit your model. It means it hit the false part of you that you built in order to control your own definition of reality. But if that model is reality, why didn’t experiential reality fit? There’s nothing you can make up inside your mind that can ever be considered reality.

当你真正达到灵性境界时，你与其他人截然不同。别人想要的，你不想要；别人抗拒的，你全然接受。你渴望打破固有的模式，并尊重那些可能扰乱你内心的体验。为什么任何人的言行都会让你感到不安？你不过身处一颗围绕着虚无中心旋转的星球。你来到这里只是短暂停留几年，然后就要离开。你怎能为一切琐事而焦虑不安？别这样。如果有什么事能扰乱你的内心，那就意味着它触动了你的固有模式。这意味着它触动了你为了掌控自己对现实的定义而构建的虚假自我。但如果这种模式就是现实，为什么体验到的现实却与之不符？你头脑中虚构的任何东西都无法被视为现实。

You must learn to be comfortable with psychological disturbance. If your mind becomes hyperactive, just watch it. If your heart starts to heat up, let it go through what it must. Try to find the part of you that is capable of noticing that your mind is hyperactive and that your heart is heating up. That part is your way out. There is no way out through building this model of yours. The only way to inner freedom is through the one who watches: the Self. The Self simply notices that the mind and emotions are unraveling, and that nothing is struggling to hold them together.

你必须学会与心理波动和平共处。如果你的思绪变得异常活跃，只需观察它。如果你的心开始发热，就让它经历它必须经历的一切。试着找到你内心那个能够觉察到思绪活跃和心跳加速的部分。那部分就是你的出路。你无法通过构建你现在的这种模式来摆脱困境。通往内在自由的唯一途径是通过那个观察者：真我。真我只是觉察到你的心智和情绪正在瓦解，并且没有任何东西试图将它们维系在一起。

Of course this will be painful. The reason you built the whole mental structure was to avoid pain. If you let it fall apart, you’re going to feel the pain that you were avoiding when you built it. You must be willing to face this pain. If you were to lock yourself in a fortress because you were afraid to come out, you would have to face that fear if you ever wanted to experience a fuller existence. That fortress would not be protecting you; it would be imprisoning you. To be free, to truly experience life, you must come out. You have to let go and pass through the cleansing process that frees you from your psyche. You do this by simply watching the psyche be the psyche. The way out is through awareness. Stop defining the disturbed mind as a negative experience; just see if you can relax behind it. When your mind is disturbed, don’t ask, “What do I do about this?” Instead ask, “Who am I that notices this?”

这当然会很痛苦。你构建整个精神体系的原因是为了逃避痛苦。如果你任由它崩塌，你就会感受到当初构建它时想要逃避的痛苦。你必须愿意面对这种痛苦。如果你因为害怕走出堡垒而把自己锁在里面，那么如果你想要体验更完整的人生，就必须直面这种恐惧。那座堡垒不会保护你，反而会囚禁你。为了获得自由，为了真正体验人生，你必须走出去。你必须放手，经历净化的过程，才能从你的精神世界中解脱出来。你只需观察精神的本来面目，就能做到这一点。出路在于觉察。不要把纷乱的思绪定义为负面体验；试着在它背后放松下来。当你的思绪纷乱时，不要问“我该怎么办？”而是问“我是谁，为什么会注意到这一点？”

In time, you will come to realize that the center from which you watch disturbance cannot get disturbed. If it appears disturbed, just notice who is noticing that disturbance. Eventually it will stop. You will then be able to rest back into the depths of your being while watching your mind and heart create their last throes of turmoil. When you reach that point, you will understand what it means to be transcendent. Awareness transcends what it is aware of. It is as separate as light is from what it shines upon. You are consciousness, and you can free yourself from all of this by relaxing behind it.

随着时间的推移，你会逐渐明白，你观察扰动的中心本身并不会受到扰动。如果它看起来受到了扰动，只需留意是谁在察觉这种扰动。最终，扰动会停止。那时，你便能回归存在的深处，静静地观察你的心智和情感在最后的挣扎中消散。当你达到那个境界，你便会明白超越的意义。觉知超越了它所觉知的一切。它如同光与它所照耀的对象一样截然不同。你就是意识，你可以通过放松地回归意识本身，从而从这一切中解脱出来。

If you want permanent peace, permanent joy, and permanent happiness, you have to get through to the other side of the inner turmoil. You can experience a life in which waves of love can rush up inside of you any time you want. It is the nature of your being. You simply have to go to the other side of the psyche. You do that by letting go of the tendency to cling. You do it by not using your mind to build false solidity. You just decide, once and for all, to take the journey by constantly letting go.

如果你渴望永恒的平静、永恒的喜悦和永恒的幸福，就必须跨越内心的纷扰。你可以体验到一种生活，在这种生活中，爱的浪潮可以随时随地涌遍你的心田。这是你与生俱来的本性。你只需抵达心灵的彼岸。而做到这一点，你需要放下执着的倾向。你只需不再用头脑去构建虚假的稳固。你只需下定决心，从此踏上这段不断放手的旅程。

At this point, the journey becomes very quick. You will go through the part of you that has always been scared to death, and you’ll see how that part has always struggled to hold it all together. If you don’t feed that part, if you just keep letting go and don’t let it cling, eventually you will fall behind the false solidity. This is not something you do; it is something that happens to you.

此时，这段旅程将变得异常短暂。你会经历内心深处那个一直恐惧至极的部分，你会看到它是如何苦苦挣扎，试图维系一切。如果你不去滋养它，如果你只是不断地放手，不让它执着，最终你会被虚假的坚固所束缚。这不是你能控制的，而是自然而然发生在你身上的。

Your only way out is the witness. Just keep letting go by being aware that you are aware. If you pass through a period of darkness or depression, just ask, “Who is aware of the darkness?” That’s how you pass through the different stages of your inner growth. You just keep letting go, and remain aware that you are still there. When you’ve let go of the dark psyche, and you’ve let go of the light psyche, and you’re no longer clinging to anything, you will reach a point where it will all open up behind you. You are used to being aware of things in front of you. You now become aware of a universe behind your seat of consciousness.

你唯一的出路是见证者。只需保持觉知，不断放下。如果你经历一段黑暗或抑郁时期，就问问自己：“谁觉知到这黑暗？” 这就是你经历内在成长不同阶段的方式。你只需不断放下，并保持觉知，意识到你依然存在。当你放下黑暗的心灵，放下光明的心灵，不再执着于任何事物时，你就会到达一个境界，一切都会在你身后展开。你习惯于觉知眼前的事物。现在，你将觉知到你意识中心背后的宇宙。

It didn’t look like there was anything behind you. Because you were so focused on building your model out of the thoughts and emotions passing before you, there was no awareness of the vast expanse of space inside. Back behind, there is a whole universe. You’re just not looking that way. If you’re willing to let go, you’ll fall back and it will open into an ocean of energy. You will become filled with light. You will become filled with a light that has no darkness, with a peace that passeth all understanding. You will then walk through every moment of your daily life with the flow of this inner force sustaining you, feeding you, and guiding you from deep within. You will still have thoughts, emotions, and a self-concept floating around in inner space, but they will be just one small part of what you experience. You will not identify with anything outside the sense of Self.

你身后似乎空无一物。因为你专注于用眼前的思绪和情绪构建你的模型，所以没有意识到你内心深处那广袤无垠的空间。在你身后，存在着一个完整的宇宙。只是你没有注意到它。如果你愿意放手，你会向后倒退，那里会展现出一片能量的海洋。你会被光芒充满。你会被一种没有黑暗的光芒充满，被一种超越一切理解的平静充满。然后，你会在日常生活的每一刻都感受到这股内在力量的流动，它滋养着你，指引着你，从你内心深处流淌而出。你的内心空间里仍然会有思绪、情绪和自我概念在流动，但它们只是你体验的一小部分。你将不再认同任何“自我”之外的事物。

Once you reach this state, you will never have to worry about anything ever again. The forces of creation will create creation, both inside and outside of you. You will float in peace, love, and compassion beyond it all, yet honoring it all. There is no need for false solidity when you are at peace with the universal expanse of your true Being.

一旦你达到这种境界，你将永远不必再为任何事担忧。创造的力量将创造万物，无论在你之内还是之外。你将超越一切，漂浮在平和、爱与慈悲之中，同时又敬畏一切。当你与你真实存在的宇宙广阔和谐共处时，便不再需要虚假的稳固。

living life
