15
15
the path of unconditional happiness
无条件幸福之路

The highest spiritual path is life itself. If you know how to live daily life, it all becomes a liberating experience. But first you have to approach life properly, or it can be very confusing. To begin with, you have to realize that you really only have one choice in this life, and it’s not about your career, whom you want to marry, or whether you want to seek God. People tend to burden themselves with so many choices. But, in the end, you can throw it all away and just make one basic, underlying decision: Do you want to be happy, or do you not want to be happy? It’s really that simple. Once you make that choice, your path through life becomes totally clear.

最高的灵性修行之路就是生命本身。如果你懂得如何度过每一天，它都会成为一种解脱的体验。但首先，你必须以正确的方式看待生活，否则它会变得非常令人困惑。首先，你必须意识到，你此生其实只有一次选择，这与你的事业、你想和谁结婚，或者你是否想寻求神灵无关。人们往往给自己背负了太多选择的重担。但最终，你可以抛开一切，只做一个最根本的决定：你想快乐，还是不想快乐？就这么简单。一旦你做出这个选择，你的人生道路就会变得无比清晰。

Most people don’t dare give themselves that choice because they think it’s not under their control. Someone might say, “Well, of course I want to be happy, but my wife left me.” In other words, they want to be happy, but not if their wife leaves them. But that wasn’t the question. The question was, very simply, “Do you want to be happy or not?” If you keep it that simple, you will see that it really is under your control. It’s just that you have a deep-seated set of preferences that gets in the way.

大多数人不敢给自己这个选择，因为他们觉得这不在他们的掌控之中。有人可能会说：“我当然想快乐，可是我老婆离开了我。”换句话说，他们想快乐，但前提是老婆不能离开他们。但这并非问题的关键。问题其实很简单：“你想快乐还是不快乐？”如果你能把问题简化到这种程度，你就会发现，快乐其实完全在你的掌控之中。只是你根深蒂固的固有观念阻碍了你。

Let’s say you’ve been lost and without food for days, and you finally find your way to a house. You can hardly make it to the doorstep, but you manage to pull yourself up and knock on the door. Somebody opens the door, looks at you and says, “Oh my God! You poor thing! Do you want something to eat? What would you like?” Now the truth is, you really don’t care what they give you. You don’t even want to think about it. You just utter the word “food.” And because you really mean it when you say you need food, it no longer has anything to do with your mental preferences. The same goes for the question about happiness. The question is simply “Do you want to be happy?” If the answer is really yes, then say it without qualifying it. After all, what the question really means is “Do you want to be happy from this point forward for the rest of your life, regardless of what happens?”

假设你迷路好几天，没吃东西，终于找到一户人家。你几乎寸步难行，但还是挣扎着站起来敲了敲门。有人开了门，看着你说：“我的天哪！你真可怜！想吃点东西吗？你想吃什么？” 事实上，你根本不在乎他们给你什么。你甚至不想去想。你只是脱口而出“食物”这个词。因为你真的需要食物，所以这不再与你的个人喜好有关。关于幸福的问题也是如此。问题很简单：“你想幸福吗？” 如果答案是肯定的，那就毫不犹豫地说出来。毕竟，这个问题的真正含义是：“从现在开始，无论发生什么，你是否想在余生中都幸福快乐？”

Now, if you say yes, it might happen that your wife leaves you, or your husband dies, or the stock market crashes, or your car breaks down on an open highway at night. Those things might happen between now and the end of your life. But if you want to walk the highest spiritual path, then when you answer yes to that simple question, you must really mean it. There are no ifs, ands, or buts about it. It’s not a question of whether your happiness is under your control. Of course it’s under your control. It’s just that you don’t really mean it when you say you’re willing to stay happy. You want to qualify it. You want to say that as long as this doesn’t happen, or as long as that does happen, then you’re willing to be happy. That’s why it seems like it is out of your control. Any condition you create will limit your happiness. You simply aren’t going to be able to control things and keep them the way you want them.

如果你回答“是”，那么你的妻子可能会离开你，你的丈夫可能会去世，股市可能会崩盘，或者你的车会在夜里抛锚在高速公路上。这些事情可能会在你生命的尽头发生。但如果你想走上最高的精神道路，那么当你对这个简单的问题回答“是”时，你必须是真心实意的。这一点毋庸置疑。这不是你的幸福是否在你掌控之中的问题。当然，它在你的掌控之中。只是当你声称自己愿意保持幸福时，你并没有真正发自内心。你想给它附加条件。你想说，只要这件事不发生，或者只要那件事发生了，你就愿意幸福。这就是为什么它看起来好像不在你的掌控之中。你人为设定的任何条件都会限制你的幸福。你根本无法控制一切，也无法让它们按照你想要的方式发展。

You have to give an unconditional answer. If you decide that you’re going to be happy from now on for the rest of your life, you will not only be happy, you will become enlightened. Unconditional happiness is the highest technique there is. You don’t have to learn Sanskrit or read any scriptures. You don’t have to renounce the world. You just have to really mean it when you say that you choose to be happy. And you have to mean it regardless of what happens. This is truly a spiritual path, and it is as direct and sure a path to Awakening as could possibly exist.

你必须给出无条件的答案。如果你决定从今往后余生都要快乐，你不仅会快乐，还会获得觉悟。无条件的快乐是最高的境界。你无需学习梵文，也无需研读任何经文。你无需遁世遁世。你只需在说你选择快乐时，发自内心。而且无论发生什么，你都必须如此。这才是真正的灵性之路，也是通往觉醒最直接、最可靠的途径。

Once you decide you want to be unconditionally happy, something inevitably will happen that challenges you. This test of your commitment is exactly what stimulates spiritual growth. In fact, it is the unconditional aspect of your commitment that makes this the highest path. It’s so simple. You just have to decide whether or not you will break your vow. When everything is going well, it’s easy to be happy. But the moment something difficult happens, it’s not so easy. You tend to find yourself saying, “But I didn’t know this was going to happen. I didn’t think I’d miss my flight. I didn’t think Sally would show up at the party wearing the same dress that I had on. I didn’t think that somebody would dent my brand-new car one hour after I got it.” Are you really willing to break your vow of happiness because these events took place?

一旦你决定要获得无条件的快乐，就必然会发生一些挑战你的事情。这种对你承诺的考验，正是促进灵性成长的动力。事实上，正是这种无条件的承诺，使之成为通往至高境界的道路。道理很简单，你只需要决定是否要违背你的誓言。一切顺利的时候，快乐很容易。但一旦遇到困难，快乐就没那么容易了。你往往会说：“但我没想到会发生这种事。我没想到我会错过航班。我没想到莎莉会穿着和我一样的裙子出现在派对上。我没想到有人会在我提车一小时后就把我的新车撞凹了。” 你真的愿意因为这些事情的发生而违背你对快乐的誓言吗？

Billions of things could happen that you haven’t even thought of yet. The question is not whether they will happen. Things are going to happen. The real question is whether you want to be happy regardless of what happens. The purpose of your life is to enjoy and learn from your experiences. You were not put on Earth to suffer. You’re not helping anybody by being miserable. Regardless of your philosophical beliefs, the fact remains that you were born and you are going to die. During the time in between, you get to choose whether or not you want to enjoy the experience. Events don’t determine whether or not you’re going to be happy. They’re just events. You determine whether or not you’re going to be happy. You can be happy just to be alive. You can be happy having all these things happen to you, and then be happy to die. If you can live this way, your heart will be so open and your Spirit will be so free, that you will soar up to the heavens.

无数你甚至还没想到的事情可能会发生。问题不在于它们是否会发生，事情一定会发生。真正的问题是，无论发生什么，你是否都想快乐。你人生的意义在于享受经历并从中学习。你来到世上不是为了受苦。痛苦对任何人都没有好处。无论你的哲学信仰如何，事实是你生而为人，终将一死。在这期间，你可以选择是否享受这段经历。事件本身并不能决定你是否快乐，它们仅仅是事件而已。你是否快乐，取决于你自己。你可以仅仅因为活着而快乐。你可以快乐地经历这一切，然后欣然赴死。如果你能这样生活，你的心将无比敞开，你的灵魂将无比自由，你将翱翔于天际。

This path leads you to absolute transcendence because any part of your being that would add a condition to your commitment to happiness has got to go. If you want to be happy, you have to let go of the part of you that wants to create melodrama. This is the part that thinks there’s a reason not to be happy. You have to transcend the personal, and as you do, you will naturally awaken to the higher aspects of your being.

这条道路引领你走向绝对的超越，因为你身上任何会给你的幸福附加条件的部分都必须舍弃。如果你想要幸福，就必须放下那个想要制造戏剧性冲突的部分。正是这部分认为你总有理由不幸福。你必须超越个人层面，当你做到这一点时，你自然会觉醒，领悟你更高层次的自我。

In the end, enjoying life’s experiences is the only rational thing to do. You’re sitting on a planet spinning around in the middle of absolutely nowhere. Go ahead, take a look at reality. You’re floating in empty space in a universe that goes on forever. If you have to be here, at least be happy and enjoy the experience. You’re going to die anyway. Things are going to happen anyway. Why shouldn’t you be happy? You gain nothing by being bothered by life’s events. It doesn’t change the world; you just suffer. There’s always going to be something that can bother you, if you let it.

归根结底，享受人生体验才是唯一理性的做法。你身处一颗在茫茫宇宙中旋转的星球上。不妨直面现实吧。你漂浮在空旷的宇宙中，而宇宙永无止境。既然你注定要来到这里，至少要快乐，享受这段经历。反正你终将一死。世事无常，你为何不能快乐呢？为生活中的种种烦恼于事无补，也改变不了世界，只会让你更加痛苦。只要你允许，总会有让你烦恼的事情发生。

This choice to enjoy life will lead you through your spiritual journey. In truth, it is itself a spiritual teacher. Committing yourself to unconditional happiness will teach you every single thing there is to learn about yourself, about others, and about the nature of life. You will learn all about your mind, your heart, and your will. But you have to mean it when you say that you’ll be happy for the rest of your life. Every time a part of you begins to get unhappy, let it go. Work with it. Use affirmations, or do whatever you need to do to stay open. If you are committed, nothing can stop you. No matter what happens, you can choose to enjoy the experience. If they starve you and put you in solitary confinement, just have fun being like Gandhi. No matter what happens, just enjoy the life that comes to you.

选择享受生活，将引领你踏上灵性之旅。事实上，它本身就是一位灵性导师。全心全意追求无条件的快乐，将教会你关于自身、关于他人、关于生命本质的一切。你将深入了解你的思想、你的内心和你的意志。但当你承诺余生都将快乐时，你必须真心实意。每当内心深处开始感到不快乐时，就放下它。与它共处。运用肯定语，或者做任何你需要做的事情来保持开放的心态。如果你下定决心，没有什么能阻挡你。无论发生什么，你都可以选择享受这段经历。即使他们让你挨饿，把你单独监禁，也要像甘地那样享受生活。无论发生什么，都要享受生命中的一切。

As difficult as that sounds, what’s the benefit of not doing it? If you’re totally innocent and they lock you up, you might as well have fun. What good does it do to not have fun? It doesn’t change anything. In the end, if you stay happy, you win. Make that your game, and just stay happy no matter what.

听起来很难，但不这么做有什么好处呢？如果你完全无辜却被关起来，那还不如好好享受一下。不享受又有什么用呢？什么也改变不了。最终，如果你保持快乐，你就赢了。把这当成你的游戏，无论如何都要保持快乐。

The key to staying happy is really very simple. Begin by understanding your inner energies. If you look inside, you will see that when you’re happy, your heart feels open and the energy rushes up inside of you. When you aren’t happy, your heart feels closed and no energy comes up inside. So to stay happy, just don’t close your heart. No matter what happens, even if your wife leaves you or your husband dies, you don’t close.

保持快乐的秘诀其实很简单。首先要了解你内在的能量。如果你向内观察，你会发现，当你快乐时，你的心扉敞开，能量在你体内涌动。当你不快乐时，你的心扉紧闭，能量无法流动。所以，想要保持快乐，就不要封闭你的心扉。无论发生什么，即使妻子离开你，或者丈夫去世，你都不要封闭自己。

There is no rule that says you have to close. Just tell yourself that no matter what happens, you’re not going to close. You really do have that choice. When you start to close, just question if you’re really willing to give up your happiness. You should examine what it is inside of you that believes there’s some benefit to closing. The slightest thing happens to you, and you give away your happiness. You were having a great day until someone cut you off on your way to work. It got you really upset and you stayed that way the rest of the day. Why? Dare to ask yourself that question. What good came from letting it ruin your day? There was no benefit. If somebody cuts you off, let go and stay open. If you really want to, you can.

没有哪条规定说你必须结束对话。你只需要告诉自己，无论发生什么，都不要结束对话。你真的有这个选择。当你开始想要结束对话时，问问自己是否真的愿意放弃自己的快乐。你应该审视一下，是什么让你觉得结束对话有什么好处。哪怕是再小的事情，你都会放弃自己的快乐。你本来过得很好，直到有人在上班路上插队。这让你非常生气，而且一整天都闷闷不乐。为什么？不妨问问自己这个问题。让这件事毁了你的一天，有什么好处呢？没有任何好处。如果有人插队，就放下这件事，保持开放的心态。如果你真的想这样做，你就能做到。

If you take on this path of unconditional happiness, you will go through all of the various stages of yoga. You will have to stay conscious, centered, and committed at all times. You will have to stay one-pointed on your commitment to remain open and receptive to life. But nobody said that you can’t do this. Staying open is what the great saints and masters taught. They taught that God is joy, God is ecstasy, and God is love. If you remain open enough, waves of uplifting energy will fill your heart. Spiritual practices are not an end in themselves. They bear fruit when you become deep enough to remain open. If you learn to stay open at all times, great things will happen to you. You simply have to learn not to close.

如果你踏上这条通往无条件幸福的道路，你将经历瑜伽的各个阶段。你必须始终保持觉知、专注和投入。你必须一心一意地保持开放和接纳的生活态度。但没有人说过你做不到。保持开放正是伟大圣人和大师们教导我们的。他们教导我们，神是喜悦，神是狂喜，神是爱。如果你足够开放，一波波令人振奋的能量将充满你的心。灵性修行本身并非目的。当你足够深入地体验并保持开放时，它们才会结出果实。如果你学会始终保持开放，美好的事情将会发生在你身上。你只需要学会不要封闭自己。

The key is to learn to keep your mind disciplined enough so that it doesn’t trick you into thinking that this time it’s worth closing. If you slip, get back up. The minute you slip, the minute you open your mouth, the minute you start to close and defend yourself, get back up. Just pick yourself up and affirm inwardly that you don’t want to close, no matter what happens. Affirm that all you want is to be at peace and to appreciate life. You don’t want your happiness to be conditional upon the behavior of other people. It’s bad enough that your happiness is conditional upon your own behavior. When you start making it conditional upon other people’s behavior, you’re in serious trouble.

关键在于学会保持头脑清醒，不让它欺骗你，让你觉得这次值得闭嘴。如果你失言了，就立刻站起来。一旦你失言，一旦你开口，一旦你开始闭嘴为自己辩解，就立刻站起来。振作起来，在内心默默告诉自己，无论发生什么，你都不想闭嘴。默念你只想内心平静，珍惜生命。你不希望自己的幸福取决于他人的行为。你的幸福取决于自己的行为就已经够糟糕了，当你开始让幸福取决于他人的行为时，你就真的麻烦大了。

Things are going to happen to you, and you’re going to feel the tendency to close. But you have the choice to either go with it or let it go. Your mind will tell you that it’s not reasonable to stay open when these things happen. But you have limited time left in your life, and what’s really not reasonable is to not enjoy life.

生活中总会发生一些事，你会感到想要封闭自己。但你可以选择顺其自然，也可以选择放下。你的理智会告诉你，面对这些事情，保持开放的心态是不明智的。但你的人生有限，真正不明智的是放弃享受生活。

If you have trouble remembering that, then meditate. Meditation strengthens your center of consciousness so that you’re always aware enough to not allow your heart to close. You remain open by simply letting go and releasing the tendency to close. You just relax your heart when it starts to tighten. You don’t have to be outwardly glowing all the time; you’re just joyful inside. Instead of complaining, you’re just having fun with the different situations that unfold.

如果你记不住这一点，那就冥想。冥想能增强你的意识中心，让你始终保持足够的觉知，不让自己的心封闭起来。你只需放下执念，释放封闭的冲动，就能保持开放。当心开始紧绷时，放松它。你不必时时都容光焕发，只需内心充满喜悦即可。与其抱怨，不如享受生活中各种不同的境遇。

Unconditional happiness is a very high path and a very high technique because it solves everything. You could learn yoga techniques, such as meditation and postures, but what do you do with the rest of your life? The technique of unconditional happiness is ideal because what you’re doing with the rest of your life is already defined—you’re letting go of yourself so that you can remain happy. As far as your spirituality goes, you’re going to grow very rapidly. A person who actually does this every moment of every day is going to notice the cleansing of their heart. This is because they’re not getting involved in the stuff that comes up. They’re also going to notice the purification of their mind because they are not getting involved in the mind’s melodrama. Their Shakti (Spirit) is going to awaken even if they know nothing about Shakti. They will come to know a happiness that is beyond human understanding. This path solves daily life and it solves spiritual life. The greatest gift one can give to God is to be pleased with His creation.

无条件的快乐是一种极高的境界，也是一种极高的技巧，因为它能解决一切问题。你可以学习瑜伽技巧，比如冥想和体式，但你余下的人生该如何度过呢？无条件的快乐技巧之所以理想，是因为它已经明确了你余下人生的意义——你放下自我，从而保持快乐。就你的灵性而言，你会迅速成长。一个每天每时每刻都践行这种技巧的人，会感受到心灵的净化。这是因为他们不再被纷扰的事物所困扰。他们也会感受到心灵的净化，因为他们不再沉溺于头脑的戏剧性冲突。即使他们对灵性（Shakti）一无所知，他们的灵性也会觉醒。他们将体验到一种超越人类理解的快乐。这条道路既能解决日常生活的问题，也能解决灵性生活的问题。一个人能给予上帝最伟大的礼物，就是对祂的创造感到满意。

Do you think God likes to be around people that are happy or people that are miserable? It’s not hard to tell. Just think about it by imagining that you’re God. You created the heavens and earth so that you can play and experience yourself, and now you’re dropping down to check on your humans. So God asks the first human He sees,

你认为上帝喜欢和快乐的人在一起，还是喜欢和痛苦的人在一起？这不难判断。想象一下你是上帝。你创造了天地万物，是为了让自己玩耍和体验，现在你降临人间，看看你的人类。于是上帝问他看到的第一个人：

“How are you doing?”

“你好吗？”

The human says, “What do you mean, how am I doing?”

人说：“你什么意思？我做得怎么样？”

“Well, do you like it here?”

“嗯，你喜欢这里吗？”

“No, I don’t like it here.”

“不，我不喜欢这里。”

“Why not? What’s wrong?”

“为什么不行？有什么问题吗？”

“That tree is bent in five places; I want it to be straight. This person went out with somebody else, and that person ran up a hundred-dollar phone bill. This person has a nicer car than mine and that person dresses funny. It’s just terrible. Plus my nose is too big, my ears are too small, and my toes are weird. I’m not happy with it. I don’t like any of it.”

“那棵树有五处弯曲，我希望它是直的。这个人跟别人约会了，那个人欠了一百美元的电话费。这个人开的车比我的好，那个人穿衣打扮很奇怪。真是糟透了。而且我的鼻子太大，耳朵太小，脚趾也怪怪的。我不满意。我一点都不喜欢。”

So God says, “Well, how about the animals?”

于是上帝说：“那么动物们呢？”

“The animals? The ants and mosquitoes bite you; it’s a terrible thing. I can’t go out at night because there are all these animals out there. They howl and poop all over the place, and I just don’t like it.”

“那些动物？蚂蚁和蚊子会咬人，真是太可怕了。我晚上不敢出门，因为外面到处都是这些动物。它们嚎叫，到处拉屎，我实在受不了。”

Do you think God likes listening to this? He says, “What do you think—I’m a complaint department?” Then He goes and visits somebody else, and again, He asks,

你觉得上帝喜欢听这些吗？祂说：“你以为我是个投诉部门吗？”然后祂又去拜访了另一个人，再次问道：

“How are you doing?”

“你好吗？”

This person says, “I’m ecstatic.”

这个人说：“我欣喜若狂。”

God says, “Wow! Well, how do you like things?”

上帝说：“哇！怎么样，你觉得怎么样？”

“They’re beautiful. Everything I look at just creates waves of joy inside me. I look at that bent tree; it just blows me away. The ant comes and bites me, and it’s just so amazing that a tiny ant could be brave enough to bite a giant like me!”

“它们真美。我看到的每样东西都让我内心充满喜悦。我看着那棵弯曲的树，简直太震撼了。蚂蚁过来咬我，真是太神奇了，一只小小的蚂蚁竟然有勇气咬我这样的巨人！”

Now you guess who God wants to hang out with. One of the ancient names for God in the yogic tradition is Satchitananda —Eternal, Conscious Bliss. God is ecstasy. God is as high as it gets. If you want to be close to God, learn to be joyful. If you remain spontaneously happy and centered, no matter what happens, you will find God. That’s the amazing part. Yes, you will find happiness, but that’s nothing compared to what you’re really going to find.

现在你猜猜上帝想和谁在一起？在瑜伽传统中，上帝的古老名字之一是萨奇塔南达（Satchitananda）——永恒的觉知极乐。上帝就是狂喜。上帝是至高无上的境界。如果你想亲近上帝，就学会快乐。如果你无论发生什么都能保持自发的快乐和内心的平静，你就会找到上帝。这才是最神奇的地方。是的，你会找到快乐，但这与你真正将要找到的东西相比，简直微不足道。

Once you have passed through trial by fire, and you are thoroughly convinced that you will let go no matter what, then the veils of the human mind and heart will fall away. You will stand face-to-face with what is beyond you because there is no longer a need for you. When you are done playing with the temporal and finite, you will open to the eternal and infinite. Then the word “happiness” can’t describe your state. That’s where words like ecstasy, bliss, liberation, Nirvana, and freedom come in. The joy becomes overwhelming, and your cup runneth over.

当你经历过烈火的考验，并彻底确信无论如何都要放下一切，那么人类心智和心灵的面纱就会褪去。你将直面超越自身的存在，因为你不再需要自己。当你不再沉溺于短暂和有限的事物，你将敞开心扉拥抱永恒和无限。那时，“幸福”一词将无法描述你的境界。这时，狂喜、极乐、解脱、涅槃和自由等词汇便会应运而生。喜悦将如潮水般涌来，你的幸福之杯将满溢而出。

This is a beautiful path. Be happy.

这是一条美好的道路。要快乐。

16
16
the spiritual path of nonresistance
非抵抗的精神之路

One should view their spiritual work as learning to live life without stress, problems, fear, or melodrama. This path of using life to evolve spiritually is truly the highest path. There really is no reason for tension or problems. Stress only happens when you resist life’s events. If you’re neither pushing life away, nor pulling it toward you, then you are not creating any resistance. You are simply present. In this state, you are just witnessing and experiencing the events of life taking place. If you choose to live this way, you will see that life can be lived in a state of peace.

人们应该把灵性修行看作是学习如何无压力、无烦恼、无恐惧、无戏剧化地生活。这条利用生活来提升灵性的道路，才是真正的至高境界。其实，紧张和烦恼都毫无必要。压力只源于你抗拒生活中的种种际遇。如果你既不排斥生活，也不强求生活，那么你就不会产生任何抗拒。你只是全然地存在着。在这种状态下，你只是见证和体验着生活中发生的种种事件。如果你选择这样生活，你就会发现，生活可以充满平和。

What an amazing process life is, this flow of atoms through time and space. It’s just an eternal sequence of events that take form and then instantly dissolve into the next moment. If you resist this amazing force of life, tension builds within you and gets into your body, mind, and spiritual heart.

生命是一个多么奇妙的过程啊，原子在时间和空间中的流动。它就像一个永恒的序列，形态的形成，瞬间消融于下一刻。如果你抗拒这股奇妙的生命力量，紧张感就会在你体内积聚，侵蚀你的身体、心灵和精神。

It is not difficult to see the tendency toward stress and resistance in daily life. But if we want to understand this tendency, we must first examine why we are so resistant to just letting life be life. What is it inside of us that even has the ability to resist the reality of life? If you look carefully inside yourself, you will see that it’s you, the Self, the indwelling being, that has this power. It is called willpower.

在日常生活中，我们不难发现人们容易产生压力和抵触情绪。但如果我们想理解这种倾向，首先必须探究我们为何如此抗拒顺其自然，接受生活本来的样子。究竟是什么力量让我们如此抗拒生活的现实？如果你仔细审视内心，就会发现，拥有这种力量的正是你自身，是你的真我，是内在的那个存在。它被称为意志力。

Will is a real force that emanates from your being. It is what makes your arms and legs move. They don’t just move randomly by themselves. They move the way they do because you assert will to make them do so. You use the same will to hold onto thoughts when you want to concentrate on them. The power of Self, when it is concentrated and directed into the physical, mental, or emotional realms, creates a force, and we call that force “will.” That’s what you use when you try to make things happen or not happen. You are not helpless in there; you have the power to affect things.

意志是一种源自你内在的真实力量。它使你的四肢能够活动。它们并非随意移动，而是因为你运用意志力控制它们。当你想要集中注意力于某个念头时，你也运用同样的意志力来保持专注。当自我之力集中并引导至身体、精神或情感领域时，便会产生一种力量，我们称之为“意志”。当你试图让事情发生或不发生时，你正是运用了这种力量。你并非无能为力；你拥有影响事物的力量。

It’s amazing to see what we end up doing with our will. We actually assert our will in opposition to the flow of life. If something happens that we don’t like, we resist it. But since what we’re resisting has already taken place, what good is it to resist? If your best friend moves away, it’s understandable that you don’t like it. But your inner resistance to that event for years to come does not change the fact that they did, indeed, move away. It does not do anything to the reality of the situation.

看看我们最终会如何运用自己的意志，真是令人惊奇。我们竟然会违背生活的自然规律，强行运用自己的意志。如果发生了什么我们不喜欢的事情，我们会抗拒。但既然我们抗拒的事情已经发生，抗拒又有什么用呢？如果你的挚友搬走了，你当然会感到不快。但你未来几年对这件事的内心抗拒，并不能改变他们已经搬走的事实。它对现实情况没有任何影响。

The fact is, it cannot even be argued that we’re resisting the actual situation. For instance, if somebody says something that we don’t like, obviously our resistance won’t stop them from having said it. What we’re really resisting is the experience of the event passing through us. We don’t want it affecting us inside. We know it is going to make mental and emotional impressions that will not fit with what’s already in there. So we assert the force of will against the influence of the event in an attempt to stop it from passing through our hearts and minds. In other words, the experience of an event does not stop with our sensory observation of it. The event also has to pass through the psyche at an energetic level. This is a process we experience every day. The initial sensory observation touches our mental and emotional energy pools, creating movements in the energy. These movements pass through the psyche much like physical impact ripples through water. Amazingly, you actually have the ability to resist these movements of energy. The assertion of willpower can stop the energy transfer, and that’s what creates tension. You can wear yourself out struggling with the experience of a single event, or even a single thought or emotion. And you know that all too well.

事实上，我们甚至无法否认自己是在抗拒现实。例如，如果有人说了我们不喜欢的话，显然我们的抗拒并不能阻止他们说出口。我们真正抗拒的是这件事带给我们的体验。我们不希望它影响我们的内心。我们知道它会在我们心中留下与既有认知不符的心理和情感印记。因此，我们试图用意志力对抗这件事的影响，阻止它进入我们的内心。换句话说，对一件事的体验并不仅仅止于我们对它的感官观察。这件事还必须在能量层面上穿过我们的心灵。这是一个我们每天都在经历的过程。最初的感官观察触及了我们心灵和情感的能量池，在能量中激起涟漪。这些能量的涌动如同物理冲击在水中激起的涟漪一般，贯穿我们的心灵。令人惊奇的是，我们实际上有能力抗拒这些能量的涌动。过分强调意志力会阻碍能量的传递，而这正是紧张的根源。你可能会因为纠结于某件事、某个念头或某种情绪而精疲力竭。对此，你深有体会。

Eventually you’ll see that this resistance is a tremendous waste of energy. The fact is, you’re generally using your will to resist one of two things: that which has already happened or that which hasn’t happened yet. You are sitting inside resisting impressions from the past or thoughts about the future. Think of how much energy is wasted resisting what has already happened. Since the event has already passed, you are actually struggling with yourself, not with the event. In addition, contemplate how much energy is wasted resisting what might happen. Since most of the things you think might happen never do, you are just throwing your energy away.

最终你会发现，这种抗拒是在白白浪费精力。事实上，你通常用意志力去抗拒两件事：已经发生的事情或尚未发生的事情。你内心深处抗拒着过去的印象或对未来的担忧。想想看，抗拒已经发生的事情浪费了多少精力。既然事情已经过去，你实际上是在与自己作斗争，而不是与事情本身作斗争。此外，想想看，抗拒可能发生的事情又浪费了多少精力。因为你认为可能发生的事情大多都不会发生，你只是在白白浪费精力。

How you deal with your energy flow has a major effect on your life. If you assert your will against the energy of an event that has already happened, it is like trying to stop the ripples caused by a leaf dropped into a still lake. Anything you do causes more disturbance, not less. When you resist, the energy has no place to go. It gets stuck in your psyche and seriously affects you. It blocks your heart’s energy flow and causes you to feel closed and less vibrant. This is literally what is happening when something is weighing on your mind or when things just get too heavy for you.

你如何处理自己的能量流动会对你的生活产生重大影响。如果你试图用意志力对抗已经发生的事情所带来的能量，就如同试图阻止一片落叶落入平静湖面所激起的涟漪。你的任何举动只会加剧扰动，而不会减少。当你抗拒时，能量无处可去，它会滞留在你的精神深处，严重影响你。它会阻碍你心脏的能量流动，让你感到封闭、缺乏活力。这正是当你心事重重或事情让你不堪重负时的真实写照。

This is the human predicament. Events have happened and we continue to hold their energy inside of us by resisting them. Now, when we face today’s events, we are neither prepared to receive them nor capable of digesting them. This is because we’re still struggling with past energies. Over time, the energies can build up to the point that a person becomes so blocked that they either blow up or shut down completely. This is what it means to get stressed-out or even totally burned-out.

这就是人类的困境。过去的事情已经发生，我们却一直抗拒着它们的能量，将它们压抑在内心深处。如今，当我们面对当下的事件时，我们既没有做好接受的准备，也没有能力消化它们。这是因为我们仍在与过去的能量作斗争。随着时间的推移，这些能量会不断累积，最终导致人被阻塞，要么彻底崩溃，要么彻底麻木。这就是压力过大甚至精疲力竭的真正含义。

There is no reason to get stressed-out. There is no reason for blowing up or shutting down. If you do not let this energy build up inside you, but instead allow each moment of each day to pass through you, then you can be as fresh every moment as you would be on a stress-free vacation. It is not life’s events that are causing problems or stress. It is your resistance to life’s events that is causing this experience. Since the problem is caused by using your will to resist the reality of life passing through you, the solution is quite obvious—stop resisting. If you are going to resist something, at least have some rational basis for resisting. Otherwise, you are irrationally wasting precious energy.

没有理由感到压力重重。没有理由发脾气或崩溃。如果你不让这种能量在体内积聚，而是让每一天的每一刻自然流逝，那么你就能时刻保持神清气爽，如同置身于一个无压力的假期。造成问题或压力的并非生活本身，而是你对生活事件的抗拒。既然问题源于你试图用意志力抗拒生活的现实，那么解决方法显而易见——停止抗拒。如果你一定要抗拒，至少要有一些合理的理由。否则，你就是在无谓地浪费宝贵的精力。

Be willing to examine the process of resistance. In order to resist you first must decide that something is not the way you like it. Plenty of events make it right through you. Why did you decide to resist this one? Something inside of you must have a basis for deciding when to simply let things pass through and when to assert willpower to either push them away or cling to them. There are a billion things that don’t bother you at all. You drive to work every day and you hardly notice the buildings and trees. The white lines on the road don’t stress you out at all. You see them, but they pass right through you. Don’t assume, however, it’s that way for everyone. Someone who paints street lines for a living could get very stressed-out if those white lines were not even. In fact, they could get so stressed-out that they refuse to drive down that road anymore. It’s clear that not all of us resist the same things or have the same issues. This is because we don’t all have the same preconceived notions of how things should be or how much they should matter to us.

要勇于审视抵抗的过程。要进行抵抗，首先你必须认定某件事不符合你的预期。很多事情你都能坦然接受，但为什么这次你却选择抵抗呢？你内心深处一定存在某种根基，让你能够决定何时顺其自然，何时运用意志力去推开或紧紧抓住。有无数的事情根本不会困扰你。你每天开车上班，几乎不会注意到沿途的建筑和树木。路上的白线也丝毫不会让你感到压力。你看到了它们，但它们却像从你眼前掠过。然而，不要以为每个人都如此。一个以画路标为生的人，如果看到不均匀的白线，可能会感到非常焦虑。事实上，他们甚至可能因此拒绝再走那条路。显然，我们并非所有人都会对同样的事情或问题感到抗拒。这是因为我们对事物应有的状态以及它们对我们的重要性并没有相同的先入之见。

If you want to understand stress, begin by realizing that you carry around with you your own set of preconceived notions of how things should be. It is based upon these notions that you assert your will to resist what has already happened. Where did you get these preconceived notions? Let’s say that seeing azaleas in bloom stresses you out. Surely that doesn’t bother most people. Why does it bother you? All we need to know is that you once had a girlfriend who grew azaleas, and she broke up with you when they were in bloom. Now every time you see azaleas in bloom, your heart closes. You don’t even want to go near the things; they just create too much disturbance for you.

如果你想了解压力，首先要意识到你内心深处带着一套关于事物应有状态的先入之见。正是基于这些先入之见，你才会执着于抗拒已经发生的事情。那么，这些先入之见从何而来呢？假设看到杜鹃花盛开会让你感到压力。这当然不会困扰大多数人。为什么它会让你如此烦恼呢？我们只需要知道，你曾经有个女朋友，她种了杜鹃花，而她正是在杜鹃花盛开的时候和你分手的。现在，每当你看到杜鹃花盛开，你的心都会紧闭。你甚至不想靠近它们；它们只会给你带来太多的困扰。

These personal events that take place in our lives leave impressions on our minds and hearts. Those impressions become the basis for asserting our will to either resist or cling. It’s no deeper than that. The events may have happened in your childhood or at various points throughout your life. Regardless of when they happened, they left impressions inside of you. Now, based on these past impressions, you are resisting the current events that are taking place. This creates inner tension, turmoil, struggle, and suffering. Instead of seeing this and refusing to allow these past events to run your life, you buy into them. Believing they have real meaning, you put all your heart and soul into either resisting or clinging. But in truth, this entire process has no real meaning. It just destroys your life.

我们生命中发生的这些个人事件会在我们的思想和心灵上留下印记。这些印记成为我们意志力的根源，决定我们是抗拒还是执着。仅此而已。这些事件可能发生在你的童年时期，也可能发生在你人生的各个阶段。无论何时发生，它们都在你心中留下了印记。现在，基于这些过去的印记，你正在抗拒当下正在发生的事情。这会造成内心的紧张、动荡、挣扎和痛苦。你非但没有意识到这一点，也没有拒绝让这些过去的经历主宰你的生活，反而接受了它们。你相信它们具有真正的意义，于是倾尽全力去抗拒或执着。但事实上，整个过程没有任何真正的意义。它只会摧毁你的生活。

The alternative is to use life to let go of these impressions and the stress they create. In order to do this you have to become very conscious. You have to carefully watch the mental voice that tells you to resist something. It literally commands you: “I don’t like what he said. Fix it.” It gives you advice and tells you to confront the world by resisting things. Why do you listen to it? Let your spiritual path become the willingness to let whatever happens make it through you, rather than carrying it into the next moment. That doesn’t mean you don’t deal with what happens. You’re welcome to deal with it, but first let the energy make it through you. If you don’t, you will not actually be dealing with the current event, you will be dealing with your own blocked energies from the past. You will not be coming from a place of clarity, but from a place of inner resistance and tension.

另一种方法是利用生活来放下这些印象以及它们带来的压力。为了做到这一点，你必须变得非常清醒。你必须仔细观察那个让你抗拒某些事物的内心声音。它实际上是在命令你：“我不喜欢他说的那些话。纠正它。”它给你建议，告诉你通过抗拒来对抗世界。你为什么要听从它呢？让你的灵性之路成为一种意愿，让发生的一切都自然地流经你，而不是将它们带入下一刻。这并不意味着你对发生的事情置之不理。你可以选择处理，但首先要让能量流经你。如果你不这样做，你实际上处理的就不是当下发生的事情，而是你过去阻塞的能量。你将无法从清晰的状态出发，而是从内心的抗拒和紧张的状态出发。

To avoid this, begin dealing with each situation with acceptance. Acceptance means that events can make it through you without resistance. If an event takes place and is able to make it through your psyche, you will be left face-to-face with the actual situation as it truly exists. Since you are dealing with the actual event, rather than stored energies stimulated by the event, you won’t assert reactive energy from your past. You will find that you are able to deal with daily situations much better. It is actually possible to never have another problem for the rest of your life. This is because events are not problems; they’re just events. Your resistance to them is what causes the problem. But, again, don’t think that because you accept reality it means you don’t deal with things. You do deal with them. You just deal with them as events that are taking place on the planet Earth, and not as personal problems.

为了避免这种情况，首先要学会接纳每一种情况。接纳意味着你可以毫无抗拒地接受事件。如果一件事情发生并能顺利通过你的内心，你就能直面事件的真实面貌。因为你面对的是事件本身，而不是事件激发出的积压能量，所以你不会再受过去经历的影响。你会发现自己能更好地应对日常琐事。实际上，你甚至有可能从此不再遇到任何问题。这是因为事件本身并非问题，它们仅仅是事件。你对事件的抗拒才是问题的根源。但是，再次强调，不要以为接纳现实就意味着你无需面对现实。你仍然需要面对它们。你只是将它们视为发生在地球上的事件，而不是个人问题。

You will be surprised to find that in most situations there’s nothing to deal with except for your own fears and desires. Fear and desire make everything seem so complicated. If you don’t have fear or desire about an event, there’s really nothing to deal with. You simply allow life to unfold and interact with it in a natural and rational manner. When the next thing happens, you’re fully present in that moment and simply enjoying the experience of life. There are no problems. It’s all about no problems, no tension, no stress, and no burnout. When the events of this world make it through you, you have reached a deep spiritual state. You can then be conscious in the presence of whatever takes place, without building up blocked energies. When you attain that state, everything becomes clear. In contrast, everybody else is attempting to deal with the world around them while struggling with their own reactions and personal preferences. When a person is dealing with their own fears, anxieties, and desires, how much energy is left for dealing with what’s actually happening?

你会惊讶地发现，在大多数情况下，除了你自身的恐惧和欲望之外，你无需处理其他任何事情。恐惧和欲望让一切看起来如此复杂。如果你对某件事既没有恐惧也没有欲望，那就真的没什么需要处理的。你只需顺其自然，以一种自然而理性的方式与之互动。当接下来的事情发生时，你完全沉浸于当下，享受着生命的体验。没有问题。一切都与问题、紧张、压力和疲惫无关。当世间万物都与你相伴而行时，你就达到了一种深层的精神境界。那时，你可以觉察到所发生的一切，而不会积聚阻塞的能量。当你达到这种境界时，一切都变得清晰明了。相比之下，其他人都在努力应对周遭世界，同时还要与自身的反应和偏好作斗争。当一个人忙于应对自身的恐惧、焦虑和欲望时，还有多少精力去处理真正发生的事情呢？

Stop and think about what you’re capable of achieving. Up to now, your capacities have been constrained by constant inner struggles. Imagine what would happen if your awareness was free to focus only on the events actually taking place. You would have no noise going on inside. If you lived like this, you could do anything. Your capabilities would be exponential compared to what you’ve ever experienced. If you could bring this level of awareness and clarity to everything you do, your life would change.

停下来想想你究竟能做到什么。迄今为止，你的能力一直被持续不断的内心挣扎所限制。想象一下，如果你的意识可以自由地专注于正在发生的事情，会发生什么？你的内心将不再有任何杂念。如果你能这样生活，你就能做到任何事。你的能力将比你以往经历的呈指数级增长。如果你能将这种觉察和清晰的思维融入到你所做的每一件事中，你的人生将会彻底改变。

So, as your path, you take on the work of using life to let go of your resistance. Relationships are a great way to work with yourself. Imagine if you used relationships to get to know other people, rather than to satisfy what is blocked inside of you. If you’re not trying to make people fit into your preconceived notions of what you like and dislike, you will find that relationships are not really that difficult. If you’re not so busy judging and resisting people based upon what is blocked inside of you, you will find that they are much easier to get along with—and so are you. Letting go of yourself is the simplest way to get closer to others.

所以，你的人生道路就是利用生活的力量来放下你的抗拒。人际关系是与自己相处的绝佳途径。试想一下，如果你利用人际关系去了解他人，而不是为了满足你内心的压抑，那会是怎样一番景象？如果你不再试图让别人符合你预设的喜好，你会发现人际关系其实并没有那么难。如果你不再因为内心的压抑而评判和抗拒他人，你会发现他们更容易相处——你也更容易与他人相处。放下自我，是拉近与他人距离的最简单方法。

The same is true in your daily work. Daily work is fun. In fact, it’s easy. Your work is just what you do with yourself during the day while you’re spinning on a planet through empty space. If you want to be content and enjoy your work, you have to let go of yourself and let events flow through you. Your real work is what is left to do after all else passes through.

你的日常工作也是如此。日常工作很有趣，事实上，它很轻松。你的工作就是你白天在宇宙中旋转时，如何度过这段时间。如果你想感到满足并享受工作，就必须放下自我，让一切顺其自然。你真正的工作，是当一切都过去之后，剩下的事情。

Once the personal energies pass through you, the world becomes a different place. People and events will appear different to you. You will realize that you have talents and abilities you never saw before. Your whole view of life will change. Every single thing in this world will look like it’s been transformed. This happens because as you let go in one situation, it affects your clarity for other situations. For example, let’s say you’re afraid of dogs. You come to realize that other people aren’t afraid, and they make it through life. Since you’ve been afraid your whole life, you suffered while others didn’t. That suffering had no meaning. So you decide to work with your fear and relax when you see a dog. The way to work with resistance is by relaxing. That act of relaxing through your personal resistance not only changes your relationship with dogs, it changes your relationship with everything. Your soul has now learned how to let disturbing energies pass through. The next time somebody says or does something you don’t like, you automatically treat it the same as you did the fear of dogs. This process of relaxing through resistance is beneficial to everything in your life. This is because it directly addresses how to keep your heart open when it is trying to close.

当个人能量流过你之后，世界将焕然一新。人和事在你眼中都会呈现出不同的面貌。你会意识到自己拥有从未发现的天赋和能力。你对生活的整体看法将会发生改变。世间万物仿佛都经历了蜕变。这是因为你在某种情况下放下执念，会影响你对其他情况的判断力。例如，假设你害怕狗。你逐渐意识到其他人并不害怕，他们也能好好生活。因为你一生都活在恐惧中，所以你承受着痛苦，而其他人却没有。这种痛苦毫无意义。于是你决定与恐惧共处，在看到狗时放松下来。克服阻力的方法就是放松。这种通过放松来克服个人阻力的行为，不仅改变了你与狗的关系，也改变了你与万物的关系。你的灵魂已经学会了如何让那些令人不安的能量流过。下次如果有人说了或做了你不喜欢的事情，你自然而然地就会像对待害怕狗一样去处理它。这种通过抵抗而放松的过程对你生活中的一切都有益。这是因为它直接解决了如何在心扉试图关闭时保持敞开的问题。

Deep inner release is a spiritual path in and of itself. It is the path of nonresistance, the path of acceptance, the path of surrender. It’s about not resisting energies as they pass through you. If you have difficulty doing this, don’t get down on yourself. Just keep working with it. It’s the work of a lifetime to become that open, that complete, and that whole.

深层的内在释放本身就是一条灵性之路。它是一条不抗拒之路，一条接纳之路，一条臣服之路。它关乎于不抗拒能量流经你的过程。如果你难以做到这一点，不要气馁。只需坚持练习。达到那种开放、完整和圆满的状态，需要一生的时间去修行。

The key is to just relax and release, and deal only with what’s left in front of you. You do not need to worry about the rest. If you relax and release, you will see that it puts you through tremendous spiritual growth. You’ll start to feel an enormous amount of energy awaken inside of you. You will feel much more love than you’ve ever felt before. You will feel more peace and contentment, and eventually nothing will ever disturb you again.

关键在于放松身心，放下一切，只专注于眼前的事情。其他的事情无需担忧。如果你能放松下来，你会发现这会让你获得巨大的精神成长。你会开始感受到体内一股强大的能量正在觉醒。你会感受到前所未有的爱。你会感受到更多的平静和满足，最终，没有任何事物能够再打扰你。

You truly can reach a state in which you never have any more stress, tension, or problems for the rest of your life. You just have to realize that life is giving you a gift, and that gift is the flow of events that takes place between your birth and your death. These events are exciting, challenging, and create tremendous growth. To comfortably handle this flow of life, your heart and mind must be open and expansive enough to encompass reality. The only reason they’re not is because you resist. Learn to stop resisting reality, and what used to look like stressful problems will begin to look like the stepping-stones of your spiritual journey.

你真的可以达到一种境界，在这种境界中，你余生将不再有任何压力、紧张或问题。你只需要意识到，生命正在给予你一份礼物，这份礼物就是你从出生到死亡之间发生的种种经历。这些经历令人兴奋，充满挑战，并能带来巨大的成长。为了能够自在地驾驭这生命之流，你的心智必须足够开放和包容，才能接纳现实。它们之所以无法做到这一点，唯一的原因是你在抗拒。学会停止抗拒现实，那些曾经看似令人倍感压力的问题，将会变成你灵性之旅的垫脚石。

contemplating death
思考死亡

It is truly a great cosmic paradox that one of the best teachers in all of life turns out to be death. No person or situation could ever teach you as much as death has to teach you. While someone could tell you that you are not your body, death shows you. While someone could remind you of the insignificance of the things that you cling to, death takes them all away in a second. While people can teach you that men and women of all races are equal and that there is no difference between the rich and the poor, death instantly makes us all the same.

人生中最伟大的导师之一竟是死亡，这真是一个宇宙悖论。没有任何人或事能像死亡那样教会你如此之多。有人或许会告诉你，你并非你的肉体，但死亡会让你亲身体验。有人或许会提醒你，你所执着的一切都微不足道，但死亡却会在瞬间将它们全部夺走。人们或许会告诉你，男女平等，贫富之间并无差别，但死亡却会在瞬间让我们都变得一样。

The question is, are you going to wait until that last moment to let death be your teacher? The mere possibility of death has the power to teach us at any moment. A wise person realizes that at any moment they may breathe out, and the breath may not come back in. It could happen any time, in any place, and your last breath is gone. You have to learn from this. A wise being completely and totally embraces the reality, the inevitability, and the unpredictability of death.

问题是，你是否要等到最后一刻才让死亡成为你的老师？仅仅是死亡的可能性，就足以在任何时刻教会我们一些东西。智者明白，他们随时都可能呼出最后一口气，而这口气可能再也吸不回来。这可能发生在任何时间、任何地点，你的最后一口气就此消逝。你必须从中学习。智者会完全地、彻底地接受死亡的现实、它的必然性和它的不可预测性。

Any time you’re having trouble with something, think of death. Let’s say you’re the jealous type, and you can’t stand anyone being close to your mate. Think about what will happen when you’re no longer here. Is it really all that romantic that your loved one should live alone with no one to care for them? If you can get past your personal issues, you’ll find that you want the person you love to be happy and to have a full and beautiful life. Since that is what you want for them, why are you bothering them now just for talking to someone?

每当你遇到麻烦时，想想死亡。比如说，你是个爱嫉妒的人，无法忍受任何人接近你的伴侣。想想当你不在人世时会发生什么。让你的爱人孤身一人，无人照料，这真的浪漫吗？如果你能克服自己的个人问题，你会发现，你其实希望你爱的人幸福，拥有充实美好的人生。既然这是你对他们的期望，那你现在又何必仅仅因为他们和别人聊天就去打扰他们呢？

It shouldn’t take death to challenge you to live at your highest level. Why wait until everything is taken from you before you learn to dig down deep inside yourself to reach your highest potential? A wise person affirms, “If with one breath all of this can change, then I want to live at the highest level while I’m alive. I’m going to stop bothering the people I love. I’m going to live life from the deepest part of my being.”

无需等到死亡降临，你才能真正觉醒，活出自我。为何要等到失去一切，才懂得挖掘自身潜力，发挥最大潜能？智者如是说：“如果一口气就能改变一切，那么我愿在有生之年活出精彩。我不再打扰我爱的人。我要从内心深处去生活。”

This is the consciousness necessary for deep and meaningful relationships. Look how callous we get with our loved ones. We take it for granted that they’re there and that they’ll continue to be there for us. What if they died? What if you died? What if you knew that this evening would be the last time you’d get to see them? Imagine that an angel comes down and tells you, “Straighten up your affairs. You will not awake from your sleep tonight. You’re coming to me.” Then you’d know that every person you see that day, you’d be seeing for the last time. How would you feel? How would you interact with them? Would you even bother with the little grudges and complaints you’ve been carrying around? How much love could you give the ones you love, knowing it would be the last time you’d get to be with them? Think about what it would be like if you lived like that every moment with everyone. Your life would be really different. You should contemplate this. Death is not a morbid thought. Death is the greatest teacher in all of life.

这是建立深刻而有意义的人际关系所必需的意识。看看我们对待所爱之人是多么冷漠无情。我们理所当然地认为他们会一直陪伴在我们身边。如果他们去世了呢？如果你自己去世了呢？如果你知道今晚将是你最后一次见到他们呢？想象一下，一位天使降临，告诉你：“安排好你的后事。今晚你将不会醒来。你将回到我身边。”那时你就会明白，你今天见到的每个人，都将是你最后一次见到他们。你会作何感想？你会如何与他们相处？你还会在意那些你一直耿耿于怀的小怨恨和抱怨吗？当你意识到这将是你最后一次与他们相聚时，你还能给予你所爱的人多少爱？想想如果你每时每刻都以这样的心态与每个人相处，那会是什么样子。你的生活将会截然不同。你应该认真思考这个问题。死亡并非令人恐惧的念头。死亡是人生中最伟大的导师。

Take a moment to look at the things you think you need. Look at how much time and energy you put into various activities. Imagine if you knew you were going to die within a week or a month. How would that change things? How would your priorities change? How would your thoughts change? Think honestly about what you would do with your last week. What a wonderful thought to contemplate. Then ponder this question: If that’s really what you would do with your last week, what are you doing with the rest of your time? Wasting it? Throwing it away? Treating it like it’s not something precious? What are you doing with life? That is what death asks you.

花点时间想想你认为自己需要的东西。看看你投入了多少时间和精力在各种活动上。想象一下，如果你知道自己会在一周或一个月内死去，那会怎样？你的生活会发生怎样的变化？你的优先事项会如何改变？你的想法又会如何改变？认真想想，如果你只剩下最后一周，你会做什么。这是一个多么值得深思的问题。然后，仔细思考这个问题：如果你真的打算这样度过最后一周，那么你剩下的时间都在做什么？是在浪费时间吗？是在虚度光阴吗？是在视之为不珍贵的东西吗？你究竟在如何度过你的人生？这就是死亡向你提出的问题。

Let’s say you’re living life without the thought of death, and the Angel of Death comes to you and says, “Come, it’s time to go.” You say, “But no. You’re supposed to give me a warning so I can decide what I want to do with my last week. I’m supposed to get one more week.” Do you know what Death will say to you? He’ll say, “My God! I gave you fifty-two weeks this past year alone. And look at all the other weeks I’ve given you. Why would you need one more? What did you do with all those?” If asked that, what are you going to say? How will you answer? “I wasn’t paying attention… I didn’t think it mattered.” That’s a pretty amazing thing to say about your life.

假设你从未想过死亡，而死神突然出现，对你说：“来吧，该走了。” 你说：“不，你应该提前通知我，让我好好想想最后一周该怎么过。我应该再多活一周。” 你知道死神会怎么回答你吗？他会说：“我的天哪！光去年一年我就给了你五十二周。再看看我给你的其他时间，你为什么还需要一周？你都干了些什么？” 如果有人这样问你，你会怎么说？你会怎么回答？“我没注意……我觉得这无关紧要。” 这话说得真够讽刺的。

Death is a great teacher. But who lives with that level of awareness? It doesn’t matter what age you are; at any time you could take a breath and there may never be another. It happens all the time—to babies, to teenagers, to people in mid-life—not just to the aged. One breath and they’re gone. No one knows when their time will be. That’s not how it works.

死亡是一位伟大的导师。但又有谁能真正意识到这一点呢？无论你多大年纪，任何时候你都可能呼吸一次，然后就再也没有第二次机会。这种情况时有发生——婴儿、青少年、中年人——不仅仅是老年人。一次呼吸，他们就消失了。没有人知道自己的生命何时终结。事情并非如此。

So why not be bold enough to regularly reflect on how you would live that last week? If you were to ask this question of people who are truly awakened, they wouldn’t have any problem answering you. Not a thing would change inside of them. Not a thought would cross their minds. If death were to come in an hour, if death were to come in a week, or if death were to come in a year, they would live exactly the same way as they’re living now. There is not a single thing they carry inside of their hearts that they would rather be doing. In other words, they are living their lives fully and are not making compromises or playing games with themselves.

所以，为什么不大胆地定期反思一下，如果生命走到尽头，你会如何度过最后一周呢？如果你问那些真正觉醒的人这个问题，他们会毫不犹豫地回答。他们的内心不会有任何改变，也不会有任何念头闪过他们的脑海。无论死亡是在一个小时后到来，还是一个星期后到来，亦或是一年后到来，他们都会像现在这样生活。他们心中没有任何想要做的事情。换句话说，他们活得充实而有意义，不会妥协，也不会与自己玩弄感情。

You have to be willing to look at what it would be like if death was staring you in the face. Then you have to come to peace within yourself so that it doesn’t make any difference whether it is or not. There is a story of a great yogi who said that every moment of his life he felt as though a sword were suspended above his head by a spiderweb. He lived his life with the awareness that he was that close to death. You are that close to death. Every time you get in the car, every time you walk across the street, and every time you eat something, it could be the last thing you do. Do you realize that what you’re doing at any moment is something that someone was doing when they died? “He died eating dinner… He died in a car accident, two miles from his home… She died in a plane wreck on a trip to New York… He went to bed and never woke up…” At some point, this is how it happened to somebody. No matter what you’re doing, you can be sure somebody died that way.

你必须愿意去想象死亡近在眼前会是什么样子。然后，你必须内心平静，这样无论死亡是否真的存在，你都不会在意。有个伟大的瑜伽士说过，他感觉自己生命中的每一刻都像一把剑悬在头顶，被蛛网笼罩。他时刻意识到自己离死亡如此之近。你也离死亡如此之近。你每次坐进车里，每次过马路，每次吃东西，都可能是你做的最后一件事。你是否意识到，你此刻正在做的事情，正是别人临终前正在做的事情？“他吃晚饭时去世了……他死于车祸，离家只有两英里……她在去纽约的旅途中死于空难……他上床睡觉后就再也没有醒来……”在某个时刻，总会有人以这种方式死去。无论你在做什么，你都可以肯定，有人曾经以同样的方式死去。

You must not be afraid to discuss death. Don’t get uptight about it. Instead, let this knowledge help you to live every moment of your life fully, because every moment matters. That’s what happens when somebody knows they only have a week left. You can be certain that they would tell you that the most important week they ever had was that last week. Everything is a million times more meaningful in that final week. What if you were to live every week that way?

你不必害怕谈论死亡。不要为此感到紧张不安。相反，让这种认知帮助你充实地度过生命中的每一刻，因为每一刻都至关重要。当一个人知道自己只剩一周的生命时，就会发生这样的事。你可以肯定，他们会告诉你，生命中最重要的一周就是最后一周。在那最后一周里，一切都变得意义非凡。如果你能这样度过每一周，又会怎样呢？

At this point you should ask yourself why you aren’t living that way. You are going to die. You know that. You just don’t know when. Every single thing will be taken from you. You will leave behind your possessions, your loved ones, and all your hopes and dreams for this life. You’ll be taken right out of where you are. You’ll no longer be able to fill the roles you were so busy playing. Death changes everything in a flash. That’s the reality of the situation. If all these things can be changed in an instant, then maybe they aren’t so real after all. Maybe you’d better check out who you are. Maybe you should look deeper.

此时此刻，你应该问问自己，为什么你没有那样生活。你会死，你知道的，只是不知道何时会死。一切都会被夺走，你会留下你的财产、你的爱人，以及你对今生的所有希望和梦想。你会被带离你现在所处的地方，再也无法扮演你曾经扮演过的角色。死亡瞬间改变一切，这就是现实。如果所有这一切都能在瞬间改变，那么或许它们并非那么真实。或许你应该好好审视一下自己，或许你应该更深入地思考。

The beauty of embracing deep truths is that you don’t have to change your life; you just change how you live your life. It’s not what you’re doing; it’s how much of you is doing it. Let’s take a very simple example. You’ve walked outside thousands of times, but how many times have you really appreciated it? Imagine a person in a hospital bed who has just been told they’ve got a week to live. They look up at the doctor and say, “Can I walk outside? Can I look at the sky just one more time?” If it were raining outside, they would want to feel the rain just once more. For them, that would be the most precious thing. But you don’t want to feel the rain. You run and cover up.

领悟深刻真理的美妙之处在于，你无需改变你的人生，只需改变你生活的方式。重要的不是你做了什么，而是你投入了多少精力。举个简单的例子。你可能已经出门走了成千上万次，但你真正欣赏过多少次呢？想象一下，一个躺在病床上的人，被告知只剩一周的生命。他抬头看着医生，问道：“我可以出去走走吗？我可以再看看天空吗？”如果外面正在下雨，他会想要再感受一次雨水。对他来说，那将是无比珍贵的。但你却不想感受雨水。你会跑开，躲起来。

What is it that won’t let us live our lives? What is inside of us that is so afraid that it keeps us from just enjoying life? This part of us is so busy trying to make sure the next thing goes right that we can’t just be here now and live life. All the while, death is watching our footsteps. Don’t you want to live before death comes? You’re probably not going to get a warning. Very few people are told when they’re going to die. Almost everybody just takes a breath and doesn’t know they didn’t take another.

究竟是什么阻碍了我们好好生活？我们内心深处究竟是什么恐惧让我们无法享受人生？我们内心的这部分总是忙于确保接下来的事情一切顺利，以至于我们无法活在当下，好好生活。与此同时，死神正悄然注视着我们。难道你不想在死神降临之前好好活过吗？你或许不会收到任何预兆。很少有人会被告知自己何时会死。几乎每个人都只是呼吸了一口气，然后就再也没有呼吸过。

So start using every day to let go of that scared part of you that won’t let you live life fully. Since you know you’re going to die, be willing to say what needs to be said and do what needs to be done. Be willing to be fully present without being afraid of what will happen in the next moment. That’s how people live when they face death. You get to do that too, because you are facing death every moment.

所以，从现在开始，利用每一天来放下你内心那个让你无法尽情享受生活的恐惧。既然你知道自己终将一死，那就勇敢地说出该说的话，做该做的事。勇敢地活在当下，不再畏惧下一刻会发生什么。这就是人们面对死亡时的生活。你也可以这样做，因为你每时每刻都在与死亡抗争。

Learn to live as though you are facing death at all times, and you’ll become bolder and more open. If you live life fully, you won’t have any last wishes. You will have lived them every moment. Only then will you have fully experienced life and released the part of you that is afraid of living. There is no reason to be afraid of life. And the fear will fade once you understand that the only thing there is to get from life is the growth that comes from experiencing it. Life itself is your career, and your interaction with life is your most meaningful relationship. Everything else you’re doing is just focusing on a tiny subset of life in the attempt to give life some meaning. What actually gives life meaning is the willingness to live it. It isn’t any particular event; it’s the willingness to experience life’s events.

学会时刻以面对死亡的心态去生活，你会变得更加勇敢、更加开放。如果你活得淋漓尽致，就不会有任何临终遗愿。因为你的每一刻都已活过。只有这样，你才能真正体验人生，放下心中对生活的恐惧。没有理由害怕生活。一旦你明白，人生唯一值得拥有的，就是体验人生带来的成长，恐惧就会消散。生活本身就是你的事业，你与生活的互动就是你最有意义的关系。你所做的其他一切，都只是试图赋予生活某种意义，而关注生活的一小部分。真正赋予生活意义的，是体验生活的意愿。它并非指某个特定的事件，而是指体验人生百态的意愿。

What if you knew that the next person you’d see would be the last person you would ever see? You’d be right there soaking it in, experiencing it. It wouldn’t matter what they were saying; you’d just enjoy hearing the words because it would be the last conversation you’d ever have. What if you brought that kind of awareness to every conversation? That’s what happens when you’re told that death is around the corner: you change, life doesn’t change. The true seeker commits to live like that every moment and lets nothing stop them. Why should anything stop you? You’re just going to die anyway.

如果你知道接下来要见的人将是你此生见到的最后一个人，你会作何感想？你会全身心地投入其中，感受着这一切。他们说了什么并不重要；你只是享受聆听每一个字，因为这将是你们的最后一次对话。如果你将这种觉知带入每一次对话，又会怎样呢？这就是当你被告知死亡近在咫尺时会发生的事：你会改变，但生命本身不会改变。真正的求道者会承诺每时每刻都如此生活，不让任何事阻挡他们。又有什么能阻挡你呢？反正你终将一死。

If you challenge yourself to live as though it were your last week, your mind may come up with all kinds of suppressed desires. It may start talking about all the things that you’ve always wanted to do, and you may think you had better go do them. You will soon see that’s not the answer. You have to understand that it is your attempt to get special experiences from life that makes you miss the actual experience of life. Life is not something you get; it’s something you experience. Life exists with or without you. It has been going on for billions of years. You simply get the honor of seeing a tiny slice of it. If you’re busy trying to get something, you will miss the slice you’re actually experiencing. Every one of life’s experiences is different, and every experience is worth having. Life is not something to waste. It’s truly precious. That’s why death is such a great teacher. It is death that makes life precious. Look how precious life becomes when you imagine you only have a week left to live. How precious would life be if there was no such thing as death? You’d waste every second of it because you’d figure you’d always have it. It is scarcity that makes things precious. It is scarcity that makes a simple rock become a rare gem.

如果你挑战自己，像对待生命中的最后一周那样生活，你的脑海中可能会涌现出各种被压抑的渴望。你可能会想起所有你一直想做的事情，然后觉得最好赶紧去做。但你很快就会发现，这并非解决之道。你必须明白，正是你试图从生活中获取特殊体验的努力，才让你错过了生命本身的体验。生命不是你索取的东西，而是你体验的东西。生命存在，无论你是否存在。它已经持续了数十亿年。你只是有幸目睹了它短暂的一瞬。如果你忙于索取什么，你就会错过你正在体验的那一小片。生命中的每一次体验都独一无二，每一次体验都值得拥有。生命不应被浪费。它无比珍贵。这就是为什么死亡是一位伟大的导师。正是死亡让生命变得珍贵。想想看，当你想象自己只剩下一周的生命时，生命变得多么珍贵。如果没有死亡，生命又该是多么珍贵呢？你会浪费每一秒，因为你觉得你永远都会拥有它。正是稀缺性才使事物珍贵。正是稀缺性使一块普通的石头变成稀世珍宝。

So death actually gives meaning to life. Death is your friend. Death is your liberator. For God’s sake, do not be afraid of death. Try to learn what it’s saying to you. The highest way to learn is to take each moment of your life and realize that what matters is to live it fully. If you live each moment completely, you will have a fuller life and you will not have to fear death.

所以，死亡实际上赋予生命意义。死亡是你的朋友，死亡是你的解脱者。看在上帝的份上，不要害怕死亡。试着去理解它在对你诉说什么。学习死亡的最佳途径就是珍惜生命中的每一刻，并意识到真正重要的是活得充实。如果你能全然地活在当下，你的人生将会更加圆满，你也就无需惧怕死亡。

You fear death because you crave life. You fear death because you think there’s something to get that you haven’t experienced yet. Many people feel that death will take something away from them. The wise person realizes that death is constantly giving them something. Death is giving meaning to your life. You’re the one who throws your life away; you waste every second of it. You get in your car, drive from here to there, and you don’t see anything. You’re not even there. You’re busy thinking about what you’re going to do next. You’re a month ahead of yourself, or even a year. You’re not living life; you’re living mind. So it is you who throws your life away, not death. Death actually helps you get your life back by making you pay attention to the moment. It makes you say, “My God, I’m going to lose this. I’m going to lose my children. This could be the last time I’ll see them. From now on I’m going to pay more attention to them, and to my spouse, and to all my friends and loved ones. I want to get so much more out of life!”

你惧怕死亡，是因为你渴望生命。你惧怕死亡，是因为你觉得还有你尚未体验过的美好事物等待你去发现。许多人觉得死亡会夺走他们生命中的某些东西。智者明白，死亡其实一直在给予他们一些东西。死亡赋予你的生命意义。是你自己挥霍了生命；你浪费了每一秒。你开车从这里到那里，却什么也看不到。你甚至都不在现场。你忙着思考下一步该做什么。你总是想着一个月，甚至一年之后的事情。你没有真正地生活，你只是在头脑中活着。所以，挥霍生命的是你，而不是死亡。死亡实际上帮助你重获新生，因为它让你专注于当下。它让你不禁感叹：“我的天哪，我要失去这一切了。我要失去我的孩子们了。这可能是我最后一次见到他们了。从今以后，我要更加关注他们，关注我的配偶，关注我所有的朋友和爱人。我想好好珍惜生命！”

If you are living every experience fully, then death doesn’t take anything from you. There’s nothing to take because you’re already fulfilled. That’s why the wise being is always ready to die. It doesn’t make any difference when death comes because their experience is already whole and complete. Suppose you loved music more than anything else. You always wanted to hear your favorite classical composition played by your favorite orchestra. That was the dream of your life. Finally, it happens. You’re there and you’re actually hearing it. It completely fills you. The very first notes lift you to where you needed to go. This shows you that it only takes a moment to become absorbed in a transcendental peace. You really don’t need more time before death; what you need is more depth of experience during the time you’re given.

如果你全然投入地体验每一种经历，那么死亡就无法从你身上夺走任何东西。因为你已经圆满，所以没有什么可以被夺走。这就是为什么智者总是做好了死亡的准备。死亡何时到来对他们来说无关紧要，因为他们的人生体验已经完整圆满。假设你热爱音乐胜过一切。你一直渴望聆听你最爱的古典乐曲由你最爱的乐团演奏。那是你毕生的梦想。最终，梦想成真。你身临其境，亲耳聆听。音乐彻底充盈了你的身心。第一个音符便将你带到了你渴望抵达的境界。这告诉你，只需片刻，你便能沉浸于超然的宁静之中。你真正需要的并非更多的时间，而是在有限的生命中体验更深刻的人生。

That’s the way to live each moment of your life. You let it fill you completely. You let it touch you to the depths of your being. There is no moment that can’t do that. Even if something terrible happens, view it as just another experience of life. Death has made you a great promise in which you can find deep peace. The promise is that all things are temporal; they are all just passing through time and space. If you have patience, this too will pass.

这就是活在当下、感受生命每一刻的方式。让它完全充满你的身心，触及你灵魂深处。没有哪个时刻不能做到这一点。即使遭遇可怕的事情，也要把它看作是人生中的又一次经历。死亡给了你一个美好的承诺，让你在其中找到深深的平静。这个承诺就是：万物皆是暂时的，它们都只是在时间和空间中流逝。如果你有耐心，这一切也终将过去。

The wise realize that in the end, life belongs to death. Death is the one who comes in his own time to take life from you. Death is the landlord and you’re just the tenant. People say things like, “He’s living on borrowed time,” or, “He got a new lease on life.” From whom did he borrow the time? From death, of course. Death is the one who comes to claim his property because it has always belonged to him. You should have a healthy relationship with death, and it should not be one of fear. Feel grateful to death for giving you another day, another experience, and for creating the scarcity that makes life so precious. If you do this, your life will no longer be yours to waste; it will be yours to appreciate.

智者明白，最终，生命属于死亡。死亡会在适当的时候前来，带走你的生命。死亡是房东，而你只是租客。人们常说，“他是在借时间苟活”，或者“他获得了新生”。他从谁那里借来的时间呢？当然是从死亡那里。死亡前来收回它的财产，因为生命一直属于它。你应该与死亡保持一种健康的关系，而不是恐惧。要感谢死亡，感谢它赐予你新的一天，新的体验，感谢它创造了生命的稀缺性，使生命如此珍贵。如果你这样做，你的生命将不再是任你挥霍的，而是值得你珍惜的。

Death is an ultimate reality of life. The yogis and saints fully embrace death. St. Paul said, “Oh death, where is thy sting? Oh grave, where is thy victory?” (1 Cor. 15:55). Great beings don’t mind speaking of death. Yogis have traditionally gone into graveyards and burning ghats to meditate. They sit there to remind themselves of the frailty of the body and the inevitability of death. Buddhists are taught to contemplate the temporal nature of things. It is all temporal, and death says this to you.

死亡是生命的终极现实。瑜伽士和圣人坦然接受死亡。圣保罗说：“死啊，你的毒钩在哪里？阴间啊，你的胜利在哪里？”（哥林多前书 15:55）。伟大的生命并不避讳谈论死亡。瑜伽士历来会前往墓地和火葬场冥想。他们静坐于此，是为了提醒自己肉体的脆弱和死亡的必然性。佛教徒被教导要思考万物的短暂性。一切都是暂时的，而死亡正是在告诉你这一点。

So, instead of getting lost in the normal mental chatter, why not contemplate the temporal nature of life? Why not think about something meaningful? Don’t be afraid of death. Let it free you. Let it encourage you to experience life fully. But remember, it’s not your life. You should be experiencing the life that’s happening to you, not the one you wish was happening. Don’t waste a moment of life trying to make other things happen; appreciate the moments you are given. Don’t you understand that every minute you’re a step closer to death? This is how to live your life. You live it as though you were on the verge of death, because you are.

所以，与其沉溺于日常的思绪纷扰，何不思考生命的短暂本质？何不思考一些有意义的事情？不要惧怕死亡。让它解放你。让它激励你充分体验生命。但记住，这不是你的人生。你应该体验正在发生的生命，而不是你希望发生的生命。不要浪费生命中的每一刻去试图让其他事情发生；珍惜你所拥有的每一刻。难道你不明白，你离死亡更近一步吗？这才是生活的真谛。你要像濒临死亡边缘那样去生活，因为你的确如此。
