18
18
the secret of the middle way
中道的秘密

No discussion of living life as a spiritual path is complete without addressing one of the deepest of all spiritual teachings, the Tao te Ching . It discusses that which is very difficult to discuss, that which Lao-tzu called “the Tao” (pronounced: dow). Literally translated, this means “the Way.” The Tao is so subtle that one can only talk around its edges, but never actually touch it. In that treatise, the very basis for the principles of all of life is laid down. It is a treatise on the balance of the yin and the yang, the feminine and the masculine, the dark and the light. You could easily read the Tao te Ching and never understand a single word, or you could read it and tears could pour from your eyes with every word you read. The question is, do you bring to it the knowledge, the understanding, and the basis for comprehending what it is attempting to express?

任何关于如何将生活视为灵性道路的讨论，都离不开《道德经》——这部最深奥的灵性教义之一。它探讨的是难以言喻的事物，老子称之为“道”（发音：dow）。字面翻译过来就是“道路”。道如此精妙，我们只能在其边缘徘徊，却永远无法真正触及。这部著作奠定了所有生命原则的基础。它论述了阴阳、阴柔、光明与黑暗的平衡。你可以读《道德经》却一个字也看不懂，也可以读得酣畅淋漓，泪流满面。关键在于，你是否具备理解它所要表达的真谛所需的知识、理解力和基础？

Unfortunately, spiritual teachings often mask the essence of truth with mystical words. But this balance, this Tao, is actually very simple. Those who have truly learned the secrets of life recognize these truths without having read anything. If you want to understand the Tao, you must take it very slowly and keep it very simple. Otherwise, you may miss it, though it is right in front of you.

可惜的是，许多灵性教义常常用晦涩难懂的言辞掩盖真理的本质。但这种平衡，这种道，其实非常简单。真正领悟人生真谛的人，无需阅读任何书籍就能领悟这些真理。如果你想理解道，就必须循序渐进，保持简单。否则，即使它就在眼前，你也可能错过。

It is best to approach the Tao through some very simple, almost rhetorical questions. For example, is it good for a person to eat sometimes? Yes, obviously it is. Is it good for a person to eat all the time? No, of course not. Somewhere in between, you passed over the Tao. Is it good to fast periodically? Yes. Is it good to never eat? No. The pendulum can swing all the way from gorging yourself to death, to starving yourself to death. Those are the two extremes of the pendulum: the yin and the yang, expansion and contraction, nondoing and doing. Everything has two extremes. Everything has gradations of this pendulum swing. If you go to the extremes, you cannot survive. That’s how extreme the extremes are. For example, do you like hot weather? How about 6,000°F? You’d be instantly vaporized. Do you like cold weather? How about absolute zero? The molecules of your body would never move again.

最好通过一些非常简单、近乎反问的问题来接近道。例如，人偶尔吃东西好吗？当然好。人一直吃东西好吗？当然不好。介于两者之间的某个阶段，你就错过了道。定期禁食好吗？好。完全不吃东西好吗？不好。钟摆可以从暴饮暴食到饿死，一直摆到饿死。这就是钟摆的两个极端：阴与阳，扩张与收缩，无为与有为。万物皆有两极，万物皆有钟摆摆动的程度。如果你走向极端，你将无法生存。极端就是如此极端。例如，你喜欢炎热的天气吗？那6000华氏度呢？你会瞬间汽化。你喜欢寒冷的天气吗？那绝对零度呢？你身体的分子将永远无法再运动。

Let’s use an example that is a little less extreme. Do you like being close to another person? How about being so close that you’re never apart? You eat every meal together, you go everywhere together, and you do everything together. When you talk on the phone, you always use a speakerphone so that both of you can partake in every conversation. You want to be so close that you’re the same person. How long do you think that could last?

我们举个稍微温和一点的例子。你喜欢和另一个人亲近吗？如果亲近到形影不离呢？你们一起吃饭，一起去任何地方，一起做任何事。打电话时，你们总是用免提，这样你们都能参与到每一次对话中。你们想要亲近到融为一体。你觉得这种状态能持续多久？

That’s one extreme in human relationships. The other extreme is that you want your own space. You do your own thing. You’re independent. You like being separate so that you always have something to share with each other when you’re together. How independent are you? Well, you travel separately, you eat separately, and you live in separate houses. At what point are you so separate that no one can figure out if you’re having a relationship? You haven’t seen each other for years! Both of these extremes will end up the same. Too close, too far away—in either case, you won’t be talking to each other before long. Everything has its extremes, its yin and its yang.

这是人际关系中的一个极端。另一个极端是，你想要自己的空间。你做自己的事。你很独立。你喜欢保持距离，这样你们在一起的时候总有东西可以分享。你有多独立？嗯，你们各自旅行，各自吃饭，住在不同的房子里。你们要到什么程度才会如此疏远，以至于没人能看出你们是否在谈恋爱？你们可能已经好几年没见面了！这两个极端最终都会殊途同归。太近或太远——无论哪种情况，你们很快就会不再说话。万事万物都有其极端，有阴有阳。

Now let’s get a little subtler. The 6,000-degree temperature doesn’t sound so good, and absolute zero doesn’t sound so interesting either. Neither does starving to death, nor eating until you’re sick. But that part about being so close to somebody that you’re always together may sound pretty nice. You may at least like to give it a shot. If so, it’s because your pendulum has been swung in the opposite direction for too long. You’ve had too much time alone—too many dinners alone, too many movies alone, and too much traveling alone. In other words, your pendulum has swung off-center.

现在我们来谈谈更微妙的方面。6000度的高温听起来不太好，绝对零度也没什么吸引力。饿死或者吃到撑死也一样。但是，和某人形影不离，永远在一起，这听起来可能很不错。你或许至少想尝试一下。如果是这样，那是因为你的生活节奏已经完全颠倒太久了。你独处的时间太长了——太多次独自用餐，太多次独自看电影，太多次独自旅行。换句话说，你的生活节奏已经偏离了中心。

From science we know that if you pull a pendulum thirty degrees to the right, it will swing back until it’s thirty degrees to the left. You don’t need Lao-tzu to tell you this. All the laws are the same—inner laws and outer laws. The same principles drive everything in this world. If you pull a pendulum out one way, it will swing back just that far the other way. If you’ve been starving for days, and somebody puts food in front of you, you won’t be polite while you’re eating. You will shove the food into your mouth like an animal. The degree to which you will act like an animal is the exact degree to which you were starved enough to bring up your animal instincts.

科学告诉我们，如果你把钟摆向右拉30度，它会摆回到向左30度的位置。这无需老子赘述。所有规律都是一样的——内在规律和外在规律。同样的原则驱动着世间万物。如果你把钟摆向一个方向拉，它会摆回到相反的方向。如果你饿了好几天，有人把食物放在你面前，你不会有礼貌地吃。你会像动物一样狼吞虎咽。你像动物一样的程度，恰恰是你饥饿到激发出动物本能的程度。

So where is the Tao? The Tao is in the middle. It’s the place where there is no energy pushing in either direction. The pendulum has been permitted to come to balance concerning food, relationships, sex, money, doing, not-doing, and everything else. Everything has its yin and yang. The Way is the place in which these forces balance quietly. And indeed, unless you go out of the Way, they will tend to stay in peaceful harmony. If you want to understand the Tao, you must take a closer look at what lies between the two extremes. This is because neither extreme can last. How long can a pendulum stay at one of its outermost positions? It can only remain there for a moment. How long can a pendulum stay at rest? It can remain there forever because there are no forces moving it out of balance. That is the Tao. It is the center. But that does not mean that it stays static and fixed. We’re about to see that it’s much more dynamic than that.

那么，道在哪里呢？道在中心。它是能量不偏向任何方向的地方。在饮食、人际关系、性、金钱、作为、不作为以及其他一切事物上，钟摆都已达到平衡。万物皆有阴阳。道，正是这些力量静静平衡之处。的确，除非你偏离道，否则它们将保持和谐的和平状态。如果你想理解道，就必须仔细观察介于两个极端之间的状态。这是因为任何一个极端都无法持久。钟摆在其最外侧的位置能停留多久？它只能停留片刻。钟摆静止多久？它可以永远保持静止，因为没有任何力量使其失去平衡。这就是道。它是中心。但这并不意味着它是静止不变的。我们即将看到，它远比这更加动态。

First you have to realize that since everything has its yin and yang, everything has its own balance point. It is the harmony of all these balance points, woven together, that forms the Tao. This overall balance maintains its equilibrium as it moves through time and space. Its power is phenomenal. If you want to imagine the power of the Tao, examine how much energy is wasted swinging sideways. Suppose you want to go from point A to point B, but instead of walking there directly, you move from side to side like a sine wave. That would take a long time, and you would waste a lot of energy. In other words, it’s not efficient to oscillate around the path. To be efficient, you must center all of your energies on the path. If you do this, the energies that used to be wasted swinging sideways will get pulled into the center. This concentration of energies is used to accomplish the given task much more efficiently. This is the power of the Tao. When you stop swinging between the opposites you’ll find that you have far more energy than you ever imagined. That which takes somebody else hours will take you minutes. That which wears out other people will draw very little of your energy. That’s the difference between struggling with the opposites versus staying centered in order to get something done.

首先，你必须明白，万物皆有阴阳，万物皆有其平衡点。正是这些平衡点相互交织，和谐共存，构成了道。这种整体平衡使其在时空中保持稳定，其力量无比强大。若要想象道的力量，不妨想想左右摇摆会浪费多少能量。假设你想从A点到B点，但你不是直接走过去，而是像正弦波一样左右摇摆。这样会耗费大量时间，浪费大量能量。换句话说，在路径上摇摆不定效率低下。要想高效，你必须将所有能量集中于路径之上。如此一来，原本浪费在左右摇摆上的能量就会被吸引到中心。这种能量的集中能让你更高效地完成既定任务。这就是道的力量。当你不再在对立面之间摇摆不定时，你会发现自己拥有远超想象的精力。别人需要花费数小时才能完成的事情，你只需几分钟就能搞定。别人精疲力竭的事情，对你来说却几乎不费吹灰之力。这就是在对立面之间挣扎与保持专注完成任务之间的区别。

This principle holds true in every aspect of life. If you are in balance, you eat when it is time to eat, in a way that maintains the health of your body. To do otherwise is to waste energy dealing with the effects of eating too little, eating too much, or eating the wrong foods. It is much more efficient to deal with the body in a balanced manner than to be burdened with the effects of the extremes.

这条原则适用于生活的方方面面。保持平衡的生活方式，意味着在合适的时间进食，并以有益于身体健康的方式进食。反之，则会浪费能量来应对进食过少、过多或食物不当带来的种种后果。与其承受极端饮食带来的种种困扰，不如以平衡的方式对待身体，这样效率更高。

Basically, you waste tremendous energy at the extremes. The more extreme it is, the more it becomes a full-time project. For example, the relationship in which you insist upon being together all the time would be a full-time job. The only way you could have another job is if you both did the same work at the same desk. At the other extreme, if you had no relationship and you were lonely and depressed all the time, you couldn’t accomplish much. So again, it takes all your energy to do the extremes. The inefficiency of your actions is determined by how many degrees off-center you are. You will be that much less able to use your energy for living life because you are using it to adjust for the pendulum swings. Extremes are good teachers. When you examine the extremes, it’s easy to see the effects of imbalanced behavior patterns.

基本上，走极端会浪费你大量的精力。越是极端，就越像是在做一份全职工作。例如，如果你坚持要时刻待在一起，那么这段关系就相当于一份全职工作。你唯一能找到另一份工作的方式，就是你们俩在同一张桌子旁做同样的工作。而另一种极端情况是，如果你没有伴侣，总是感到孤独和沮丧，你也几乎一事无成。所以，走极端会消耗你所有的精力。你行为的低效程度取决于你偏离中心的程度。你把精力都用在了调整这种摇摆不定的状态上，因此你用于享受生活的能力就会大大降低。极端情况是很好的老师。当你审视这些极端情况时，很容易就能看出失衡的行为模式所带来的后果。

Let’s take the example of a chain-smoker. He always has a cigarette in his mouth, and he’s constantly lighting up another. A meaningful percentage of his life is involved in smoking. He’s buying cigarettes, lighting cigarettes, and smoking cigarettes. He’s also very busy trying to find places where he’s allowed to smoke. And since he doesn’t like having to go outside to light up, he’s joining the committees in favor of allowing smoking in public places. Notice how much of his energy is going into smoking. Now imagine that he decides to quit—not a single cigarette anymore. If a year later you ask him what he did last year, he will tell you that he quit smoking. That was his life for the past year. First he tried the chewing gum, but that didn’t really help. Then he tried the patch. When that didn’t work, he moved on to hypnotherapy. Because the pendulum was so far to one extreme with his smoking, it had to swing to the opposite extreme in order for him to stop smoking. Both extremes were a tremendous waste of time, energy, and effort that could have gone into more productive aspects of his life.

我们以一个老烟民为例。他嘴里总是叼着烟，不停地点烟。他生活中相当一部分时间都花在了吸烟上。他买烟、点烟、抽烟。他还忙着寻找可以吸烟的地方。由于他不喜欢出门点烟，所以他加入了支持在公共场所吸烟的委员会。注意他把多少精力都花在了吸烟上。现在想象一下，他决定戒烟——一根烟都不抽了。如果一年后你问他去年做了什么，他会告诉你他戒烟了。这就是他过去一年的生活。他先是尝试了尼古丁口香糖，但没什么效果。然后他又试了尼古丁贴片。贴片也不管用，他转而尝试了催眠疗法。因为他吸烟成瘾，所以必须彻底戒烟才能成功。这两种极端做法都极大地浪费了他本可以投入到更有成效的生活中的时间、精力和努力。

When you spend your energy trying to maintain the extremes, nothing goes forward. You get stuck in a rut. The more extreme you are, the less forward movement there is. You carve a groove and you get stuck in it. Then there’s no energy moving you in the Tao; it’s all being spent serving the extremes.

当你把精力耗费在维持极端立场上时，一切都无法前进。你会陷入停滞不前的状态。你越是走极端，前进的动力就越少。你刻意雕琢出一条固定的模式，然后深陷其中无法自拔。这样一来，你便失去了在道中前行的能量；所有的能量都消耗在了追求极端立场上。

The Way is in the middle because that’s the place where the energies are balanced. But how do you stop the pendulum from swinging to the outer edges? Amazingly enough, you do this by leaving it alone. It won’t keep swinging to the extremes unless you feed the extremes with energy. Just let the extremes go. Don’t participate in them, and the pendulum will naturally come toward the center. As it comes to the center, you will get filled with energy. This is because all the energy that had been wasted is now available to you.

道在中间，因为那里是能量平衡之处。但如何才能阻止钟摆摆动到两端呢？神奇的是，你只需顺其自然。除非你给两端注入能量，否则它不会一直摆动到极端。只需让极端消散，不要参与其中，钟摆自然会回到中心。当它回到中心时，你会充满能量。这是因为所有之前被浪费的能量现在都可供你使用。

If you choose to center and not participate in the extremes, you will come to know the Tao. You don’t grab it; you don’t even touch it. It’s just what the energy does when it’s not being used to swing toward the extremes. It finds its own way to the center of each event that takes place in life and remains quietly in the middle. The Tao is hollow, empty. Like the eye of a hurricane, its power is its emptiness. All things swirl around it, but it is unmoved. The swirl of life draws its energy from the center and the center draws its energy from the swirl of life. All these laws are the same—in weather, in nature, and in every aspect of your life.

如果你选择回归中庸，不走向极端，你就会认识道。你无需攫取它，甚至无需触碰它。当能量不被用于奔向极端时，它便会自然而然地找到自身运行的路径，抵达生命中每件事的中心，并静静地停留于此。道是空灵的，如同飓风的风眼，它的力量源于它的空性。万物围绕它旋转，而它却纹丝不动。生命的旋转从中心汲取能量，而中心也从生命的旋转中汲取能量。所有这些规律都是一样的——在天气中，在自然界中，在你生活的方方面面。

As you center by not participating in the swings, the energies will naturally find their balance. You will become much clearer because so much energy is flowing up in you. The experience of being present in each moment will become your natural state. You won’t be fixated on certain things or caught up in thoughts about the opposites. As you get clearer, life’s events will actually seem to unfold in slow motion. Once this happens, events will no longer seem confusing or overwhelming, no matter what they are.

当你不再受情绪波动的影响，而是专注于当下，能量自然会找到平衡。你会变得更加清醒，因为大量的能量在你体内向上流动。活在当下将成为你的自然状态。你不会再执着于某些事物，也不会再被对立的想法所困扰。随着你变得更加清醒，生活中的种种事件仿佛会慢下来。一旦达到这种状态，无论发生什么，你都不会再感到困惑或不知所措。

This is quite different from how most people live. If they’re driving a car and somebody cuts them off, they get upset for the next hour, or maybe for the rest of the day. For the being who is in the Tao, events take place and last just as long as they are taking place. That’s it. If you’re driving and somebody cuts you off, you feel your energy start to pull off-center. You actually feel it in your heart. As you let go, it comes back to center. You don’t follow the extremes, so your energy comes back to the current moment. When the next event happens, you’re there. You’re always there, and that makes you much more capable than the person who is reacting to past imbalances. Almost everyone has a point at which they get out of balance. Once gone, who’s minding the store? Who takes care of the energies that unfold while you’re not there? Remember, whoever remains present with fixity of purpose comes out on top in the end.

这与大多数人的生活方式截然不同。如果他们开车时被人别车，他们会在接下来的一个小时甚至一整天里为此感到沮丧。但对于遵循道的人来说，事情的发生和持续就如同它们正在发生一样，仅此而已。如果你开车时被人别车，你会感觉到自己的能量开始偏离中心。你甚至能从内心深处感受到这种变化。当你放下执念时，能量就会回归中心。你不会走向极端，所以你的能量会回到当下。当下一个事件发生时，你依然在那里。你始终在那里，这使你比那些对过去的失衡做出反应的人更有能力。几乎每个人都有失去平衡的时刻。一旦失去平衡，谁来守护？谁来照看在你不在时发生的能量变化？记住，最终，那些始终保持专注、目标明确的人才能获得成功。

When you move in the Tao, you are always present. Life becomes absolutely simple. In the Tao, it’s easy to see what’s happening in life—it’s unfolding right in front of you. But if you have all kinds of reactions going on inside because you’re involved in the extremes, life seems confusing. That’s because you’re confused, not because life’s confusing.

当你顺应道时，你便始终活在当下。生活变得无比简单。在道中，你很容易看清生活中发生的一切——它就在你眼前徐徐展开。但如果你因为陷入极端而内心充满各种反应，生活就会显得混乱。那是因为你感到困惑，而不是生活本身令人困惑。

When you stop being confused, everything becomes simple. If you have no preference, if the only thing you want is to remain centered, then life unfolds while you simply feel for the center. There is an invisible thread that passes through everything. All things move quietly through that center balance. That is the Tao. It is really there. It is there in your relationships, in your diet, and in your business activities. It is there in everything. It is the eye of the storm. It is completely at peace.

当你不再困惑，一切都变得简单。如果你没有偏好，如果你唯一想要的只是保持内心的平静，那么生活便会在你感受中心的过程中自然展开。有一条无形的线贯穿万物。万物都静静地围绕着这个中心平衡运转。这就是道。它真实存在。它存在于你的人际关系中，存在于你的饮食中，存在于你的事业活动中。它存在于一切事物之中。它是风暴的中心。它完全平静。

To give you an idea of what it feels like to be in that center, let’s use the example of sailing. We’ll begin by going sailing when there’s no wind. That’s one extreme, and we’re not going anywhere. Now let’s go sailing when there’s tremendous wind but there’s no sail. That is the opposite extreme and, again, we’re not going anywhere. Sailing is such a good example because there are many forces interacting together. There’s the wind, the sail, the rudder, and the tension of the ropes on the sail. There is a tremendous interplay of forces. What happens if the wind is blowing and you hold the sail too loosely? It doesn’t work. What if you hold it too tightly? You tip over. To sail properly you must hold it just right. But where is just right? It is in the center point of tautness of the sail against the force of the wind—not too much, and not too little. It’s what we call the “sweet spot.” Imagine that feeling when the wind hits the sail just right, and you’re holding the ropes just right. You take off with a perfect feeling of balance. Then the wind shifts and you adjust to it. You, the wind, the sail, and the water are one. All the forces are in harmony. Should one force shift, the others shift at the same instant. This is what it means to move in the Way.

为了让你们体会一下处于这种平衡状态的感觉，我们以帆船为例。首先，我们假设在无风的情况下航行。这是一种极端情况，我们寸步难行。现在，我们假设在狂风呼啸但没有帆的情况下航行。这是另一种极端情况，同样，我们寸步难行。帆船是一个很好的例子，因为它涉及多种力的相互作用。有风、帆、舵，还有帆绳的张力。各种力之间存在着巨大的相互作用。如果风很大，而你把帆拉得太松会怎样？船就开不动了。如果拉得太紧呢？船就会翻。要想航行得当，你必须把帆拉得恰到好处。那么，哪里才是恰到好处呢？它位于帆与风力之间张力的平衡点——既不能太紧，也不能太松。这就是我们所说的“最佳点”。想象一下，当风恰到好处地吹拂着帆，你握住绳索的姿势也恰到好处时，那种感觉。你带着完美的平衡感扬帆起航。然后风向改变，你也随之调整。你、风、帆和水融为一体。所有力量和谐共存。如果其中一种力量发生变化，其他力量也会立即随之改变。这就是顺应天道的真谛。

In the Tao of sailing, the balance point is not static; it’s a dynamic equilibrium. You move from balance point to balance point, from center to center. You can’t have any concepts or preferences; you have to let the forces move you. In the Way, nothing is personal. You are merely an instrument in the hands of the forces, participating in the harmony of balance. You must reach the point where your whole interest lies in the balance and not in any personal preference for how things should be. It’s that way with all of life. The more you can work with the balance, the more you can just sail through life. Effortless action is what happens when you come into the Tao. Life happens, you’re there, but you don’t make it happen. There is no burden; there is no stress. The forces take care of themselves as you sit in the center. That is the Tao. It’s the most beautiful place in all of life. You can’t touch it, but you can be at one with it.

在航海之道中，平衡点并非静止不变，而是一种动态平衡。你从一个平衡点移动到另一个平衡点，从一个中心移动到另一个中心。你不能有任何概念或偏好；你必须顺应自然之力。在道中，一切皆非个人。你只是自然之力手中的工具，参与到平衡的和谐之中。你必须达到这样的境界：你所有的注意力都集中在平衡本身，而不是任何个人对事物应有状态的偏好上。人生亦是如此。你越能驾驭平衡，就越能轻松驾驭人生。当你进入道中，便能体验到毫不费力的行动。生活自然发生，你身处其中，但你无需掌控它。没有负担，没有压力。当你安坐于中心时，自然之力会自行运转。这就是道。它是生命中最美好的境界。你无法触及它，但你可以与之合一。

Eventually you will see that in the way of the Tao you’re not going to wake up, see what to do, and then go do it. In the Tao, you are blind, and you have to learn how to be blind. You can never see where the Tao is going; you can only be there with it. A blind person walks down a city street with the use of a cane. Let’s give that cane a name: it’s the seeker of the extremes, it’s the feeler of the edges, it’s the toucher of the yin and the yang. People who walk with the use of that cane often tap from side to side. They’re not trying to find where they should walk; they’re trying to find where they shouldn’t walk. They’re finding the extremes. If you cannot see your way, all you can do is feel for the edges. But if you feel the edges, and don’t go there, you will stay in the Way. That’s how you live in the Tao.

最终你会明白，在道的道路上，你不会醒来后立刻明白该做什么，然后就去做。在道中，你是盲人的，你必须学会如何盲目。你永远无法预知道的走向；你只能与它同在。一个盲人拄着拐杖走在城市的街道上。我们不妨给这根拐杖起个名字：它是探寻极致的，是感知边缘的，是触及阴阳的。拄着拐杖的人常常左右摇晃。他们不是在寻找应该走的地方，而是在寻找不应该走的地方。他们在寻找极致。如果你看不见前路，你所能做的就是感知边缘。但如果你感知到边缘，却不去触碰，你就能留在道中。这就是你如何在道中生活。

All the great teachings reveal the way of the center, the way of balance. Constantly look to see if that’s where you are living or if you are lost in the extremes. The extremes create their opposites; the wise avoid them. Find the balance in the center and you will live in harmony.

所有伟大的教义都揭示了居中之道，平衡之道。要时刻审视自己是否身处其中，还是迷失于极端之中。极端会带来其对立面；智者避而远之。在居中寻得平衡，你便能和谐生活。

19
19
the loving eyes of god
上帝慈爱的目光

How can anyone really know anything about God? We have so many teachings, so many concepts, and so many views about God. But they’ve all been touched by people. In the end, it’s amazing how much our ideas about God conform to the different cultures from which they come.

谁又能真正了解上帝呢？关于上帝，我们有如此多的教义、概念和观点。但它们都受到了人的影响。最终，我们关于上帝的观念与它们所源自的不同文化竟如此契合，这真是令人惊叹。

Fortunately, deep within us, there is a direct connection to the Divine. There is a part of our being that is beyond the personal self. You can consciously choose to identify with that part, rather than with the psyche or the body. When you do this, a natural transformation begins to take place within you. Over time, as you observe this transformation, you will see what it’s like to be coming toward God. You actually begin to know what it feels like to be moving in the direction of Spirit. The changes you see within you are reflective of the force you’re approaching. Just as rain makes you wet and fire makes you warm, so you can know the nature of God by looking into the mirror of your transformed self. This is not a philosophy; it is a direct experience.

幸运的是，在我们内心深处，与神性有着直接的连接。我们存在着超越个人自我的部分。你可以有意识地选择认同这部分，而不是认同你的心理或肉体。当你这样做时，一种自然的转变便会在你体内开始发生。随着时间的推移，当你观察这种转变时，你就会体会到接近神是什么感觉。你开始真正地了解朝着灵性方向前进的感受。你内在的变化反映了你正在接近的力量。正如雨水使你湿润，火焰使你温暖，你也可以通过审视你转变后的自我来了解神的本质。这并非一种哲学理论，而是一种直接的体验。

Spiritual growth can be experienced just like anything else. You may have experienced a time in your life when you felt a lot of negativity, anger, and resentment. You know how that feels, and you know how you feel toward others when you’re feeling that way. You know how your heart feels, and you know what your thoughts and actions are like. You know that space. It’s not a philosophy; it’s a direct experience.

灵性成长和其他任何事物一样，都是可以体验到的。你或许经历过一段充满负面情绪、愤怒和怨恨的时期。你明白那种感觉，也知道在这种情绪下你会如何看待他人。你知道自己内心的感受，也知道自己的想法和行为。你了解那种状态。它不是一种哲学理论，而是一种直接的体验。

If you grow past that part of you, over time you will actually drift away from the feelings of tension and anxiety. The entire cloud of lower vibrations will appear further and further away from where you sit inside. The cloud may still be there, but if you don’t identify with it or hold onto it, it can no longer hold onto you. As you release the lower vibrations, you naturally stop thinking they’re you or that there’s anything you have to do about them. As you let go of them, your Spirit drifts upward.

如果你能超越自身那一部分，随着时间的推移，你自然会逐渐远离紧张和焦虑的感觉。低频能量的阴霾会越来越远，远离你内心深处。阴霾或许依然存在，但如果你不再认同它，不再执着于它，它就无法再束缚你。当你释放低频能量时，你自然而然地不再认为它们代表你，也不再觉得你需要对它们做些什么。当你放下它们，你的灵魂便会向上提升。

How do you know your Spirit drifts upward? You know the same way you know that you’re breathing, the same way you know that your heart beats, and the same way you know that you have thoughts. You’re in there and you directly experience it.

你如何知道你的灵魂在上升？你知道的方式，就像你知道自己在呼吸，知道自己的心跳，知道自己有思想一样。你身处其中，直接体验着这一切。

What does it mean to drift upward? It’s an experience of being drawn further back inside yourself. You’re no longer held down to your earthly self, so you begin to feel more spaciousness inside. You feel that there’s more of a distance between you and the thoughts and emotions inside of you. You drift back, and then in and up.

向上漂移意味着什么？它是一种被拉向内心深处的体验。你不再受制于尘世的自我，因此开始感到内心更加开阔。你感到自己与内心的思想和情绪之间有了更大的距离。你向后漂移，然后向内向上漂移。

How does it feel when you drift up? You don’t feel as much anger, fear, or self-consciousness. You don’t feel resentment toward people. You don’t close or get tight as often. Things still happen that you don’t want to happen, but they don’t seem to touch you as much. They can’t reach back to where you are because you’ve drifted behind the part of you that reacts to things. These are actual experiences, not merely something you were told about. It’s just what naturally happens when you let go of the lower vibrations of your being. You drift in and up to the deeper vibrations.

当你提升意识状态时，感觉如何？你不再感到那么多的愤怒、恐惧或自我意识。你不再对人心生怨恨。你不再那么频繁地封闭自己或变得紧张。你仍然会遇到不想发生的事情，但它们似乎不再那么触动你。它们无法再影响到你，因为你已经超越了你内心那个对事物做出反应的部分。这些都是真实的体验，并非只是别人告诉你的。当你放下自身较低的振动频率时，这一切自然而然就会发生。你会提升到更深层次的振动频率。

Where are you going? Even if you have no basis for understanding what is happening to you, you are still having the undeniable experience of going somewhere. What you begin to feel is that you’re going into your spiritual being. As you associate less with the physical and psychological parts of your being, you begin to identify more with the flow of pure energy.

你要去哪里？即使你无法理解自己正在经历什么，你仍然会真切地感受到自己正在前往某个地方。你会开始感觉到，你正在进入你的精神世界。随着你与自身生理和心理层面的联系减少，你会开始更多地与纯粹能量的流动产生共鸣。

What does it feel like to identify more with Spirit than with form? You used to walk around feeling anxiety and tension; now you walk around feeling love. You just feel love for no reason. Your backdrop is love. Your backdrop is openness, beauty, and appreciation. You don’t have to make yourself feel that way; that is how Spirit feels. If you were asked how the body normally feels, you might say that it’s generally uncomfortable about one thing or another. How about the psyche? If you were being totally honest, you’d probably say that it’s generally full of complaints and fears. Well, how does Spirit normally feel? The truth is, it always feels good. It always feels high. It always feels open and light.

与灵性而非形体认同更多是怎样的感受？你过去常常感到焦虑和紧张；现在你感到充满爱。你无需任何理由就能感受到爱。你的背景是爱。你的背景是开放、美好和感恩。你无需刻意让自己有这种感觉；这就是灵性本身的感觉。如果有人问你身体通常感觉如何，你可能会说它总是因为这样那样的事情而感到不舒服。那么心灵呢？如果你完全诚实，你可能会说它通常充满了抱怨和恐惧。那么，灵性通常感觉如何呢？事实上，它总是感觉良好。它总是感觉振奋。它总是感觉开放而轻松。

Because of this, you naturally begin to center more and more on the spiritual part of your being. You do this not by reaching for Spirit, but by letting go of the rest. There really is no other way. The personal self cannot touch Spirit; you must release the personal self. As you release it, you drift back. As you go further back, you get higher. You get higher in vibration and higher in the amount of love and lightness that you feel. You just begin to soar. This happens in an ever-increasing, continuous progression.

正因如此，你自然而然地会越来越关注你存在的灵性层面。你并非通过追求灵性来实现这一点，而是通过放下其他一切。别无他法。个人的自我无法触及灵性；你必须放下个人的自我。当你放下它时，你便会回归本源。随着你回归得越来越远，你的境界也会越来越高。你的振动频率会越来越高，你感受到的爱与轻盈也会越来越强烈。你开始翱翔。这是一个不断增强、持续推进的过程。

As you let go and willingly release the physical, emotional, and mental aspects of your being, Spirit becomes your state. You don’t claim to understand what is happening to you; you just know that as you go further and further back, it gets more and more beautiful. You naturally begin to experience the vibrations that were described by the great saints and sages of different traditions. You realize that you, too, can have deep spiritual experiences and be “…in the Spirit on the Lord’s Day” (Rev. 1:10).

当你放下并心甘情愿地释放你存在的物质、情感和精神层面时，灵性便成为你的状态。你无需声称理解发生在你身上的一切；你只需知道，当你不断深入回溯时，一切便愈加美好。你自然而然地开始体验到不同传统中伟大圣贤所描述的那些振动。你意识到，你也能拥有深刻的灵性体验，也能“在主日被圣灵充满”（启示录 1:10）。

But ultimately, how do you really know anything about God? How can you ever know about what is beyond you? You know because those who have gone beyond have come back and said that the Spirit you’re experiencing is the doorway to God. When they let go of the lower aspects of their being, they experienced just what you’re experiencing. They felt tremendous love, Spirit, and light waking up inside of them. They felt that nothing could come in through their senses that was higher than what was already going on inside. They drifted further and further back and got higher and higher. Then one day, all of a sudden, they weren’t there. There was no sense of “I” anymore. There was no sense of a separateness experiencing the love and light. There was only the ultimate expansiveness of their sense of Self merging into the love and light, like a single drop of water merging into the ocean.

但归根结底，你究竟如何才能真正了解上帝？你又如何才能了解超越自身之外的事物？你知道，因为那些超越自我的人已经回归，并告诉你，你所体验到的灵性正是通往上帝的门户。当他们放下自身低级的层面时，他们体验到了你正在体验的一切。他们感受到巨大的爱、灵性和光芒在他们体内觉醒。他们感到，没有任何事物能够通过他们的感官进入，超越他们内在已有的体验。他们不断回归本源，不断提升境界。然后有一天，突然之间，他们不再存在。“我”的概念消失了。体验爱与光时，不再有任何分离感。只有他们自我意识的终极扩展，与爱与光融为一体，如同水滴融入大海。

When the drop of consciousness that knows itself as an individual drifts back far enough, it becomes like the drop that falls into the ocean. The Atman (Soul) falls into the Paramatman (Supreme Soul). The individual consciousness falls into the Universal Oneness. And that’s it.

当那滴觉知自身为个体的意识漂流到足够远的地方，它就如同落入大海的水滴。阿特曼（灵魂）落入帕拉玛特曼（至高灵魂）。个体意识落入宇宙一体。仅此而已。

When that happens, people say interesting things like, “I and my Father are one” (John 10:30) and “…the words that I speak unto you I speak not of myself: but the Father that dwelleth in me, he doeth the works” (John 14:10).

当这种情况发生时，人们会说一些有趣的话，比如“我与父原为一”（约翰福音 10:30）和“……我对你们所说的话，不是凭着自己说的；乃是住在我里面的父作他自己的事”（约翰福音 14:10）。

They all spoke like that. They said they had merged and that there was no differentiation within the Universal Oneness of God. The drop of consciousness, which is individual Spirit, is like a ray of light emanating from the sun. The individual ray is really no different from the sun. When consciousness stops identifying itself as the ray, it comes to know itself as the sun. Beings have merged into that state.

他们都那样说话。他们说他们已经融合，在宇宙一体的上帝之中，不存在任何区别。意识的碎片，也就是个体的灵性，就像太阳发出的一道光束。这道光束实际上与太阳并无二致。当意识不再将自身视为光束时，它便开始认识到自身就是太阳。众生都已融入到那种状态之中。

In the mystical Gospel of John, Christ says, “That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us … I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one…” (John 17:21-23). So it was taught in the Hindu Vedas; so it was taught in the Jewish Kabbalah; so it was written by the great Sufi mystic poets; and so it was taught in all the great religious traditions of all time. Such a state exists; one can merge into the Universal Absolute. One can merge into God.

在神秘的约翰福音中，基督说：“使他们都合而为一。正如你父在我里面，我在你里面，使他们也在我们里面……我在他们里面，你在我里面，使他们完完全全地合而为一……”（约翰福音 17:21-23）。印度教吠陀经如此教导；犹太教卡巴拉如此教导；伟大的苏菲神秘主义诗人如此书写；历代所有伟大的宗教传统如此教导。这样的境界是存在的；人可以融入宇宙绝对，融入神。

This is how you know something about God. You become one with Him. Ultimately, the only way to know about God is by letting your being merge into The Being, and then seeing what happens to you. This is universal consciousness, and the qualities of the beings who have attained this deep state are similar in every religion.

这就是你了解神的方式。你与祂合而为一。归根结底，了解神的唯一途径就是让你的存在融入祂，然后观察你身上会发生什么。这就是宇宙意识，而达到这种深层境界的生命所具有的特质，在所有宗教中都是相似的。

What happens to one who walks this path toward God? What transformations do they go through along the way? To understand this, imagine what would happen if you started feeling tremendous love for all creatures, for every plant, for every animal, and for all the beauties of nature. Imagine if every child seemed like your own, and every person you saw looked like a beautiful flower, with its own color, its own expression, shape, and sounds. As you went deeper and deeper, you would start noticing a phenomenal thing—you are no longer judging. The process of judging has simply stopped. There is just appreciating and honoring. Where there used to be judging, there is now respecting, loving, and cherishing. To differentiate is to judge. To see, to experience, and to honor is to participate in life instead of standing back and judging it.

走上这条通往神的道路，会发生什么？他们会经历怎样的转变？为了理解这一点，不妨想象一下，如果你开始对所有生灵、每株植物、每只动物，以及大自然的一切美好都怀有无比的爱，那会是怎样一番景象？想象一下，如果每个孩子都像你的孩子一样，你看到的每个人都像一朵美丽的花，拥有各自的颜色、表情、形状和声音。随着你不断深入体验，你会开始注意到一件奇妙的事情——你不再评判。评判的过程已经停止了。取而代之的是欣赏和尊重。曾经的评判，如今已被尊重、爱和珍惜所取代。区分即是评判。而观察、体验和尊重，才是真正地参与生命，而不是袖手旁观、妄加评判。

When you walk through a beautiful botanical garden, you feel open and light. You feel love. You see beauty. You don’t judge the shape and placement of every leaf. The leaves are of all sizes and shapes and they face every-which-way. That’s what makes them beautiful. What if you felt that way about people? What if they didn’t all have to dress the same, believe the same, or behave the same? What if they were like the flowers, and however they happened to be seemed beautiful to you?

漫步在美丽的植物园中，你会感到轻松自在，心生爱意，目睹万物之美。你不会去评判每一片叶子的形状和位置。叶子大小各异，形状千姿百态，朝向也各不相同。正是这些特质造就了它们的美。如果你对人也有同样的感觉呢？如果他们不必穿着同样的衣服，拥有同样的信仰，或者举止同样？如果他们像花朵一样，无论他们以何种面貌示人，你都会觉得他们很美，那又会怎样呢？

If that happened, you’d get a glimpse of God. That’s the best way to know God. Watch what happens to you as you get closer to Him. It’s really the only way you can know anything about God. If you try to read about God in a book, you’ll find five other books that say the opposite. Better yet, you’ll find five interpretations of the same book. Somebody writes something and somebody else gets a Ph.D. proving it wrong. If you move your search for God down to the mental level, somebody will dispute it. It’s all part of the mind game.

如果那样的话，你就能瞥见上帝。那是认识上帝的最佳途径。观察一下当你靠近祂时，你的身体会发生什么变化。这才是你真正了解上帝的唯一途径。如果你试图从一本书中了解上帝，你会发现还有五本书的说法与此相反。更甚者，你会发现同一本书有五种不同的解读。有人写了一些东西，然后另一个人拿到博士学位，证明它是错的。如果你把对上帝的探寻降低到理性的层面，总会有人反驳你。这一切都是思维游戏的一部分。

You can’t know God that way. It must come from actual experience. That’s what happens to you when you meditate. That’s what happens when you let go of your lower self. You drift into Spirit, and as you drift into Spirit, these transformations take place within you. All you have to do is notice them, and you will start to notice the tendency toward the qualities of the Divine. The further back you go, the more you will see these natural qualities unfolding inside of you. Each step along the way, you get a clearer glimpse of what it must be like to sit in that Divine State.

你无法通过这种方式认识神。它必须来自实际体验。当你冥想时，就会发生这样的体验。当你放下低级自我时，就会发生这样的体验。你会融入灵性，随着你融入灵性，这些转变会在你内在发生。你只需觉察它们，就会开始注意到你身上逐渐显现的神性特质。你越是追溯过往，就越能看到这些自然的神性在你内在展开。每一步，你都会更清晰地领悟到，安住于神圣状态究竟是怎样的体验。

There are those who know of the existence of the Divine Force. They’ve had enough direct inner experience to know that Divine Consciousness is a reality. They have seen glimpses of a force that is omniscient, omnipresent, and omnipotent; a force that is aware of all things at all times, equally. It is universally conscious.

有些人知道神圣力量的存在。他们拥有足够的直接内在体验，足以确信神圣意识的真实存在。他们曾瞥见一种全知、全在、全能的力量；一种在任何时间、任何地点都平等地感知万物的力量。它具有普世意识。

What does creation look like from that Divine State? What have they seen, those who have gone beyond and looked through the eyes of God? They see that there is no judging. Judging faded away long ago. There’s just more beauty to see. Such a being feels, “Now I can see all the flowers at once. Now I can experience what each of my children and all of my diversity is doing. Now I can feel more love, more compassion, more understanding, and more admiration for all the different expressions and actions of my creation.” That is what it looks like to a saint. And a true saint dwells with God.

从神圣的境界来看，造物是怎样的？那些超越尘世、透过神眼所见的人，他们看到了什么？他们看到，那里没有评判。评判早已消逝。那里只有更多值得欣赏的美。这样的人会想：“现在我可以同时看到所有的花朵。现在我可以体验到我的每一个孩子，以及我所有的多样性都在做什么。现在我可以感受到更多的爱、更多的怜悯、更多的理解，以及对我的造物所有不同表达和行为的更多赞赏。”这就是圣人眼中的造物。而真正的圣人与神同在。

What if it is really true that God is not judging? What if God is loving? We all know that true love doesn’t judge. Love sees nothing but beauty in its beloved. There is no impurity. There is no possibility of impurity. No matter what it beholds, it’s all beautiful. That is how true love sees. That is what it looks like through the eyes of love. So if God is love, what must it look like through those eyes—the eyes that are filled with infinite love and unconditional compassion?

如果上帝真的不评判呢？如果上帝充满爱呢？我们都知道，真爱不评判。爱在所爱之人眼中只有美好。没有瑕疵，也不存在瑕疵的可能性。无论它看到什么，都是美好的。这就是真爱的视角。这就是透过爱的眼睛所看到的。那么，如果上帝就是爱，透过那双充满无限爱和无条件慈悲的眼睛，祂又会是什么样子呢？

If you’ve ever really loved anybody, then you know what true love means. It means that you love them more than you love yourself. If you truly love someone, your love sees past their humanness. It embraces their whole being, including past wrongs and current shortcomings. It is like the unconditional love of a mother. A mother devotes every moment of her life to a child who is physically or mentally challenged. She thinks the child is beautiful. She doesn’t focus on the shortcomings; in fact, she doesn’t even see them as shortcomings.

如果你曾经真正爱过一个人，你就会明白真爱的含义。真爱意味着你爱他胜过爱自己。如果你真心爱一个人，你的爱会超越他的人性，包容他的全部，包括他过去的过错和现在的不足。这就像母亲无条件的爱。一位母亲会将生命中的每一刻都奉献给身患残疾或智力障碍的孩子。在她眼中，孩子是美丽的。她不会关注孩子的缺点；事实上，她根本不认为那是缺点。

What if that is how God looks upon His creation? Then you’ve lost out if you’ve been told otherwise. Instead of being encouraged to feel completely protected, loved, honored, and respected by the Divine Force, you’ve been taught that you’re being judged. Because you’ve been taught that, you feel guilt and fear. But guilt and fear do not open your connection to the Divine; they only serve to close your heart. The reality is that God’s way is love, and you can see this for yourself. If, for even one moment, you can look at someone with the eyes of true love, you’ll know those eyes are not yours. Your eyes could never look with that amount of love. Your eyes could never be that unconditional. Your eyes could never, even in a million years, see only beauty and total perfection in your beloved. Those are the eyes of God looking down through you.

如果上帝就是这样看待祂的创造物呢？如果你一直被灌输相反的观念，那么你就错过了很多。你本应感受到神圣力量的完全保护、爱护、尊崇和尊重，却被教导说你正受到审判。正因为如此，你才会感到内疚和恐惧。但内疚和恐惧并不能打开你与神圣的连接；它们只会让你的心扉紧闭。事实上，上帝的道路是爱，你可以亲眼见证这一点。哪怕只有一瞬间，如果你能用真爱的目光注视一个人，你就会明白那双眼睛并非你的。你的眼睛永远无法拥有如此深沉的爱。你的眼睛永远无法如此无条件。即使过了一百万年，你的眼睛也永远无法在你爱的人身上看到纯粹的美丽和完美。那是上帝透过你的双眼注视着你。

When the hand of God reaches out to give through you, there’s nothing you wouldn’t give. You would give your last breath and never even think about it. It wouldn’t even cross your mind to hold back. You would give anything and everything for your beloved. When you feel love this deeply, you feel that it is coming from something greater than you. It is transcendental love. It is divine, unconditional, selfless love. The masters spoke of that love. The ones who went beyond said it’s the state you attain when you drift into Spirit. That is how Spirit looks upon its creation. That is what you should be taught. No matter what you do, and no matter what you’ve done, you will always be loved by Him.

当上帝之手通过你伸出援手时，你会毫无保留地付出一切。你会献出最后一口气，甚至毫不犹豫。你不会有任何保留的念头。你会为挚爱之人付出一切。当你如此深切地感受到爱时，你会觉得它来自超越自身的存在。那是超越一切的爱。那是神圣的、无条件的、无私的爱。大师们曾谈论过这种爱。那些超越尘世的人说，那是你融入灵性时所达到的境界。灵性就是这样看待它的造物的。这才是你应该学习的。无论你做了什么，无论你曾经做过什么，你都将永远被祂所爱。

When Christ told the story of the prodigal son to his disciples, he spoke of one son who had gone away and squandered all his wealth. Yet when he came home for help, his father treated him better than the son who had stayed home and worked. Christ explained that this was because one son had always been home, but the prodigal son had been lost, and the father had missed him. There was no judging—only loving (Luke 15:11-32).

基督给门徒讲浪子回头的故事时，提到一个儿子离家出走，挥霍了所有的财富。然而，当他回家寻求帮助时，父亲却比对待那个留在家里工作的儿子更善待他。基督解释说，这是因为一个儿子一直待在家里，而浪子迷失了方向，父亲一直思念着他。父亲没有论断，只有爱（路加福音 15:11-32）。

Christ also said, “He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone…” (John 8:7). What did he teach? What did he say? How did he look upon this world? He taught completely selfless, compassionate love. He hung on the cross next to thieves and robbers, and when a thief asked to be remembered, Christ said that he would share that day in heaven with him (Luke 23:39-43). What were his first words upon the cross? “Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do” (Luke 23:34). That is the love of a mother. That’s how a mother talks about her child. The level of love and compassion is so deep that the child can do no wrong. If a mother can attain to selfless love, then what about God, the creator of love?

基督也说过：“你们中间谁是没有罪的，谁就可以先拿石头打她……”（约翰福音 8:7）。他教导了什么？他说了什么？他如何看待这个世界？他教导的是完全无私、充满怜悯的爱。他与盗贼和强盗一同被钉在十字架上，当一个盗贼请求基督记念他时，基督说他会与他一同在天堂里度过那一天（路加福音 23:39-43）。他在十字架上说的第一句话是什么？“父啊，赦免他们，因为他们不知道自己所做的是什么”（路加福音 23:34）。这就是母爱。这就是母亲谈论自己孩子的方式。这份爱和怜悯如此深沉，以至于孩子做什么都是对的。如果一位母亲都能达到无私的爱，那么创造爱的上帝又该如何呢？

Do you want to know how God looks upon this world? Do you want to know how He feels about different kinds of people? Then look at the sun. Does the sun shine more brightly on a saint than on anyone else? Is the air more available to the saint? Does the rain fall on one neighbor’s trees more than another’s?

你想知道上帝如何看待这个世界吗？你想知道祂对不同类型的人有何感受吗？那就看看太阳吧。阳光照耀在圣徒身上是否比照耀在其他人身上更明亮？空气是否更容易被圣徒呼吸？雨水是否更多地落在某个邻居的树上？

You can turn your eyes from the sun’s light and live in darkness for a hundred years. If you then turn them toward the light, the light is still there. It is there for you just the same as for the person who has enjoyed its brilliance for a hundred years. All of nature is like this. The fruit on the tree willingly gives itself to everyone. Do any of the forces of nature differentiate? Does anything in God’s creation, other than the human mind, actually pass judgment? Nature just gives and gives to whoever will receive. Should you choose not to receive, it doesn’t punish you. You punish yourself because you choose not to receive. If you say to the light, “I will not look at you. I’m going to live in darkness,” the light just keeps shining. If you say to God, “I don’t believe in you and want nothing to do with you,” creation continues to sustain you.

你可以把目光从阳光下移开，在黑暗中生活一百年。如果你之后把目光转向光明，光明依然在那里。它对你来说，和对那个享受了它光辉一百年的人一样。整个自然界都是如此。树上的果实乐意赐予每一个人。自然界的力量会区别对待吗？除了人类的思维之外，上帝的创造物中还有什么会真正进行评判呢？自然只是不断地给予，给予那些愿意接受的人。如果你选择不接受，它不会惩罚你。惩罚你的是你，因为你选择了不接受。如果你对光明说：“我不看你，我要生活在黑暗中”，光明依然会照耀。如果你对上帝说：“我不信你，我不想和你有任何瓜葛”，造物依然会继续供养你。

Your relationship with God is the same as your relationship with the sun. If you hid from the sun for years and then chose to come out of your darkness, the sun would still be shining as if you had never left. You don’t need to apologize. You just pick your head up and look at the sun. It’s the same way when you decide to turn toward God—you just do it. If, instead, you allow guilt and shame to interfere, that’s just your ego blocking the Divine Force. You can’t offend the Divine One; its very nature is light, love, compassion, protection, and giving. You can’t make it stop loving you. It’s just like the sun. You can’t make the sun stop shining on you; you can only choose not to look at it. The moment you look, you’ll see it’s there.

你与神的关系就像你与太阳的关系。如果你多年来一直躲避阳光，后来选择走出黑暗，太阳依然会照耀大地，仿佛你从未离开过。你无需道歉，只需抬起头，仰望太阳。当你决定转向神时，也是如此——只需去做。相反，如果你让内疚和羞耻感干扰你，那只是你的自我阻碍了神圣的力量。你无法冒犯神；祂的本质就是光明、爱、慈悲、保护和给予。你无法让祂停止爱你。这就像太阳一样。你无法让太阳停止照耀你；你只能选择不去看它。当你再次去看它时，你会发现它就在那里。

As you drift back into Spirit, you will see that those are the eyes that look out upon this world. That is the heart that shines down upon everything and everyone. Through those eyes, the most wretched of creatures looks beautiful. That’s the part that no one understands. People say that God cries when He looks at this earth. The saint sees that God goes into ecstasy when He looks upon this earth, under all conditions, and at all times. Ecstasy is the only thing God knows. God’s nature is eternal, conscious bliss. No matter what you’ve done, you’re not going to be the one thing that ruins it.

当你回归灵性，你便会明白，那双眼睛俯瞰着这个世界。那颗心照耀着万物，照耀着每一个人。透过那双眼睛，最卑微的生灵也显得美丽动人。这是无人能理解的部分。人们说，上帝看着这世间会哭泣。圣人却明白，上帝在任何境况、任何时刻，看着这世间，都会进入极乐之境。极乐是上帝唯一知晓的。上帝的本质是永恒的、觉知的极乐。无论你做过什么，你都不会是破坏这一切的罪魁祸首。

The beauty is that you can experience this ecstasy. And when you begin to feel this joy, that’s when you’ll know God’s nature. Then nobody will upset or disappoint you. Nothing will create a problem. It will all appear as part of the beautiful dance of creation unfolding before you. Your natural state will get higher and higher. You’ll feel love instead of shame. Instead of being unwilling to lift your eyes to the Divine because of what you’ve said or done, you’ll see the Divine as a place of unconditional refuge.

美妙之处在于，你可以体验到这种狂喜。当你开始感受到这种喜悦时，你就会认识神的本质。那时，没有人会令你心烦或失望。没有什么会制造问题。一切都会成为在你面前展开的美妙造物之舞的一部分。你的自然状态会越来越高。你会感受到爱，而不是羞愧。你不再会因为自己的言行而不敢仰望神，而是会将神视为无条件的庇护所。

Contemplate this, and let go of the idea of a judgmental God. You have a loving God. In truth, you have love itself for a God. And love cannot do other than love. Your God is in ecstasy and there’s nothing you can do about it. And if God is in ecstasy, I wonder what He sees when He looks at you?

仔细想想，放下你对上帝会评判的执念。你拥有的是一位慈爱的上帝。事实上，你拥有的就是对上帝的爱本身。而爱除了爱之外，别无他能。你的上帝沉浸在极乐之中，你对此无能为力。既然上帝如此沉浸在极乐之中，我很好奇，当祂注视着你时，祂看到了什么？

About the Author

作者简介

Michael A. Singer is author of the highly successful The Untethered Soul , which has also been published in Turkey, Brazil (in Portuguese), Switzerland (in German), Spain, Japan, China, the Netherlands, Denmark, Finland, Poland, and Italy. Singer received a master’s degree in economics from the University of Florida in 1971. During his doctoral work, he had a deep inner awakening and went into seclusion to focus on yoga and meditation. In 1975, he founded Temple of the Universe, a now long-established yoga and meditation center where people of any religion or set of beliefs can come together to experience inner peace. Through the years, Singer has made major contributions in the areas of business, the arts, education, healthcare, and environmental protection. He previously authored two books on the integration of Eastern and Western philosophy: The Search for Truth and Three Essays on Universal Law: Karma, Will and Love . Visit www.untetheredsoul.com for more information.

迈克尔·A·辛格是畅销书《不羁的灵魂》（The Untethered Soul）的作者，该书已被翻译成土耳其语、巴西语（葡萄牙语）、德语（瑞士）、西班牙语、日本语、中国语、荷兰语、丹麦语、芬兰语、波兰语和意大利语出版。辛格于1971年获得佛罗里达大学经济学硕士学位。攻读博士学位期间，他经历了一次深刻的内在觉醒，并隐居起来专注于瑜伽和冥想。1975年，他创立了宇宙圣殿（Temple of the Universe），如今已成为一个历史悠久的瑜伽和冥想中心，任何宗教信仰的人们都可以在这里相聚，体验内心的平静。多年来，辛格在商业、艺术、教育、医疗保健和环境保护等领域做出了重大贡献。他此前还著有两本关于东西方哲学融合的书籍：《寻求真理》（The Search for Truth）和《论宇宙法则的三篇论文：业力、意志和爱》（Three Essays on Universal Law: Karma, Will and Love）。访问www.untetheredsoul.com了解更多信息。

About the Institute of Noetic Sciences (IONS)

关于诺埃提克科学研究所（IONS）

Noetic Books is an imprint of the Institute of Noetic Sciences, which was founded in 1973 by Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell. IONS is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit research, education, and membership organization whose mission is advancing the science of consciousness and human experience to serve individual and collective transformation. “Noetic” comes from the Greek word nous , which means “intuitive mind” or “inner knowing.” Noetic sciences further the explorations of conventional science through rigorous inquiry into those aspects of reality—such as mind, consciousness, and spirit—that include but go beyond physical phenomena. Our primary program areas include integral health and healing, extended human capacities, and emerging worldviews. The specific work of the institute includes the following:

Noetic Books是Noetic Sciences研究所的出版品牌。该研究所由阿波罗14号宇航员埃德加·米切尔于1973年创立。IONS是一家501(c)(3)非营利性研究、教育和会员组织，其使命是推进意识和人类体验科学的发展，以服务于个人和集体的转变。“Noetic”一词源于希腊语“nous”，意为“直觉思维”或“内在认知”。Noetic科学通过对现实的各个方面（例如心灵、意识和精神）进行严谨的探究，进一步拓展了传统科学的探索，这些方面不仅包含物理现象，更超越了物理现象本身。我们的主要项目领域包括整体健康与疗愈、拓展人类潜能以及新兴世界观。研究所的具体工作包括：

  • Sponsorship of and participation in research
    赞助和参与研究
  • Publication of the quarterly magazine Shift: At the Frontiers of Consciousness
    出版季刊《转变：意识的前沿》
  • The monthly membership program, Shift in Action, and its associated website, www.shiftinaction.com
    每月会员计划“Shift in Action”及其相关网站www.shiftinaction.com
  • Presentation and cosponsorship of regional and international workshops and conferences
    举办和联合主办区域性和国际性研讨会和会议
  • The hosting of residential seminars and workshops at its on-campus retreat facility, located on 200 acres forty-five minutes north of San Francisco
    该机构在其位于旧金山以北 45 分钟车程、占地 200 英亩的校园静修设施内举办住宿研讨会和工作坊。
  • The support of a global volunteer network of community groups
    得到全球社区团体志愿者网络的支持
